movies.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
movies.cast: Keir Dullea, Gary Lockwood, William Sylvester, and Douglas Rain
movies.description: William Friedkin’s visually stunning film follows small-time crook Roy Scheider from Brooklyn to the sweltering South American jungles, where he lands a job hauling nitroglycerine with hard-luck losers Bruno Cremer and Francisco Rabal. Rather than simply remake Henri-Georges Clouzot’s famed WAGES OF FEAR, Friedkin re-imagined the story as a bleak, cosmic vision of man vs. nature, climaxing in the mind-bending image of Scheider and crew literally pushing a loaded truck across a spindly rope bridge.

Written, directed, and produced by Wong Kar-wai, 2046 picks up loose ends from two previous Wong features, Days of Being Wild (1990) and In the Mood for Love (2000), with Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung reprising their respective roles as writer Chow Mo-wan and his lost soulmate, Su Li-zhen. Named for the apartment in which Chow and Su connected, 2046 weaves together four disparate narratives about the romantic affairs Chow pursues while writing science fiction (with beautifully realized scenes pulled from his pulp sci-fi novels), gambling, and trying to move on. “A puzzle, a valentine, a sacred hymn to beauty… and a cynical shrug of the shoulders at the damned impermanence of it all, 2046 is a movie to live in,” Glenn Kenny declared in Premiere .

movies.title: A Litany for Survival: The Life and Work of Audre Lorde
movies.description: This epic portrait of the award-winning Black lesbian poet, mother, teacher, and activist Audre Lorde catalogs an incredibly impactful, revolutionary career. From her childhood roots in Harlem to her battle with breast cancer, the film explores a life, and a body of work, that bridged the Civil Rights movement, the women’s movement, and the struggle for lesbian and gay rights. New restoration premier; Q&A to follow with Ada Gay Griffin, Michelle Parkerson & J.T. Takagi

movies.title: Alphaville
movies.description: A brilliant mashup of dystopian sci-fi, French New Wave, and 1950s American pulp noir. Jean-Luc Godard’s idiosyncratic feature follows hard-boiled private eye Lemmy Caution (Eddie Constantine, who had already played the character for a decade in less avant-garde fare) in his mission to capture or kill Professor von Braun, creator of the fascist computer Alpha 60 that rules the grim city of Alphaville. With the help of Natacha von Braun (Anna Karina), the professor’s computer programmer daughter, Caution rages against the machine with the ineffably human qualities of love and poetry. Hailed for its unique take on pulp fiction and sci-fi, Alphaville won the prestigious Golden Bear at the 1965 Berlin International Film Festival.

It was recorded and filmed in front of an intimate and increasingly rowdy audience at El Coyote in Los Angeles on April 28, 2025, by the band's long-time collaborator John Angus Stewart.
Screens with Amyl and The Sniffers 2025 concert film LIVE AT ALLY PALLY, mixed in 5.1 Dolby surround sound.

movies.title: Best In Show + Every Dog Has His Day: Ilak’S Birthday
movies.description: Best in Show (2000) Dir. Christopher Guest With Jennifer Coolidge, Christopher Guest, John Michael Higgins, Michael Hitchcock, Eugene Levy, Jane Lynch, Michael McKean, Catherine O'Hara, Parker Posey 89min; DCP Excitement, nerves, whining, and panting bubble up in anticipation of the Mayflower Dog Show, as a cast of eccentric dog-owners traverse the nation for the biggest day of the year. From the warbled southern drawl of Christopher Guest as Harlan Pepper to Catherine O’Hara’s unforgettable physical comedy, Parker Posey’s serious-as-a-knife portrayal of a 2000s yuppie, Jennifer Coolidge as a charmingly vapid gold-digger, and the late, great Fred Willard as a dog show judge who seemingly has never crossed paths with a dog, each performance in Best in Show is turned up to 11. Featuring arguably the funniest dog reaction shot in cinema history in its first five minutes, this largely improvised comedy is the kind of film that does not just suggest but demands repeated viewings. Christopher Guest ( Waiting for Guffman , A Mighty Wind ) is at his directorial best, amplified by a who’s who of actors extracting gut-busting performances through off-the-cuff delivery and unimaginable line reads. Preceded by: Every Dog Has His Day: Ilak’s Birthday (1925) With Ilak the Wolf Dog, Rin-Tin-Tin, Peter the Great 2min; Digital Canine actors celebrate Ilak the Wolf Dog’s birthday in this early example of dogs on the silver screen.

movies.title: Born In Flames
movies.description: Set 10 years after a revolution that supposedly transformed the country into a social-democratic utopia, Lizzie Borden’s prescient postpunk provocation features a band of radicals—led by Black, lesbian, and working-class women—who fight back in a world where racism, sexism, and inequality are still the norm. Delivering a mix of TV newscasts, pirate-radio transmissions, and street-protest footage, Born in Flames conveys the incandescent rage of time when it was made, while also uncannily predicting the fragility and fragmentation of progressive movements to come.

movies.title: Butthole Surfers: The Hole Truth and Nothing Butt
movies.description:
A documentary feature about the legendary American punk band Butthole Surfers. The film tells the story of how two accounting students from Trinity College in San Antonio found solidarity in their weirdness, recruited like-minded misfits – queers, weirdos, and nonconformists like naked performance artist/dancer Kathleen Lynch – and embarked on one of the most radical rock journeys of all time. Somehow this band, with a defiantly non-commercial name, ended up as a major influence on acts like Nirvana and even scored a No. 1 hit song.
Beyond the band’s story, the film tells the human story of the people behind the band. It gives an intimate look at lead singer Gibby Haynes, guitar wizard Paul Leary, drummers Teresa Nervosa and King Coffey, and bassist Jeff Pinkus – five American originals with incredible personal stories.

When the system is broken, two men divided by everything agree on one thing: the law has limits. They don’t.

movies.description: This rural murder mystery is one of Italian cult favorite Lucio Fulci's most successfully atmospheric and intense, with more than a few shocks thrown in to goose the audience. When dead kids start popping up around a sleepy and very Catholic Italian village, the police are stymied and the locals think it's a witch (Florinda Bolkan who previously starred in Fulci's LIZARD IN A WOMAN'S SKIN), but a determined newspaperman (the handsome Tomas Milian of many Italian crime and western movies) and the daughter of a wealthy family (Barbara Bouchet). DON'T TORTURE A DUCKLING counterbalances a completely trashy, sometimes sleazy, always tasteless plot with a very artful use of setting to set mood and tone. You will feel the heat. You will not believe the ending!

movies.title: Fallen Leaves + Jean The Matchmaker
movies.description: Fallen Leaves (2023) Dir. Aki Kaurismäki With Alma Pöysti, Jussi Vatanen, Janne Hyytiäinen, Nuppu Koivu 81min; DCP In Finnish with English subtitles Winner of the Jury Prize at Cannes, as well as the Palm Dog’s Grand Jury Prize, the latest from brilliant Finnish filmmaker Aki Kaurismäki showcases his striking blend of crystalline visuals, dark humor, and piercing observation. Fallen Leaves follows two lonely people who meet by chance in the Helsinki night and try to find the first, only, and ultimate love of their lives. Their path towards this honorable goal is clouded by the man’s alcoholism, lost phone numbers, not knowing each other’s names or addresses, and life’s general tendency to place obstacles in the way of those seeking their happiness. This gentle tragicomedy features Kaurismäki’s own dog, making her debut in a small but pivotal (and heart stealing) role. Preceded by: Jean the Matchmaker (1910) Dir. Lawrence Trimble With Florence Turner, Charles Kent, Jean 13min Jean the Vitagraph Dog, America’s first canine screen star, starred in a bevy of early silent films, almost all of them lost aside from Jean the Matchmaker . Shot in 1910 near Portland, Maine, the charming short follows two bashful brothers relying on their charismatic collie companion to win the hearts of the local girls. Jean’s star grew so bright that when she took a break to have a family in 1913, Motion Picture World reported the news: “Jean, the Vitagraph dog, is the happy mother of six little ones. Mother and children all doing nicely, thank you." Jean the Matchmaker provides a rare opportunity to see the dog that paved the way for canine actorsl—and inspired this series.

movies.title: Faust (1926)
movies.description: Mobilizing the full resources of the Ufa Studios, F.W. Murnau (Nosferatu, Sunrise) orchestrated a colossal adaptation of Goethe's FAUST that ranks alongside Fritz Lang's Metropolis as the greatest achievement of the German silent cinema.Gösta Ekman stars as the titular alchemist who, struggling with his faith amidst a devastating plague, is offered the power to cure and the gift of youth...in exchange for his soul. As the diabolical Mephisto, Emil Jannings (The Last Laugh) delivers a performance of operatic scale and intensity, by turns charming, comical, and horrific.This special Kino edition contains the Friedrich Wilhelm Murnau Foundation’s meticulous restoration of the original German version of the film (with unique hand-painted intertitles), as well as a lengthier alternate cut prepared by the Ufa Studios in 1930.

movies.title: GHOST: 2 Big To Rig
movies.description:
Captured live over the course of GHOST’s two sold-out shows in Mexico City last year, 2 BIG TO RIG is the definitive document of the band's unforgettable SKELETOUR WORLD TOUR.
Featuring the only pro-shot footage of Papa V Perpetua and his band of Nameless Ghouls from the phone-free SKELETOUR, 2 BIG TO RIG immerses the audience in the GHOST live ritual, including exclusive behind-the-scenes and backstage access.
2 BIG TO RIG was created to share the SKELETOUR experience with the faithful in the territories where staging the show was not logistically feasible – and is a love letter to all those who have shared the GHOST ritual.
Shot on 16mm film, GHOST has never looked or sounded better, ripping through material from the band's six albums, including 2025’s global #1 Skeletá as well as non-LP favorites including “Mary On A Cross,” “Kiss the Go-Goat,” and “The Future is a Foreign Land.”

Chris Marker With Jean Négroni, Hélène Chatelain, Davos Hanich, Jacques Ledoux 28min; DCP In French with English subtitles The Last Angel of History (1996) Dir. John Akomfrah With George Clinton, Kodwo Eshun, Edward George, Greg Tate, Ishmael Reed 45min; Digital Two short features offer disparate visions of what the future may hold. In Chris Marker’s poetically haunting La Jetée , a stylistically revolutionary 1962 time-travel fable conveyed entirely in stills, a prisoner in post-apocalyptic Paris is sent to the past and future in search of a way to save the world. In The Last Angel of History , a 1996 hybrid documentary by Ghanaian-born British artist and writer John Akomfrah, a time-traipsing “Data Thief” conducts archeological digs in search of links between Black music, Pan-African culture, and future technology, bolstered with commentary from George Clinton, Greg Tate, Octavia E. movies.description:
After a seven-year hiatus following the devastating loss of their beloved bandmate Chester Bennington, Linkin Park's remaining members struggle to find their way forward. Their shared history and enduring friendship, combined with the fresh perspective of two new band members, spark a renewed creative energy that leads them on a transformative journey of artistic reinvention.

Following the band from intimate 2022 studio sessions through their explosive From Zero album release and concert in São Paulo, the film UNSHATTER weaves together rare vault footage, electrifying performances from sold-out shows, and candid interviews with band members and fans – capturing the raw, honest story of what it means to start over.

"Feed me, Seymour! Feed me all night long."
A singing plant. A daring hero. A sweet girl. A demented dentist. And one of the most outrageously fun movies ever made.
Rick Moranis is mild-mannered Seymour Krelborn, a down-on-his-luck employee at a plant shop in skid row who’s in love with Audrey (Ellen Greene), the unlucky-in-love girlfriend of the most sadistic dentist in town. But everything changes when Seymour finds a strange and unusual new plant that will only grow if given a different sort of plant food – people!
As the Audrey II gets bigger and bigger, Seymour finally realizes that he needs to stop it before it can take over the world, but can he destroy the alien plant and get the girl?

movies.description:
An ode to young lovers from that patriarch of elegant quirk, Wes Anderson.
Set on a picturesque New England island in a Kodachrome summer of ’65, MOONRISE KINGDOM tells the story of Suzy and Sam, two troubled 12-year-olds who fall in love, make a secret pact, and run away together into the wilderness. As parents, authorities, and an entire Khaki Scout Troop mobilize to find them, a violent storm is brewing off-shore – and the peaceful island community is turned upside down in every which way.
Starring Anderson troupe regulars Bill Murray and Jason Schwartzman, along with heavy-hitters like Frances McDormand, Bruce Willis, Edward Norton, Tilda Swinton, and Harvey Keitel (plus the always welcome Bob Balaban), MOONRISE KINGDOM is a charm-saturated ‘60s romp awash in Anderson’s unconventional style.

movies.title: Nosferatu (1922)
movies.description: In the town of Wisbourg, estate agent Mr. Knock is pleased to receive a commission from Count Orlok to find a house for him. He dispatches his young assistant, Hutter, to Orlok's castle in the far-off Carpathians. He tells Hutter to get him to buy the vacant house just opposite Hutter's own. Hutter arrives at his destination safely and the Count is all too eager to buy the proposed property, especially after he sees a photo of Hutter's pretty young wife Ellen. Hutter soon realizes the evil he's dealing with and is locked away while Orlock makes his way by ship to Wisbourg. As Orlok travels to Wisbourg, plague descends in his wake and the people of Wisbourg begin to sense the coming of evil. Hutter eventually escapes Orlok's castle, determined to return home as quickly as possible, but exhausted and ill, finds himself in hospital. Hutter nonetheless arrives home the same day as Orlok and the townsfolk begin to panic over the increasing number of deaths.

movies.title: Nostalghia
movies.description: Andrei Tarkovsky explained that in Russian the word nostalghia conveys “the love for your homeland and the melancholy that arises from being far away.” This debilitating form of homesickness is embodied in his film about Russian intellectual Andrei Gorchakov doing research in Italy, who becomes obsessed with the Botticelli-like beauty of his translator Eugenia, as well as with the apocalyptic ramblings of a self-destructive wanderer named Domenico. Written with frequent Michelangelo Antonioni collaborator Tonino Guerra ( L’Avventura ), this mystical and mysterious collision of East and West incorporates an unnamed German Shepherd in a small role—a quiet nod to Tarkovsky's own pup and broader love of dogs.

movies.title: On a String
movies.description: Isabel (Isabel Hagen) is a young, Juilliard-trained violist still living at home with her parents in the heart of New York City. She’s trying to make a living playing gigs with her friends, but when her toxic ex-boyfriend reappears – who also happens to be the Philharmonic's "newest, hottest cellist" – he informs her of a viola opening in the prestigious orchestra. Nothing can go wrong, right?

movies.title: On The Silver Globe
movies.description: After abandoning a dystopian future Earth, a small band of dissident astronauts crash-land on an earthlike planet and set out to establish a new human civilization—only to discover in time that they carry the seeds of their own slow demise and a new mythology. Polish writer-director Andrzej Żuławski adapted On the Silver Globe from The Lunar Trilogy , novels written between 1901 and 1911 by his grand-uncle, Jerzy Żuławski. After a year of filming in 1976 and 1977, Polish authorities shut down the production and ordered all materials destroyed, but the studio, cast, and crew preserved reels, costumes, and props, allowing Żuławski to devise a conclusion in time to screen the film at Cannes in 1988. RogerEbert.com proclaimed, “Even out of time, even incomplete, even now that its director is gone for good, On the Silver Globe endures and its beautiful power will never dim.”

movies.title: Powwow People
movies.description: Powwow People is a vérité-style documentary grounded in the rhythms, relationships, and lived experience of a contemporary Native gathering. Rather than entering as outside observers, the filmmakers organized the powwow itself, inviting dancers, singers, vendors, and community members to participate in the making of this film. Structured around the arc of a single day, the film follows four central figures: Gina Bluebird, who frames the powwow’s shape and guides its setup; Ruben Littlehead, the MC whose presence anchors the present moment; Jamie John, a non-binary dancer imagining the future of these traditions; and Freddie Cozad, a singer and drummer considering the past. The film culminates in a 30-minute unbroken shot of a Northern Traditional dance special, drawing the viewer into the textures, movement, and collective presence of the powwow. It is both a reflection of a beloved community and a gesture toward the continuities of Native life. Q&A with Sky Hopinka following the 7pm screenings on 9/11 and 9/12

movies.title: Silence Of The Lambs + Dog Factory
movies.description: The Silence of the Lambs (1991) Dir. Jonathan Demme With Jodie Foster, Anthony Hopkins, Scott Glenn, Ted Levine 118min; DCP When a top student at the FBI’s training academy (Foster) is tasked with hunting down a twisted serial killer, she employs the help of Dr. Hannibal Lecter (Hopkins), a psychiatrist who also happens to be a violent psychopath. Still the most recent movie to win all of the “Big Five” categories at the Academy Awards (and the only horror film to win Best Picture), Demme’s haunting psychological investigation not only lingers in the minds of its viewers, but in the cultural imaginary of American horror cinema. Alongside career-defining performances from a steadfast Foster and skin-crawling bravura depiction of psychopathy from Hopkins, a spunky little Bichon Frisé Darla (as Buffalo Bill’s companion Precious) delivers the punctuation to one of the film’s most famous lines: “It rubs the lotion on its skin, or else it gets the hose again!” Preceded by: Dog Factory (1904) Dir. Edwin S. Porter 4min; Digital This dark and surreal film from Edison’s studio features a vaudevillian trick in which sausages are turned into dogs and back again to their initial form through a “Dog Transformer” machine.

movies.title: Solaris
movies.description: Andrei Tarkovsky’s landmark of philosophical science fiction follows a psychologist dispatched to a space station outside the fictional planet of Solaris. The remaining crew has gone insane and the rules of consciousness seem to break down, leaving him to confront his innermost memories and desires—not to mention a certain ghost from his past. Made in response to Stanley Kubrick’s 2001: A Space Odyssey , Solaris draws us into its mysterious orbit as it explores not the wonders of a brave new world but the far more complex enigmas of the human mind.

movies.description: William Friedkin’s visually stunning film follows small-time crook Roy Scheider from Brooklyn to the sweltering South American jungles, where he lands a job hauling nitroglycerine with hard-luck losers Bruno Cremer and Francisco Rabal. Rather than simply remake Henri-Georges Clouzot’s famed WAGES OF FEAR, Friedkin re-imagined the story as a bleak, cosmic vision of man vs. nature, climaxing in the mind-bending image of Scheider and crew literally pushing a loaded truck across a spindly rope bridge.

movies.title: Space Dogs
movies.description: The first living being sent into space (to a certain death) was Laika, a stray dog from the streets of Moscow. In Russia, a legend spread that she had returned to earth as a ghost, roaming the streets she called home alongside her tangible descendants. A sparse documentary following the lives of stray dogs in Moscow (and the humans that weave in and out of their lives), Space Dogs blurs legend with truth, capturing the humanity of non-humans and humans alike.

movies.title: Space Is The Place
movies.description: Avant-garde jazz keyboardist, composer, and bandleader Sun Ra brought his iconoclastic Afrofuturist vision—and his chaotically swinging ensemble, the Arkestra—to the big screen with this 1974 feature, co-written by Ra based on lectures he’d delivered at the University of California, Berkeley. Touching down in Oakland after years in space, the regal Ra and his cohorts revisit the leader’s early days as a strip-club pianist, meets with inner-city youth, and sets out to rescue the Black population from earthly exploitation.

movies.title: Stalker
movies.description: One of the most immersive and rarefied experiences in the history of cinema, Andrei Tarkovsky’s Stalker embarks on a metaphysical journey through an enigmatic post-apocalyptic landscape. A hired guide—the “Stalker” of the title—leads a writer and a scientist into the heart of the Zone, the restricted site of a long-ago disaster, where the three men eventually zero in on the Room, a place rumored to fulfill one’s most deeply held desires. Adapting a science-fiction novel by Arkady and Boris Strugatsky, and making what would be his final Soviet feature, Tarkovsky created a challenging and visually stunning work, with painstaking attention to material detail and organic atmosphere. At once a religious allegory, a reflection of contemporary political anxieties, and a meditation on film itself—among many available interpretations— Stalker envelops the viewer in a multitude of possible meanings.

movies.title: Terminator 2: Judgment Day 35th Anniversary
movies.description:
From visionary director James Cameron, TERMINATOR 2: JUDGMENT DAY is the ultimate sci-fi blockbuster that redefined action forever. Arnold Schwarzenegger is back. This time, he’s the protector.
In a future ruled by machines, young John Connor holds the key to humanity’s survival. When a reprogrammed Terminator is sent back in time to protect him, a new threat emerges: the T-1000, a terrifying next-generation assassin capable of becoming anyone, anywhere. No rules. No limits. No mercy. As Sarah Connor races to stop Judgment Day before it begins, the fate of humanity hangs by a thread.
Winner of multiple Academy Awards, T2 delivers iconic action, legendary one-liners, and groundbreaking visual effects that changed cinema forever.
Back on the big screen this Judgment Day for the 35th anniversary.

movies.title: Tetsuo: The Iron Man
movies.description: A “metal fetishist” driven mad by maggots wriggling in the wounds he has created by driving metal into his flesh runs out into the night and is killed by an automobile. The driver, a businessman, buries the corpse with his girlfriend’s help, but soon begins to discover metal thorns and scabs erupting on his own body. A cult classic written, directed, edited, and produced by Shinya Tsukamoto, Tetsuo: The Iron Man earned a reputation as “one of the most pulverisingly effective sci-fi horror films of the past quarter of a century” ( Sight & Sound ) and comparisons to similarly transgressive works by Sam Raimi, David Cronenberg, and David Lynch.

movies.title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
movies.description:
It is difficult to imagine precisely what cinema would be without its most influential and memorable titles. THE CABINET OF DR. CALIGARI in particular stands out as one such notable title in the international canon that in its time and forever thereafter has been heralded as a masterpiece of its craft, the singular model for expressionist, black-and-white filmmaking.
A landmark of horror filmmaking, its visual style is often copied or paid homage, and its remarkable twist ending has become all but a modern trope. Its long, haunting shadows and canted, dreamlike production design stay with viewers weeks, months, and years following an initial viewing.
The film is credited for introducing the "twist" ending and inspired EDWARD SCISSORHANDS by Tim Burton, THE IMAGINARIUM OF DR. PARNASSUS by Terry Gilliam, and Martin Scorsese's SHUTTER ISLAND, all of which share many striking similarities to CALIGARI.
"The first thing everyone notices and best remembers about THE CABINET OF DR. CALIGARI (1920) is the film's bizarre look. The actors inhabit a jagged landscape of sharp angles and tilted walls and windows, staircases climbing crazy diagonals, trees with spiky leaves, grass that looks like knives. These radical distortions immediately set the film apart from all earlier ones." – Roger Ebert, Chicago Sun-Times

movies.title: The Dog Stars
movies.cast: Josh Brolin, Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley, Guy Pearce, Benedict Wong, Alara-Star Khan
movies.description: Ridley Scott making a post-apocalyptic movie is all you need to say to get us interested. THE DOG STARS swaps zombie hordes and wasteland spectacle for something quieter and more haunting: a survival story about the people who keep searching for hope after the world has already ended. Jacob Elordi leads an incredible ensemble that includes Josh Brolin, Margaret Qualley, Allison Janney, Benedict Wong, and a grizzled-looking Guy Pearce. And yes, there is a dog in THE DOG STARS. His name is Jasper and he’s a very good boy.

movies.description: Harry Lehman (John Turturro) is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York. Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily canceled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie. When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.

movies.title: The Outsiders: The Complete Novel
movies.description:
Francis Ford Coppola's "A-side" to his gang war films and S.E. Hinton adaptations (with RUMBLE FISH being the "B-side") remains one of the defining films of an alternate-Brat Pack and '80s masculinity. Starring a veritable who’s who of ‘80s heroes and heartthrobs – Swayze! Cruise! Lowe! Estevez! – in some of the earliest roles of their careers.
A teen gang in rural Oklahoma, the Greasers are perpetually at odds with rival group the Socs. When Greasers’ Ponyboy (C. Thomas Howell) and Johnny (Ralph Macchio) get into a brawl that ends in the accidental death of a Socs member, the boys go on the run. Soon, Ponyboy and Johnny, along with the intense Dallas (Matt Dillon) and their other Greaser buddies, must contend with the consequences of their violent lives.

movies.title: The Thin Man
movies.description: Nick, a former detective, retired when he married the wealthy heiress Nora, instead content to spend his days galavanting around high society. Abetted by his wife’s restless desire for adventure, the retired lawman embarks on a whodunnit quest to identify a missing inventor. Despite approaching a century since its release, The Thin Man flows with a miraculously contemporary pace and humor, replete with quick-firing ratatat from the leading couple, a jaw-dropping overconsumption of alcohol, and some truly belly laugh-inducing reaction shots from canine actor Skippy as Asta.

movies.title: The Twilight Saga: New Moon
movies.description: The supernatural tale of star-crossed lovers continues as the Cullen family flees Forks in order to protect Bella (Kristen Stewart), and the heartbroken high-school senior discovers that vampires aren't the only creatures in town. Realizing that Bella will never be safe as long as he's around, Edward (Robert Pattinson) makes the difficult decision to leave his beloved behind shortly after her 18th birthday. Reeling from her loss, Bella embraces self-destruction after being comforted by Edward's image during a moment of mortal peril. But as heavy-hearted as Bella may be, her friend Jacob (Taylor Lautner) distracts her from her sorrows by helping her renovate a weather-beaten motorbike. When Bella encounters a former adversary with a sizable grudge, she's rescued from harm at the last second by a pack of enormous, ferocious wolves. Subsequently delving into the history of the Quileutes, Bella discovers the secrets of Jacob's tribe while looking forward to a reunion with Edward that may have deadly consequences.

movies.title: The Wizard Of Oz
movies.description: The most seen film in cinematic history also features the most iconic dog to ever arf on the silver screen: Terry the Cairn Terrier as the ever-loyal Toto. While the prismatic story of Dorothy’s voyage through a magical world wasn’t the first Technicolor film put to screen, it surely popularized the technology with its jaw-dropping revelatory transition to vibrant color upon the Kansan’s arrival in Oz. Nominated for five Academy Awards and launching Judy Garland to international stardom, Victor Fleming’s ( Gone with the Wind ) landmark cinematic achievement lives on nearly 90 years after its release as America’s most enduring fairytale story.

movies.title: The Wrong Girls
movies.description: It's been a while since we got a good old-fashioned stoner comedy on the big screen. Kristen Stewart and Alia Shawkat star as codependent best friends scraping by paycheck to paycheck and bong rip to bong rip until a case of mistaken identity sends them into increasingly absurd trouble. Produced by the team behind BLOCKERS, THE WRONG GIRLS also features Seth Rogen and Kumail Nanjiani as the voices of two talking cats, which feels exactly right.

movies.title: Twilight (2008)
movies.description: TWILIGHT is an action-packed, modern-day love story between a teen girl and a vampire. Bella Swan (Kristen Stewart) has always been a bit different, never fitting in with the girls at her school. When Bella is sent to live with her father in the rainy little town of Forks, Washington, she doesn’t expect much to change. Then she meets the mysterious and dazzlingly beautiful Edward Cullen (Robert Pattinson), a boy unlike any she’s ever met. Edward is a vampire, but he doesn’t have fangs and his family is unique in that they choose not to drink human blood. Edward has been waiting 90 years for a soul mate, which he finds in Bella. They are soon swept up in a passionate and unorthodox romance. Edward must struggle to resist the primal pull of her scent, which could send him into an uncontrollable frenzy, but what will they do when a clan of new vampires – James (Cam Gigandet), Laurent (Edi Gathegi), and Victoria (Rachelle Lefevre) – come to town and threaten to disrupt their way of life?

movies.title: Umberto D.
movies.description: This neorealist masterpiece by Vittorio De Sica follows an elderly pensioner as he strives to make ends meet during Italy’s postwar economic recovery. Alone except for his dog, Flike, Umberto struggles to maintain his dignity in a city where human kindness seems to have been swallowed up by the forces of modernization. His simple quest to satisfy his basic needs—food, shelter, companionship—makes for one of the most heartbreaking stories ever filmed, and an essential classic of world cinema.

movies.title: Union County
movies.description: This unflinching look at the opioid epidemic follows brothers Cody (Poulter) and Jack Parsons (Centineo) as they navigate a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program, and pursue the promise of a brighter, sober future together. Anchored by poignant, moving performances from its leading duo, Ohio-born filmmaker Adam Meeks’ creates a film imbued with realism for an honest, compassionate portrait of a battle being fought across America and the solidarity that flowers on its front lines.

Penniless and unhoused, Wendy (Williams) is traveling to Alaska when she loses her dog (played by Reichhardt’s own pup Lucy), sending her on a mission to reunite with her sole confidant. Minimal and heart-wrenching, Wendy and Lucy is a stunning exploration of loneliness, and a masterclass display of Reichhardt's meticulous vision.

movies.director: Masaki Kobayashi Based on a collection of folktales by Lafcadio Hearn
movies.cast: Tatsuya Nakadai, Rentarô Mikuni, Michiyo Aratama, Misako Watanabe

movies.title: 12 Years A Slave
movies.description: 12 Years a Slave is based on an incredible true story of one man’s fight for survival and freedom. In the pre-Civil War United States, Solomon Northup (Chiwetel Ejiofor), a free Black man from upstate New York, is abducted and sold into slavery. Facing cruelty personified by a malevolent slave owner (Michael Fassbender) as well as unexpected kindnesses, Solomon struggles not only to stay alive, but to retain his dignity. In the twelfth year of his unforgettable odyssey, Solomon's chance meeting with a Canadian abolitionist (Brad Pitt) forever alters his life. The winner of three Academy Awards including Best Picture, 12 Years a Slave returns to BAM screens alongside the new restoration of Gordon Park’s version of the same story, Solomon Northrup’s Odyssey .

movies.title: 2026 Oscar Nominated Animated Shorts
movies.description: These meticulously animated works of art follow a wide range of fascinating characters, from an Olympic swimmer who survived the Holocaust to an intrepid kid bravely attempting to rescue her village. Please note that some films contain disturbing material and may not be suitable for very young children. Butterfly Dir. Florence Miailhe France, 15min A poignant retelling of Olympic swimmer Alfred Nakache’s life, from his rise to fame to surviving Auschwitz, presented as memories flashing back during his final swim. Forevergreen Dirs. Nathan Engelhardt & Jeremy Spears US, 13min A joyful adventure featuring an orphaned bear cub and a fatherly tree turns serious when the cub is tempted by the allure of easy food. Fire and deadly danger ensue as the cub is left bereft of hope and on the verge of a ruinous end, until the sacrificial love of the tree falls into place. The Girl Who Cried Pearls Dirs. Chris Lavis & Maciek Szczerbowski Canada, 17min A haunting fable about a girl overwhelmed by sorrow, the boy who loves her, and how greed leads good hearts to wicked deeds. Retirement Plan Dir. John Kelly Ireland, 7min Ray (voiced by Domhall Gleeson) fantasizes about everything he’d love to do in retirement, once he finally has the “time.” The Three Sisters Dir. Konstantin Bronzit Israel & Cyprus, 14min Three sisters live a lonely life on an isolated island, each in their own small house. One day, circumstances change, and they are forced to rent out one of the houses. Also screening in this program: Éiru Dir. Giovanna Ferrari Ireland, 13min When the water mysteriously disappears from the well in a warrior clan’s village, an intrepid child descends into the belly of the earth to retrieve it. Éiru is the story of a kid in search of a challenge and a goddess in search of a champion.

movies.title: 2026 Oscar Nominated Live-Action Shorts
movies.description: These Oscar-contending films from Israel, the UK, the US, and France explore the messy, beautiful, and often forbidden ways we seek connection. Butcher’s Stain Dir. Meyer Levinson-Blount Israel, 26min Samir, a Palestinian butcher working at an Israeli supermarket, is accused of tearing down the Israeli hostage posters in the break room. Samir sets out to prove his innocence in order to keep the job he so desperately needs. A Friend of Dorothy Dir. Lee Knight UK, 21min Dorothy is a lonely widow whose body is failing but whose mind remains sharp as ever. When 17-year-old JJ accidentally kicks his football into her garden, an unlikely friendship blossoms. Jane Austen’s Period Drama Dirs. Steve Pinder & Julia Aks US, 12min In 1813 England, Essy Talbot’s long-awaited marriage proposal takes a messy turn when her period arrives at a very bad time. The Singers Dir. Sam A. Davis US, 18min The Singers is a film adaptation of a 19th-century short story written by Ivan Turgenev, in which downtrodden patrons in a lowly pub connect unexpectedly through an impromptu sing-off. Two People Exchanging Saliva Dirs. Natalie Musteata & Alexandre Singh France, 36min In a society where kissing is punishable by death and people pay for things by receiving slaps to the face, an unhappy woman shops compulsively in a department store and becomes entranced by one of the employees.

A sort-of sequel to Wong’s Days of Being Wild and In the Mood for Love, the ’60s-set 2046 revisits Tony Leung Chiu-wai’s Chow, now a suave science-fiction writer, to chronicle his various affairs with women (including Faye Wong, Zhang Ziyi, and Gong…

movies.title: 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple
movies.description: The nature of the infected is changing… Director Nia DaCosta expands the grisly, post-apocalyptic world first forged by Danny Boyle and Alex Garland with 2002’s 28 Days Later and built upon in 2025’s 28 Years Later . In this third entry, Dr. Kelson (Fiennes) forms a relationship whose consequences could alter the fate of humanity, while Spike’s (Williams) encounter with Jimmy Crystal (O’Connell) spirals into a nightmare he can’t escape. In the world of The Bone Temple, the infected are no longer the greatest threat to survival—the inhumanity of the survivors proves far more terrifying.

movies.title: 3 Women
movies.description: Alongside his more touted multi-character panoramas, Altman also had a fondness for small-scale dramas investigating the complexities of female psychology, and of these none is greater than the ineffable 3 Women, which finds Shelley Duvall, Sissy Spacek,…

movies.title: 9 To 5
movies.description: Three working women try to overthrow their misogynist, egotistical boss in this wacky, over-the-top 1980 comedy. Directed by Colin Higgins (writer of Harold and Maude ), and perhaps best-known for its titular theme song, the workplace romp spawned a television series, stage adaptation, and further launched Dolly Parton to mainstream superstardom.

movies.title: 99%: The Occupy Wall Street Collaborative Film
movies.director: Aaron Aites, Audrey Ewell & Nina Krstic
movies.description: Lou Reed narrates this award-winning documentary, a deep dive into the breadth and depth of the Occupy Wall Street Movement. The spark lit in a small park in lower Manhattan would snowball into an international movement, aimed at removing money from politics in an effort to move power from corporate interests into the hands of the people. The thought-provoking presentation includes interviews from Occupiers, economist Jeffrey Sachs, and business magnate Russell Simmons, tracing the movement’s aims of tackling affordable access to health care and education, protecting the environment, creating jobs, and more.

movies.title: A Day in the Country + People on Sunday
movies.director: Robert Siodmak, Jean  Renoir , Edgar G. Ulmer
movies.description: Two slices of life from Europe entre deux guerres, and two compact masterpieces. Renoir’s featurette fragment, based on a Guy de Maupassant short story and only edited 10 years after its shoot came to a premature end, evokes the disappeared world of…

movies.title: A Flame At The Pier
movies.description: 35mm print imported from Japan (courtesy of the Japan Foundation) “An early masterpiece by Shinoda, this bleak youth film follows Sabu (Takashi Fujiki), who exploits fellow dockworkers under orders from his boss. He falls for Yuki (Mariko Kaga, making her feature film debut), but their bittersweet romance spirals into conflict. Set against the sharply photographed docklands of Yokohama, the film marks the fourth collaboration between Shinoda and Shuji Terayama. Together, they deftly weave themes of working class struggles and labor strikes into the story, making a critique of postwar reality of Japan. Terayama also contributed two theme songs, performed by the lead Takashi Fujiki.” - Akinaru Rokkaku

movies.title: A Grin Without A Cat
movies.description: This epic film-essay from Chris Marker ( La Jetée ) investigates the worldwide political wars of the ‘60s and ‘70s, especially the emergence of the New Left. Originally released in 1978, BAM is delighted to show the restored and “re-actualized” version Marker released after the fall of the Soviet Union 15 years later. Described by Marker as "scenes of the Third World War," the film interweaves imagery of Lewis Carroll's Cheshire Cat in an indictment of the leftist movement’s unfortunate failure to manifest meaningful change. Whereas Vineland tracks the story of a fictional left wing revolutionary, Marker’s film traces the movement’s real successes and failures in the West.

movies.title: A Guide to Walk Cycles for Animators and Non-Animators
movies.description: Join Low Cinema for a collection of eclectic short independent animated films from the brilliant filmmakers who contributed to the zine A Guide to Walk Cycles for Animators and Non-Animators , compiled and written by Magician Studio. Screening curated by Magician Studio (a project of James Thacher and Amanda Bonaiuto )

movies.title: A Litany For Survival: The Life And Work Of Audre Lorde
movies.description: This epic portrait of the award-winning Black lesbian poet, mother, teacher, and activist Audre Lorde catalogs an incredibly impactful, revolutionary career. From her childhood roots in Harlem to her battle with breast cancer, the film explores a life, and a body of work, that bridged the Civil Rights movement, the women’s movement, and the struggle for lesbian and gay rights. New restoration premier; Q&A to follow with Ada Gay Griffin, Michelle Parkerson & J.T. Takagi

movies.title: A Matter Of Life And Death
movies.description: Haya grew up in the shadow of a curse’s promise that she would die at 30. After a series of failed attempts to end her life—an effort to take her fate into her own hands—she crosses paths with a brilliant but emotionally withdrawn surgeon. Youssef, who suffers from an abnormally slow heartbeat and only truly feels alive when he's operating and holding a scalpel, might be just who Haya has been looking for. Her request that Youssef kill her kicks off a flowering relationship, and a surprisingly uplifting exploration of the existential struggles that plague so many on the precipice of entering their thirties.

movies.title: A New Leaf
movies.description:
The world may be getting less perfect, but at least we are slowly starting to have the works of Elaine May available for viewing, and thus that much richer with odd comedy.
Henry, a carefree playboy having just burned through his trust fund and allergic to the idea of actual work, turns his efforts toward landing a sugar mama with comically disastrous results. In the nick of time, he meets Henrietta, a clumsy heiress with a passion for botany, and the two marry. Moving into her home and formulating a plan to murder her and collect, he finds stiff competition with her lawyer and household staff all already preying on her wealth. When Henrietta sets out to find the new species of fern she has discovered, Henry tags along for the canoe trip in the Adirondacks, finding it a perfect opportunity for an accident. But can he really go through with it, being that she so sweetly intends to name the plant after him? (Cristina Cacioppo)
Introduced by film professor, Steven DeRosa

movies.title: A Night With Alex Tatarsky
movies.description: The word cinema is an abbreviation of the French cinématographe , a term coined by the Lumière Brothers, who combined the Greek words for “movement” and “writing” to describe this new form of expression. As part of Triple Canopy Presents: Magic, Alex Tatarsky—2025 Triple Canopy fellow—will share a local clown’s take on “movement writing.” Tatarsky will present research and workshop characters live with the audience for a new piece of fiction that considers American traditions of conjuring and spirit channeling in the lineage of experimental improvisational performance. Part lecture, part seance, Tatarsky’s performance draws on the researcher and artist Shannon Taggart’s investigations into spectral photography and “spirit cinema” to investigate the life of objects and the material of spirit.

movies.title: A Sad And Beautiful World
movies.description: Across three decades of passion, loss, and hope, Nino and Yasmina are bound by a magnetic relationship. Torn between love and survival, the reunited childhood sweethearts must decide whether to build a family and seek happiness in Lebanon, or leave their home amid the country’s unfolding tragedies. A heartfelt portrayal of resilience, A Sad and Beautiful World made its world premiere at Venice Days, where it won the People’s Choice Award. Followed by a Q&A with director Cyril Aris

movies.title: A Tribe Called Love
movies.description: New York Premiere In a Somali neighbourhood in Toronto, innocent teenagers Farah and Halima fall in love. But both have been warned to stay away from each other because they are from different tribes. When Farah's family moves to Vancouver because of a neighbourhood tragedy, the young lovers are torn apart. Their romance rekindles in their 20s when they reunite in Toronto. That is, until the same cultural barriers that once divided them resurface. Will their love be enough to rewrite their fate, or are some tragedies destined to repeat themselves? This modern-day Romeo and Juliet cautionary tale explores whether cultural barriers can be broken once and for all. A Tribe Called Love is told with the pop, bang and pizzazz of Scott Pilgrim vs The World , mixed with the tension, comedy, and tightly-knit neighbourhood of Spike Lee's Do The Right Thing . Winner of the Audience Choice Award at the 2025 Reelworld Film Festival. May 22 screening followed by a Q&A with director Mohamed Ahmed, producer Andy Marshall, and cast—moderated by Muna Mohamed

movies.title: A Tribute To Assata: Eyes Of The Rainbow
movies.description: After escaping from prison in 1979, the revolutionary, thinker, and Black Panther and Black Liberation Army leader Assata Shakur found political asylum in Cuba, where she lived in exile for over 40 years. Gloria Rolando’s Eyes of the Rainbow finds Shakur in Havana discussing life before and after exile and her own Afro-Cuban roots. Weaving together Shakur’s spiritual connection to the Yoruba Orisha Oya, her militant political commitments and an Afro-diasporic tapestry of music, Rolando dedicated the documentary to “all women who struggle for a better world.” Assata Shakur joined the ancestors on September 25, 2025 and the screening will be an occasion for remembrance centered on her lifelong devotion to freedom from all forms of oppression. The screening will be followed by a conversation with series programmer Yasmina Price, organizer Monifa Bandele and filmmaker Yaania Bell about collective struggle, memory, and the intertwinement of culture and militancy.

movies.title: A Woman’S Tormet
movies.cast: Tara Chung, Jennifer Jordan, Jake Teague, Marlene Willoughby, Anna Davis, Jeffrey Hurst

movies.title: Abraham Lincoln
movies.description: This pre-Hays Code biopic from D. W. Griffith ( The Birth of a Nation ) follows the life of Abraham Lincoln, chronicling his early years as a country lawyer and romance with Ann Rutledge through to his presidency and later assasination. This hushed film, far from the rousing American mythmaking of John Ford’s Young Mister Lincoln or Griffith’s own Americana, depicts a Lincoln (portrayed brilliantly by Walter Huston—who also plays the Devil in All That Money Can Buy ) haunted by past tragedy and fated to an early demise.

movies.title: Afro-Cuban Music
movies.description: Through experimental polemics, observational studies and historical investigations, these inventive documentaries explore the African roots of Cuban music through the intersection of cultural and political struggle. NOW! (1965) Dir. Santiago Alvarez 6min, DCP Influential Cuban filmmaker Santiago Alvarez combines footage of police brutality and Black Liberation from the 60s Civil Rights movement, scored by Lena Horne’s urgent musical call to action in a radical montage. Habana Solo (2000) Dir. Juan Carlos Alom 15min, Digital A city symphony in miniature, Alom’s powerful short juxtaposes Havana’s streets and peoples and the music of Afro-Cuban street performers. Y . . . tenemos sabor (1967) Dir. Sara Gómez 30min, DCP Following pioneering Rumba musician Alberto Zayas, this dynamic documentary takes us through the history of Cuban music. A Short Radiography of Hip Hop in Cuba (2004) Dir. Ricardo Bacallao 21min, DCP A look at the history of hip-hop culture in Cuba through the eyes of Rodolfo Rensoli, founder of the Cuban Hip Hop Festival.

movies.title: After Hours
movies.description: Cheech and Chong! Sultry sculptress Linda Fiorentino! Bad Brains! These are but a few of the characters that Midtown computer jockey Paul Hackett (Griffin Dunne) will encounter when venturing into the wilds of a pre-gentrification downtown New York…

movies.title: After Hours
movies.description: When office worker Paul Hackett (Dunne) embarks on a seemingly innocuous journey downtown to meet up with a mysterious woman (Arquette) he met at a coffee shop hours earlier, her surreal behavior is just the first of many surprises. As the night unravels, this portrait of 1980s SoHo follows Hackett into Berlin-themed nightclubs, the apartment of a distressed waitress (Teri Garr), and the ice cream truck of a do-gooder driver (Catherine O’Hara). This early-career Scorsese masterpiece—anchored by Michael Ballhaus’ frantic cinematography—toes the line between haunting and absurd as increasingly higher stakes prevent Hackett’s simple journey: to get home.

movies.title: After Oil
movies.description: Across Algeria, South Africa, and Kenya, communities and refugee camps confront the realities of the global energy transition. Stories of resistance to fossil fuel extraction on indigenous land, the unequal distribution of energy infrastructure in cities, and grassroots struggles for self-determination in resource-exploited regions intertwine to reveal the human stakes of energy policy. Together, these perspectives illuminate the broader political, environmental, and social challenges shaping Africa in the green energy transition. Followed by a Q&A with director Boima Tucker

movies.title: Alam
movies.description: Tamer, a Palestinian living in Israel, leads the life of a typical high school student until the beautiful Maysaa​​’ arrives. Hoping to impress her, he agrees to take part in a mysterious operation to covertly raise the Palestinian flag and peacefully disrupt local celebrations on the eve of Israel’s Independence Day—a day of mourning for Palestinians. Unsure of his own convictions, Tamer must determine what matters to him. A skillful examination of the fraught political awakening young Palestinians are forced to undergo, this striking debut feature film from Firas Khoury “perfectly captures teenage fearlessness and bravado along with a certain cluelessness about how the real world works” ( Variety ).

movies.title: All Dirt Roads Taste Of Salt
movies.description: The feature debut from writer-director Raven Jackson, All Dirt Roads Taste of Salt serves as a decade-spanning portrait of Mack, a Black woman in Mississippi. With minimal dialogue and breathtaking cinematography from Jomo Fray ( Nickel Boys ), the sparse, unhurried film weaves alternately through love and heartbreak, joy and sorrow, connection and loss in a stunning dedication to the experience of being alive. The July 25 screening followed by a Q&A with Raven Jackson.

movies.title: All That Money Can Buy (Aka The Devil And Daniel Webster)
movies.description: In 1840, hardworking farmer Jabez Stone is broke and plagued by seemingly pre-ordained bad luck. After a series of mishaps cement his tough streak, his impulsive declaration that he would sell his soul to the devil manifests the personification of evil himself (a mischievous, terrifying Walter Huston—who also plays the eponymous role in D. W. Griffith’s Abraham Lincoln ) offering good luck in exchange. As Stone’s ill-begotten luck improves and his wealth mounts, he transforms into an increasingly sinister husband, son, and community member. Originally released as All That Money Can Buy but later dubbed The Devil and Daniel Webster , this supernatural thriller unpacks the nefarious nature of wealth.

movies.title: All That’S Left Of You
movies.description: A deeply moving, multigenerational drama, All That’s Left of You follows a Palestinian teenager who gets swept into a protest in the Occupied West Bank and experiences a moment of violence that rocks his family. The film unfolds as his mother recounts the political and emotional threads that led to that fateful moment. Spanning seven decades, the film—Jordan’s official selection for the 98th Academy Awards—traces the hopes and heartaches of one uprooted family, bearing witness to the scars of dispossession and the enduring legacy of survival. Followed by a Q&A with director & actor Cherien Dabis and actor Adam Bakri.

movies.title: Alma Punk (Punk Soul)
movies.description: Like Nadie es Innocente , Minter’s 1991 film Alma Punk combines improvisation and non-actors in a uniquely produced exploration of Mexico City’s punk scene. Starring a cast led by real-life punk Ana Hernandez (as Alma, which also means “soul”), Alma Punk traces the tortuous path of a young riot grrl from the Mexico City punk scene as she moves north to Tijuana and, eventually, towards the United States. It confidently breaks with the rules of staging docudrama with an unsparing look at Alma’s love life, unfakeable scene bohemianism, and extensive location footage of Mexico before NAFTA and after the 1985 earthquake.

movies.title: Alpha
movies.description: Life swiftly starts to unravel for Alpha and her single mom after the rebellious 13-year-old comes home with a stick-and-poke tattoo made with a used needle at a house party—a mark that may be related to a contagious blood-borne disease that turns its victims into disintegrating stone. The third feature by French director and screenwriter Julia Ducournau, winner of the Palme d’Or at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival for Titane , is a mysterious, unsettling allegory for the 1980s AIDS crisis and the waves of hysteria, prejudice, and exclusion it produced.

movies.title: American Doctor
movies.cast: Thaer Ahmad, Mark Perlmutter, Feroze Sidhwa
movies.description: From Oscar®-nominated and Emmy® Award-winning filmmaker Poh Si Teng, American Doctor follows three American physicians— Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian—united by a single oath to save lives. After volunteering in besieged hospitals in Gaza, they return home determined to fight for the patients and colleagues they left behind, taking their battle from the front lines of war to the halls of Congress.

movies.title: Ana
movies.description: The second docufiction collaboration between Reis and Cordeiro, and perhaps the most narratively grounded, Ana follows its titular elderly matriarch and her family in Portugal’s Trás-os-Montes region. In its dedication to Ana as subject, she contains a multiplicity, representing a vibrant tapestry of nature and tradition woven into the region’s daily life.

movies.title: And Then There Was Light
movies.description: The confrontation of a traditional rural/agrarian culture bound to the land and the cycles of the seasons and an urban/industrial society that has largely forgotten these ties, an abiding concern of Iosseliani’s cinema, plays out against a backdrop…

movies.title: Arco
movies.description: In the year 2075, a 10-year-old girl witnesses a mysterious boy in a rainbow suit fall from the sky. Arco comes from an idyllic far future where time travel is possible. Iris shelters him, and will do whatever it takes to help him return to his time. In return, Arco gives Iris hope for an optimistic future. Directed by author and comic-book illustrator Ugo Bienvenu, this vivacious animated feature debuted at Cannes and won recognition from the New York Film Critics Online and Lumière Awards alongside dozens of prestigious nominations. Academy Award nominee, Best Animated Feature

movies.title: Arteeast Presents Prince Of Nothingwood
movies.description: Co-presented with ArteEast Sonia Kronlund follows Salim Shaheen, the most prolific actor-director-producer in Afghanistan, as he leaves Kabul to shoot his 111th film (or maybe 114th? He’s lost count). In tow is the director’s trusty troupe of delightful outcasts, each more eccentric than the last, determined to make films by whatever means necessary—even if it means dodging landmines and firing live ammunition to get the shot. In conjunction with ArteEast, we’re thrilled to screen Kronlund’s “magical and intrepid” ( The Guardian ) Prince of Nothingwood for one night only on March 3. Stay after the screening for filmmaker Arsalan Danish in conversation with Moshtari Hilal and Parwana Haydar of the Afghan Visual Arts & History Collective

movies.title: Arzé
movies.description: Mira Shaib’s feature debut follows Arzé (Abou Abboud), a single mother in Beirut attempting to expand her business selling homemade pies. To afford a delivery scooter, she steals her sister’s beloved bracelet, only to have the scooter stolen the same day. Arzé and her son embark on a journey navigating through the bustling neighborhoods of Beirut to find what they’ve lost as guilt and pressure mount.

movies.title: Assassination
movies.description: 35mm print imported from Japan (courtesy of the Japan Foundation) “Near the end of Japan’s feudal era, Ronin Hachiro Kiyokawa, a smart but shady leader working for the Shogunate, is being secretly watched by a spy ready to kill him if he switches sides. As violence grows between rival political groups, the film digs into themes of loyalty, power, and deception. Its non-linear flashback style keeps Kiyokawa’s true motives unclear. The film stands out as an important part of the Japanese New Wave movement, and Tetsurō Tamba gives a subtle, mysterious performance as Kiyokawa.” - Shun Inoue

movies.title: Backrooms
movies.description: Drawing on the deep dread of so-called “liminal” spaces—the non-places of depopulated office buildings and parking lots of late capitalist America—this feature debut from 20-year-old Kane Parsons was inspired by a sprawling fictional location first chronicled in a 2019 4chan thread. A simple premise straight out of the internet age snowballs into psychological terror as store-owner Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor) and his therapist (Renate Reinsve) venture into an unknown dimension through a strange doorway that has appeared in the basement of a furniture showroom.

movies.title: Bakri Family Shorts Program
movies.description: In addition to their distinguished careers in feature films, members of the Bakri family have appeared in numerous short films spanning a variety of visions and styles. This collection of representative shorts—including one in which Ziad Bakri directs his father and brother—illuminates facets of everyday Palestinian life and more. The Salt Fisherman (2011) Dir. Ziad Bakri 18min With Mohammad Bakri, Saleh Bakri A fisherman lives alone, rising with the sun and carrying his anxieties and tools to the sea, where he works. What's behind his days? Upshot (2024) Dir. Maha Haj 34min With Mohammad Bakri, Areen Omari, Ala Hlehel Suleiman and Mona lead a solitary life caring for animals and trees, and have constant heated discussions about their children’s life choices. Their routine is disturbed when a stranger shows up one day, calling to mind a painful past. The Present (2020) Dir. Farah Nabulsi 24min With Saleh Bakri, Mariam Kanj, Mariam Basha A father and his daughter set out to buy his wife a gift for their wedding anniversary, but are soon confronted by a military checkpoint. Mare Nostrum (2016) Dirs. Rana Kazkaz and Anas Khalaf 13min With Ziad Bakri, Zayn Khalaf On a Mediterranean shore, a Syrian father makes a decision that puts his daughter’s life at risk.

movies.title: Bam | Arteeast Presents: My Father And Qaddafi
movies.description: Jihan’s father Mansur Rashid Kikhia was the Foreign Minister of Libya, ambassador to the United Nations, and a human rights lawyer. After serving in Qaddafi's increasingly brutal regime, he defected from the government and became the leader of the peaceful opposition. For many, Kikhia was a rising star who could have been the next leader of Libya. In 1993, he disappeared from his hotel in Egypt. Jihan’s mother Baha Al Omary, a strong-willed Syrian-American artist, began searching for him, launching the family into an international political maze. Her mission to find justice brought her to the Libyan desert in the middle of the night, face to face with Qaddafi to negotiate her husband’s release. Yet it wasn’t until after the regime’s fall, 19 years later, that his body was found in a freezer near Qaddafi’s palace. My Father and Qaddafi takes the audience on a raw and reflective journey as Jihan pieces together a father she barely remembers, while discovering the troubled history and politics of Libya. Her journey starts from fading personal memories, leading to encounters with family members, her father’s peers, and historical archive footage. Hoping at first to uncover the truth, Jihan instead transforms the mystery into a curiosity that brings her closer to her father and her Libyan identity. She approaches politics not as a distant subject, but as a lived experience that penetrates into every human relationship—even between a little girl and her father. Screening will be followed by a discussion.

movies.title: Barbarella
movies.description: In the 41st century, astronaut Barbarella (Fonda) is tasked with finding Dr. Durand Durand, a scientist the Earth’s government believes to be developing a weapon that could signal the end of humanity. In a 98 minute run-time littered with sensationally campy set design and vibrant costuming, Barbarella’s quest sends her from planet to planet in this ‘60s signature cult film.

movies.title: Before Sunrise
movies.description: Linklater’s ongoing, decades-spanning story of a love affair through its many ups and downs begins here, with a chance encounter on a train between Ethan Hawke and Julie Delpy, the American Jesse and the French Céline, who together will pass a day and…

movies.title: Beloved
movies.description: Based on Toni Morrison’s 1987 novel of the same name, Demme’s Gothic horror take on one of contemporary literature’s most enduring stories is teeming with the notes that made its original text so moving: emotional, powerful, and haunting. The tale of a formerly enslaved woman plagued by a poltergeist and fantastically revisited by a reincarnated daughter, Beloved marries magical realism with the material tragedy of America’s past.

movies.title: Berlin Express
movies.description: In the aftermath of World War II, a diverse group of train passengers band together in search of a kidnapped German peace activist. One of the only American-made “rubble films” (shot in bombed-down locations across Frankfurt and Berlin), Tourneur presents a striking image of Europe after the war. It also conveys a Pynchonian flair in its constant shifting of loyalties and geographies, akin to Gravity’s Rainbow .

movies.title: Bicycle Thieves
movies.description: Hailed around the world as one of the greatest movies ever made, the Academy Award–winning Bicycle Thieves , directed by Vittorio De Sica, defined an era in cinema. In poverty-stricken postwar Rome, a desperate man is on the first day of a new job when his bicycle, which he needs for his work, is stolen. With his young son in tow, he sets off to track down the thief. Simple in construction and profoundly rich in human insight, Bicycle Thieves embodies the greatest strengths of the Italian neorealist movement: emotional clarity, social rectitude, and brutal honesty.

movies.title: Billy Liar
movies.director: John Schlesinger Screenplay by Keith Waterhouse and Willis Hall Based on Waterhouse & Hall’s play and Waterhouse’s novel
movies.cast: Tom Courtenay, Julie Christie, Mona Washbourne, Finlay Currie, Leonard Rossiter
movies.description: Alternately hilarious and mortifying, one of the finest—certainly the funniest—movies to come out of the 1960s Brit New Wave explosion. Based on Keith Waterhouse’s novel and the hit West End play by Waterhouse and Willis Hall (with Courtenay and Albert Finney alternating the title role), the movie adaptation would spawn a popular TV series, a sequel to the novel ( Billy Liar on the Moon ), and a successful stage musical, while cementing the careers of both Courtenay (“probably the best of Britai

movies.title: Black Cops, Spies And Overseers
movies.description: Programmed by Steven W. Thrasher and Jesse Trussell The silver screen is replete with Black cops who make us laugh (Eddie Murphy’s Axel Foley in Beverly Hills Cop , OJ Simpson’s Officer Nordberg in The Naked Gun , Cleavon Little's Bart in Blazing Saddles) and Black spies who question the American empire (Tamara Dobson in Cleopatra Jones , Lawrence Cook in The Spook Who Sat by the Doo r). Are these films “only a movie” or “just funny”—or are they policing the boundaries of our imaginations? Inspired by Steven W. Thrasher’s book The Overseer Class , this series of 12 American films made over 70 years challenges our assumptions about the performance of dramatic Black police (Sidney Poitier in In the Heat of the Night , Denzel Washington in Training Day ), outright overseers (Samuel L. Jackson in Django Unchained , Poitier in Band of Angels ), and even queerbaiting undercover spies (Al Pacino in Cruising ).

movies.title: Black Girl
movies.description: Seventeen-year-old dreamer Billie Jean (Peggy Pettit) is the youngest in a family of loving yet discouraging women. Her mother, Mama Rosie (Louise Stubbs), cares deeply about her three biological children. However, her own personal disappointments have left her embittered, and she only offers encouragement to her adopted daughter, Netta (Leslie Uggams). When Netta, a successful teacher, returns to visit the family, she may be the voice of guidance and hope Billie Jean desperately needs. Followed by a Q&A with writer J.E. Franklin

movies.title: Black Girl + Borom Sarret
movies.description: Black Girl (1966) Dir. Ousmane Sembène With Mbissine Thérèse Diop 59min; DCP In French with English subtitles Father of African cinema Ousmane Sembène’s feature debut is one of the most acclaimed films ever made. Senegalese housemaid Diouana (Diop) is brought to France by the white family she works for, finding herself isolated in an unfamiliar country and trapped in a life of domestic servitude–a situation that the dignified young woman refuses to accept. Both a landmark of world cinema and a devastating indictment of colonialism’s tragic legacy, Black Girl is the first African film to receive international acclaim; Martin Scorsese called it: “an astonishing movie—so ferocious, so haunting, and so unlike anything we’d ever seen.” Sembène’s luminous black and white images have a direct expressive power, and they gleam anew in this restoration. Borom Sarret (1963) Dir. Ousmane Sembène 20min; DCP In French with English subtitles. Sembène’s first film, a neorealist look at the hardscrabble life of a wagon driver who encounters a cross-section of Dakar’s inhabitants as he makes his rounds through the streets of the city.

movies.title: Black Orpheus
movies.description: Winner of both the Academy Award for best foreign-language film and the Cannes Film Festival’s Palme d’Or, Marcel Camus’ Black Orpheus (Orfeu negro) brings the ancient Greek myth of Orpheus and Eurydice to the 20th-century madness of Carnival in Rio de Janeiro. With its eye-popping photography and ravishing, epochal soundtrack, Black Orpheus was an international cultural event, and kicked off the bossa nova craze that set hi-fis ablaze around the world.

movies.title: Black& Loving: The Artist Way
movies.description: Chronicles of a Lying Spirit (by Kelly Gabron) (1992) dir. Cauleen Smith 6min; digital Looking for "Looking for Langston" (2019) dir. Ada M. Patterson 15min; DCP Looking for Langston (1989) dir. Isaac Julien 45 min; DCP black& loving, a film program created by Tyler Green and Sokhna Samb to celebrate Black and queer artists, returns to BAM with the artist way , commemorating creators whose works have defined American culture and influenced today’s Black artists. Chronicles of a Lying Spirit (by Kelly Gabron) , directed by Cauleen Smith, offers an experimental reintegration of Black women into history. Looking for "Looking for Langston" was made by Ada M. Patterson after learning about, but being unable to see, the classic Isaac Julien work. Finally Julien’s critically acclaimed Looking for Langston explores the personal life of the beloved poet and activist Langston Hughes, incorporating archival footage from the Harlem Renaissance. These filmmakers situate their works to address the Black experience through the lens of gender and sexuality, as well as issues arising from that intersection.

movies.title: Blind Fury
movies.cast: Rutger Hauer, Terry O’Quinn, Brandon Call, Noble Willingham, Lisa Blount, Nick Cassavetes
movies.description: It'll hit you right between the eyes!

movies.title: Blknws: Terms & Conditions
movies.description: Visual artist and filmmaker Kahlil Joseph’s video installation “BLKNWS” debuted in galleries and museums across the country in 2019, immersing viewers in the imagined world of a television news network from a Black perspective. After expanding this concept into a short film, Joseph has developed it even further into a feature film, and the result is a celebration of Black life that reconceptualizes and remediates common, corporate notions of journalism. Joseph’s sprawling film is an uninterrupted gush of ideas, mixing newly shot footage and extant media, leaping from fantastical images to historical narratives, collapsing boundaries that often separate documentary and fiction. A multidimensional work of vision and ambition, BLKNWS: Terms & Conditions offers an alternately riotous and meditative compendium of the Black experience.

movies.title: Blood Theatre
movies.description: Cooked inside a popcorn machine, stabbed in the ticket booth, fried by a film projector: these are just a few of the fates awaiting some supremely unlucky cinema workers in Rick Sloane’s bloody 1980s slasher comedy. Come out for an evening of grisly on-screen fun—and rest assured that, unlike the theater depicted on screen, you’ll be safe and sound at BAM. Featuring a reading by A.T. Pratt before the screening on February 13 .

movies.title: Blow Out
movies.description: In the enthralling BLOW OUT, brilliantly crafted by Brian De Palma (MISSION: IMPOSSIBLE), John Travolta (PULP FICTION) gives one of his greatest performances as a movie sound effects man who believes he has accidentally recorded a political assassination. He enlists the help of a possible eyewitness to the crime (Nancy Allen, ROBOCOP), who may be in danger herself, to uncover the truth. With its jolting stylistic flourishes, intricate plot, profoundly felt characterizations, and gritty evocation of early-1980s Philadelphia, BLOW OUT is an American paranoia thriller unlike any other, as well as a devilish reflection on moviemaking.

movies.title: Blue Film
movies.description: When fetish camboy Aaron Eagle (Kieron Moore) visits a client in exchange for $50,000, he discovers a masked man (Reed Birney) with a camera and a series of increasingly probing questions. But when the man reveals a disturbing connection to Aaron’s past, the two drop their personas and gradually reveal their true desires in this seductive thriller. Described by IndieWire as “independent cinema at its most provocative,” Elliot Tuttle’s debut feature goes where few films dare to, posing as many questions as it answers in a tightly performed chamber drama.

movies.title: Blue Heron
movies.description: In the late 1990s, eight-year-old Sasha and her Hungarian immigrant family relocate to a new home on Vancouver Island, but their fresh start is interrupted by increasingly dangerous behavior from the eldest son, Jeremy. At wit’s end, their parents are presented with a shattering choice. Award-winning director Sophy Romvari’s semi-autobiographical debut feature is a lyrical, profound testament to the things we carry with us, masterfully chronicling the haze of a languid summer and the clarity of the moments that defined it. Q&A with director Sophy Romvari following the 4/21, 7pm screening

movies.title: Body And Soul
movies.description: Pioneering African American filmmaker Oscar Micheaux's Body and Soul , produced outside of the Hollywood system, follows an escaped convict seeking refuge by attempting to pass himself off as a reverend in a small Georgia town. In a magnetic film debut, Paul Robeson portrays two roles, the Reverend and his estranged identical twin brother. Juxtaposing the devious faux religious man against a kind young brother, Robeson’s masterful screen turn marked the beginning of what would become a legendary career in film, stage, and music.

movies.title: Bouchra
movies.description:
Q&A with filmmakers and artists Orian Barki, Meriem Bennani, John Michael Boling, and Jason Coombs on June 26th
, June 27th, and June 28th. Introduction on July 2nd.

movies.title: Bouchra
movies.description: Deeply felt, surprisingly sexy, and formally adventurous, the feature debut from acclaimed visual artists Meriem Bennani and Orian Barki (best known together from their 2020 web series 2 Lizards ) forges new ground that “will make it a classic of queer cinema for years to come” ( Next Best Picture ). With a lived-in granularity and unmistakable visual style, Bouchra is a singular portrait effortlessly toeing the line between documentary, visual art, and resonant family drama. Wrestling with writer’s block for her first film, Bouchra, a queer Moroccan jackal living in NYC starts having difficult yet overdue phone calls with her mother in Casablanca. Balancing the precarity of working as an artist in the city, the rift in her identity between her two homes, and an array of friendships and romantic interests, Bouchra’s emotional reckoning with her mother and herself becomes her path to expression.

movies.title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
movies.description: Coppola at his most boldly baroque, Gary Oldman wearing cinema’s most iconic updo, a puppyish young Keanu Reeves trying to make his way back to Winona Ryder, and Anthony Hopkins as vampire hunter Abraham Van Helsing—it’s all here in this opulent…

movies.title: Bride of the Earth
movies.description: Güney, a stubbornly individualistic, rabble-rousing talent whose cinema stirred together Kurdish/Turkish folklore and aspects of the Western into a potent and highly politicized compound, took on the lead role in this lyrical yet naturalistic…

movies.title: Calle Málaga
movies.description: Maria Angeles, a 79 year-old Spanish woman, lives alone in Tangier, Morocco enjoying her daily routine. But her life is turned upside down when her daughter arrives from Madrid to sell the apartment she has always called home. Determined to stay, she does everything she can to get her apartment and belongings back and, unexpectedly, rediscovers love and sensuality along the way.

movies.title: Candyman
movies.description: This quintessential ‘90s fixture of contemporary horror follows a Chicago graduate student who, in the midst of studying urban folklore, accidentally summons a hook-handed ghost who appears whenever his name is chanted 5 times in front of the mirror. While the film’s campy horror thrills inspired a bevy of sequels, the original displays a heftier moral timbre: exploring the legacy of slavery in the US through the lingering story of the Candyman’s initial demise.

movies.title: Caribbean Film Series
movies.description: Programmed by Third Horizon and The Luminal Theater Our biannual series, produced in partnership with The Luminal Theater and Third Horizon, returns for a weekend of diverse original cinema created by the brightest Caribbean filmmakers. The winter lineup features new work by artists from across the Caribbean and throughout the diaspora, including local creators.

movies.title: CARRIE (1976)
movies.description: Sissy Spacek makes Carrie a truly frail creature whose wide eyes are so much like a cat caught in the light that you’d rather keep your distance to avoid the scratch. Enduring the humiliation that is the true stuff of teenage girl nightmares – public shame for getting your period – Carrie is constantly on the receiving end of her classmates’ pranks. At home, she is taunted with religious nonsense and talk of dirty pillows, so what’s a girl to do but transfer all that rage into telekinetic powers? Building to the end that everyone knows even if you haven’t seen the movie (has someone out there really not seen it?), CARRIE is so effectively terrifying, repeat viewings won’t numb you to it.

movies.title: Center Stage
movies.cast: Maggie Cheung, Han Chin, Carina Lau, Tony Leung Ka-fai In Cantonese, Mandarin, and English

movies.title: Change Of Life
movies.description: Co-written by Reis, Rocha’s Change of Life represents another node in the evolution of the former’s docudrama style. When Adelino returns from service in the Angolan War of Independence, he finds the woman he loves married to his brother. He skips town to find work in rural Portugal, only to find himself thrust into a surprising romance that challenges him to change his life. Though more formally traditional than his later work, Reis’ collaboration with Rocha maintains one of the key facets of his entire oeuvre: a deep commitment to portraying the complex humanity of his subjects.

movies.title: Changing Lanes (2002)
movies.description: Ostensibly a movie about road markings, British theater director Roger Michell's second major motion picture (after 1999's Notting Hill ) turns into a high-stakes class-conflict-ridden drama about egoism, corruption, and the New York City family court system. A stacked cast — Ben Affleck, Samuel L. Jackson, Sidney Pollack, Toni Collette — and composer David Arnold's tense score propel this underrated gem to unexpected heights of craft and societal insight. –CB Part of Changing Changing Lanes Lanes. Presented in partnership with Ridgewood Rides .

movies.title: Changing Lanes (2025)
movies.description: After a beloved teacher is killed in a hit-and-run on McGuinness Boulevard, Greenpoint neighbors launch a grassroots campaign to transform the notorious four-lane boulevard into a safer two-lane street with a protected bike lane. The film demonstrates how grassroots activism and community advocacy can be powerful tools for street safety, even in the face of fierce opposition. A sharp look at who our streets are really built for and a rousing case for democracy at the street level. The screening will be followed by a panel discussion featuring Kevin LaCherra of Make McGuinness Safe , Zach Wyche of NYC DOT , and Samantha Kattan , candidate for Assembly District 37 .
