Part of Changing Changing Lanes Lanes. Presented in partnership with Ridgewood Rides .

movies.title: Chasing Butterflies
movies.description: In the French countryside, in a chateau that’s arrived at a state of genteel decay, two eccentric old women live, as they have for years, practicing the nearly forgotten rituals of the prewar haute bourgeoisie, surrounded by beautiful, dusty relics of a…

movies.title: Chungking Express
movies.description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’…

movies.title: Cinema Ephemera
movies.description: Join us for The Human Machine, the first installment of a new film series presented by Cinema Ephemera. Rich Remsberg and Shawn Rosenheim have curated an evening of ephemeral films: vintage classroom instruction, industrial animations, forgotten children’s TV shows, declassified military training films, religious movies, scraps of stock footage, and a bunch of weird science stuff. “These are films that were not necessarily meant to last beyond their original showings,” said Remsberg. “They weren’t even necessarily meant to be considered films.” “This is an accidental chronicle of 20th century America,” adds Rosenheim, speaking of their collection culled from government archives, flea markets, dumpsters, and the basements of old hoarders. “This is a world both very familiar and very strange.” Travel with us through the old, weird America. From 1920s personal hygiene guides to NASA’s zero-gravity experiments to amateur disco exhibitions, this is a celebration of the ordinary and the forgotten. Some of it is funny. Some is disturbing. Much of it is unbelievably beautiful – a revelation of our world in all its poverty and extravagance. “Breaking open the original context of these films allows us to see the gems among the pot shards,” said Remsberg. “You’ll never look at the 20th Century in the same way again.”

movies.title: Cinema Paradiso
movies.description: Often credited with reviving Italy’s film industry in the late 1980s, this Oscar-winning film tells the story of a mischievous and precocious boy, Totò, who falls in love with the movies, spending every spare moment hanging around the titular theater in his small Sicilian town. When the cinema is rebuilt after a devastating fire that leaves the projectionist, Totò’s mentor, permanently blind, Totò, still a child, is tapped to run the reels, and a cinematic life suddenly unfurls before him.

movies.title: Cinema Tropical At 25: Nostalgia For The Light
movies.description: In his stirring 2010 visual essay, Chilean master documentarian Patricio Guzmán turns to the remote, high-altitude Atacama Desert to craft a meditation on memory, history, and eternity. Beneath some of the clearest skies on Earth, astronomers gather to study the origins of the universe. Yet the desert also preserves traces of the past—from pre-Columbian mummies to the remains of political prisoners disappeared after Chile’s 1973 military coup. In this otherworldly landscape, earthly and celestial quests converge: archaeologists uncover ancient civilizations, women search for their missing loved ones, and astronomers scan the heavens for distant galaxies. Nostalgia for the Light opens Guzmán’s celebrated trilogy exploring landscape, memory, and Chile’s unresolved past. Cinema Tropical continues the celebration of its 25th anniversary with landmark Latin American films of the new millennium.

movies.title: Cinema Tropical At 25: Silvia Prieto
movies.description: On her 27th birthday, Silvia Prieto decides to change her life only to spiral into an identity crisis when she discovers other women share her name. Buoyed by quick wit and a pop-infused eye for consumer culture, Silvia embarks on a wry, screwball-inspired quest for self-definition. This hilariously absurd deadpan comedy, written and directed by Latin American cinema trailblazer Martín Rejtman, became a landmark of New Argentine Cinema, inspiring a wave of filmmakers with its signature minimalism. To celebrate Cinema Tropical’s 25th anniversary, Silvia Prieto —the very first film screened by the organization—returns to New York, this time in dazzling 4K.

movies.title: Claire's Knee
movies.description: Shot in the environs of Lake Annecy, Claire’s Knee—the fifth entry in Rohmer’s series of Six Moral Tales—concerns a cultured, soon-to-be-wed diplomat (Jean-Claude Brialy) who develops a consuming obsession with the knee of an acquaintance’s…

movies.title: CLOWNSPIRACY
movies.description: A small town high school misfit investigates the appearance of creepy clowns before an upcoming election, discovering the clowns are more than they appear. Tickets:https://www.eventbrite.com/e/clownspiracy-tickets-1990612090348?aff=oddtdtcreator

movies.title: Collateral
movies.description: Los Angeles cabbie Max Durocher (Jamie Foxx) is in for the toughest fare of his working life when he picks up one Vincent (Tom Cruise, natty in charcoal gray sharkskin suit), a jazz enthusiast and professional hitman who quite firmly insists that his…

movies.title: Coming Home
movies.description: One of the most compelling pictures ever made about the shattering aftermath of the Vietnam War, Coming Home earned eight Academy Award nominations and won three for Best Actress (Jane Fonda), Actor (Jon Voight) and Original Screenplay. Coming Home is a heartrending and unforgettable examination of a critical period in our nation's history and an uncompromising, extraordinarily moving film directed by the great Hal Ashby ( The Last Detail ). When Marine Captain Bob Hyde (Dern) leaves for Vietnam, his wife Sally (Fonda) volunteers at a local hospital. There she meets Luke Martin (Voight), a former sergeant whose war injury has left him a paraplegic. Embittered with rage and filled with frustration, Luke finds new hope and confidence through his growing intimacy with Sally. The relationship transforms Sally's feelings about life, love, and the horrors of war. And when, wounded and disillusioned, Sally's husband returns home, all three must grapple with the full impact of a brutal distant war that has changed their lives forever.

movies.title: Coming To America
movies.description: Coming to America casts comedian Eddie Murphy as pampered African prince Akeem, who rebels against an arranged marriage and heads to America to find a new bride. Murphy's regal father (Jones) allows the prince 40 days to roam the US, sending along faithful retainer Semmi (Hall) to make sure nothing untoward happens. To avoid fortune hunters, they conceal their true identity and pass as poor foreign students working at McDowell's. Akeem finds a perfect match in the boss’s daughter, Lisa (who makes a memorable dash through the rain into the subway - with Hoyt-Schermerhorn doubling for Sutphin in Queens). Murphy and Hall play multiple roles, and innumerable celebrity cameos are peppered throughout the proceedings—including the Duke Brothers from Murphy’s 1983 hit, Trading Places .

movies.title: Conversation Piece
movies.description: Introduction by David Campany, Creative Director, International Center of Photography on Friday, August 7th

movies.title: Cotton Queen
movies.description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonizers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the center of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields—and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

movies.title: Cotton Queen
movies.description: New York Premiere In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonizers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the center of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields—and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again. Followed by a Q&A with director Suzannah Mirghani, actor Rodney Sharkey, and musician Alsarah—moderated by Sarra Idris

movies.title: Crocodile Dundee Ii
movies.description: Yes, we really are screening a 35mm print of Crocodile Dundee II . Mick Dundee’s (Hogan) return to the screen sets up another slew of fish-out-of-water antics in the big city. Rehashing a lot of what made the first film pop—for better or worse—Dundee’s return serves as a surprising love letter to New York City, and features a pretty iconic set piece in the Hoyt-Schermerhorn station.

movies.title: Cuba & Haiti
movies.description: Three short films explore the interconnections of Cuba and Haiti in the larger narrative of the Black Caribbean. De bateyes (1971) Dir. Sara Gómez 24min, DCP Foregrounding Haitians and Afro-Cubans, this short documentary on the titular sugar mills of Cuba looks at the everyday life of its workers in a cinematic history of agriculture, labor and class struggle. Reshipment / Reembarque (2014) Dir. Gloria Rolando 58min In the early 20th century, Haitians crossed the Gulf of Gonaives to work as laborers in the cane fields. When the sugar market crashed, many were forcibly returned to Haiti. Here, the voices of prominent historians join the memories of Haitians and their descendants in Cuba to understand a complex economic chapter. Simparele (1974) Dir. Humberto Solás 30min Humberto Solas reconstructs Haitian history through music, dance, visual art, and documentary footage.

movies.title: CULT CINEMA
movies.description: Film Noir Cinema presents “CULT CINEMA”: a night of sheer cinematic madness dedicated to the most obscure films ever made.

movies.title: Dakan
movies.description: Touted as the first queer love story from West Africa, this poignant, unapologetic drama endures beyond the controversy and celebration it received upon its premiere at the 1997 Cannes Film Festival. Sory (Aboucar Touré) and Manga (Mamady Mory Camara) feel an irrepressible romantic connection they cannot deny. But after the young men share their authentic feelings with their parents, they are separated and sent in different directions. Sory begins to work in his father’s business, while Manga must spend a year with a traditional healer in the backcountry—and both are firmly encouraged to settle down with women. As Sory and Manga attempt to meet social conventions, it gradually becomes clear that their personal journeys are more parallel than divergent. A rarely screened milestone in queer cinema, Mohamed Camara’s Dakan (Destiny) is a powerful call to listen to—and trust in—one’s heart.

movies.title: Daughters Of The Dust
movies.description: At the dawn of the 20th century, a multi-generational family in the Gullah community on the Sea Islands off South Carolina struggles to maintain their cultural heritage while contemplating a migration to the mainland. The first wide release by a Black female filmmaker, the film was met with wild critical acclaim and rapturous audience response when it initially opened in 1991 and still resonates today, influencing generations of young filmmakers.

movies.title: Daughters Of The Dust
movies.description: At the dawn of the 20th century, a multi-generational family in the Gullah community on the Sea Islands off South Carolina struggles to maintain their cultural heritage while contemplating a migration to the mainland. The first wide release by a Black female filmmaker, the film was met with wild critical acclaim and rapturous audience response when it initially opened in 1991 and still resonates today, influencing generations of young filmmakers. Series programmer Ashley Clark will introduce the screening and sign his new book, The World of Black Film .

movies.title: Days and Nights in the Forest
movies.description: Leaving crowded Calcutta behind for a few days of rustication in the Palamau woods—while bringing the deeply ingrained prejudices of their castes and their sex along as baggage—four middle-class young men hope that their holiday will provide the…

movies.title: De Cierta Manera (One Way Or Another)
movies.description: This vivid portrait of the post-revolutionary era explores the relationship between middle-class schoolteacher Yolanda and factory worker Mario, tracing how her latent class bias and his ingrained machismo manifest. In her only full-length feature, Gómez moves fluidly between inter-personal conflict, collective life and documentary footage deliver a sharp, intersectional perspective on the process–rather than the event–of social, economic and political transformation, reckoning with racialized poverty, gendered exclusion, and dedication to the revolutionary horizon.

movies.title: De Palma
movies.description: In the annals of Hollywood film since the artistic glories of the New Hollywood era, few have a better reputation and body of work in the field of the suspense film exploring the contemporary darkness in American life than Brian De Palma. Here, the great film writer and director takes us through his professional life in his own words of a career that would redefine film horror and suspense. All the while, he also confesses the challenges of working in Hollywood and the price that even great artists pay for being a part of it.

movies.title: Deliverance
movies.description: A quartet of city slicker businessman buddies (Jon Voight, Ned Beatty, Ronny Cox and, in a star-making role, Burt Reynolds) leave Atlanta to head into the Georgia backwoods for what’s meant to be a little weekend canoe trip… and stumble headlong…

movies.title: Demon Pond
movies.description: New 4K Restoration “ Demon Pond is a haunting fantasy drama set in a remote village where a mysterious bell-ringing ritual is believed to prevent a dragon goddess from unleashing a devastating flood. When a traveling schoolteacher becomes involved with the villagers, the boundary between myth and reality begins to blur. Adapted from a play by Izumi Kyōka, the film blends folklore, theatrical stylization, and lush cinematography into a dreamlike experience. Featuring a mesmerizing performance by renowned onnagata actor Tamasaburō Bandō, the film stands as a unique fusion of cinema and traditional Japanese theater.” - Shun Inoue

movies.title: DENCHU-KOZO
movies.description: Hikari is a boy who is bullied and teased by the other boys at school because he has the odd distinction of having an electricity pole growing out of his back. However, one of his classmates, a girl named Momo, comes to his rescue.

movies.title: Der Fan
movies.description: Teen runaway Simone (Désirée Nosbusch, entrancingly opaque) loves the Neue Deutsche Welle pop singer known only as “R” (Bodo Staiger)… loves him so much, in fact, that she could just about eat him alive. And when she finally meets her idol—only…

movies.title: Desert Hearts
movies.description: Donna Deitch’s classic of lesbian cinema is one of the greatest love stories of all time. The year is 1959, and Professor Vivian Bell (Helen Shaver) has arrived in Reno, NV, for a divorce. There she meets Cay Rivvers (Patricia Charbonneau), a backwards-driving, jean short-wearing sculptor/casino employee who is brazenly herself. These two opposing forces circle around each other, falling in lust and love, as Cay dares Vivian to take a risk for something more. Now, four decades since its theatrical release in 1986, join us in celebrating a film that was ahead of its time and beyond time. From an overwhelming kiss in the rain to one of the best sex scenes ever put on film, Desert Hearts redefined what queer women could expect from our movies. The romance crackles with possibility, but its love story goes beyond this central pair—it’s also about the bonds of friendship, the challenge of family, and the importance of embracing the entirety of oneself.

movies.title: Disclosure Day
movies.description: If you found out we weren’t alone, if someone showed you, proved it to you, would that frighten you? This summer, the truth belongs to eight billion people. Spielberg’s latest sci-fi movie event, his first film since 2022’s The Fabelmans , returns to a legacy of grand, other-worldly, mysterious spectacle. Starring Emily Blunt ( Oppenheimer ), Josh O’Connor ( Challengers ), and Colin Firth ( The King’s Speech ), Disclosure Day thrills in the tense moment when the unknown becomes known.

movies.title: Do You Love Me
movies.description: Select introductions by guests including ArteEast's Sylvia Feghali and Céline Semaan, Slow Factory CEO and host of Everything is Political, on July 10th, 11th, and 12th

movies.title: Do You Love Me
movies.description: A love letter to Beirut, this playful and personal journey through Lebanon’s audiovisual memory spans 70 years of film, TV, home videos, and photography exploring the Lebanese collective psyche—marked by joy and intimacy, destruction and loss. Through the eyes of citizens, filmmakers, and artists, the film reconstructs a fragmented history in a country without a national archive, celebrating creative expression as both resistance, renewal, and a way to preserve memory. Do You Love Me had its New York Premiere at New Directors/New Films 2026, and its world premiere at Venice Days.

movies.title: Double Suicide
movies.description: One of former theater student Shinoda’s towering masterpieces, this hyper stylized tragedy adapts a 1721 play by the legendary Japanese dramatist Chikamatsu Monzaemon. Originally written for the bunraku (puppet theater) tradition, Shinoda’s film uses human actors—but also integrates the black-clad puppeteers of bunraku. Following the travails of an Osaka merchant and his courtesan lover, Shinoda’s film is simultaneously indebted to tradition and bracingly modern. With a score by avant garde composer Toru Takemitsu and equally stylized sets and costumes, the film stands amongst the most daring statements of the Japanese New Wave.

movies.title: Double Take
movies.description: Magic and cinema both revolve around illusion. Sleights of hand and deliberate techniques invite audiences to look again, squinting intently in a practice of truth-seeking. Double Take is composed of two experimental films by women exercising repetition as a cinematic conceit, emphasizing all that can be discovered (and undone) with an echo. Deux fois (1968) Dir. Jackie Raynal 63 min, digital. With Jackie Raynal, Francisco Viader With Deux fois , the dexterous film editor Jackie Raynal made her directorial debut as part of the radical film collective Zanzibar Group. Filmed entirely during a nine-day trip to Barcelona, Deux fois orbits around Raynal herself: she breaks the frame, decorum, and rules of temporality in an experimental work that begins as a story and ends as a manifesto. Chronicles of a Lying Spirit (By Kelly Gabron) (1992) Dir. Cauleen Smith 2 min, digital The interdisciplinary artist Cauleen Smith challenges the dominant terms of representation and authorship, interrogating the place of Black people across histories of media. In Chronicles of a Lying Spirit , Smith superimposes voice, image, and text into a play of photographic fragments and dueling narrators that dances at the margins of biography, myth, and mediatized fact.

movies.title: Dr. Strangelove
movies.description: A thrilling (and gut-busting) examination of the height of Cold War tension, Kubrick’s 1964 comedy chronicles the story of a mentally unstable American general’s sudden order of a nuclear attack on the Soviet Union. Peter Sellers, in particularly magnetic form, portrays three characters in this equally funny and disturbing romp through one of America’s most tumultuous periods. From black comedy at the end of the world to characters named Buck Turgidson and Jack D. Ripper, there’s more than a little Pynchon DNA in Kubrick’s classic.

movies.title: Drunken Master II
movies.description: Sixteen years after starring in Yuen Woo-ping’s Drunken Master, the film that cemented its star’s place as the clown prince of martial arts cinema, Jackie Chan returned to the role of bibulous warrior Wong Fei-hung (aka “Freddie Wong”) with Lau in…

movies.title: Dry Lake (Aka Youth In Fury)
movies.description: 35mm print imported from Japan (courtesy of the Japan Foundation) Released amid protests against the 1960 United States–Japan Security Treaty (which culminated in hundreds of thousands surrounding the Japanese National Diet building), Shinoda’s study of a young student radical marks an early blast of the Japanese New Wave’s youth energy. With a screenplay by leftist firebrand poet, theater director, and later filmmaker Shuiji Terayama, the film’s anticapitalist and anti-imperialist depiction of postwar Japan shows the alienation that fueled the protests—and made some consider more violent action.

movies.title: Duck Soup
movies.description: In this classic from the Marx Brothers, Groucho plays Rufus T. Firefly, newly-named dictator of bankrupt (and fictional) Freedonia. Relations with Sylvania begin to deteriorate, in part due to the antics of the nation’s two inept spies, portrayed by Chico and Harpo, sending the two nations on a path towards war. The Marx Brothers—and their equally whimsical and deadpan slapstick—were a tangible inspiration on Pynchon, often referenced in his novels.

movies.title: Dumplings
movies.description: Expanding his segment of the same name in the horror anthology film Three… Extremes, Chan’s Dumplings tells the deliciously deviant tale of ex-soap star Mrs. Li (Miriam Yeung) who, her looks fading and husband Tony Leung Ka-fai’s eye wandering,…

movies.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
movies.description: A world-conquering pop culture phenomenon on its original release, today it’s easier to see Spielberg’s boy-and-his-alien fable as the movie it always was—modest and familiar in its domestic setting, supremely sensitive to all the fun and the fear…

movies.title: El Juego De La Vida: A Special Benefit Screening For Colombia
movies.cast: Mildred Leal, Donny Juan Pablo Lozano Leal, Anyi Paola Rodriguez, Leydy Daniela Cruz, Inés María Álvarez, Carlos García.
movies.description:
EL JUEGO DE LA VIDA:  A Special Benefit Screening for Colombia

For 14 years, a filmmaker follows five Colombian families striving to move forward in a country where social mobility does not guarantee opportunity. Through inequality, setbacks, and small victories, their stories show how origins can shape, but not define, destiny. El Jugo de la Vida is an intimate portrait of struggle, dignity, and hope in Colombia.

movies.title: El Sett
movies.description: Dubbed “Egypt’s fourth pyramid,” Umm Kalthum was one of the most globally adored singers of the 20th century, and Egypt’s leading musical voice. In this sprawling biopic, Hamed centers Kalthum’s final sickness-plagued performance as a venue for a trip down memory lane, exploring her humble beginnings and the ensuing seven decades of triumph, failure, love, and all that informed one of the most enduring careers in the history of contemporary music.

movies.title: El Topo
movies.description: Chilean-born mime-turned-filmmaker Jodorowsky plays the title role in this acid Western staple of the midnight movies, strapping on the six-shooter as a lone gunfighter—his name means “The Mole” in Spanish—traveling across a psychedelic desert…

movies.title: Electronica
movies.description: Foot-tapping, heart-pounding soundtracks anchor this series, an amalgam of films from across the globe boasting electronic-heavy soundtracks. Revel in the ecstatic techno of Run Lola Run , the gritty industrial cacophony of Fight Club , or the ‘80s synth-pop muzak of Decoder . This collection of Y2K and Cyberpunk films overflowing with dance-club debauchery and the criminal underground will surely get your heart—and mind—racing.

movies.title: Ellos Son, Los Violadores
movies.description: This documentary follows Los Violadores, Argentina’s first punk band and a pioneering force in the development of Spanish-language punk music. Rebellious, marginal, defiant, and innovative, the ‘80s group carved out a space and a place for themselves in dark years of repression and censorship, with furious melodies and lyrics steeped in social commentary.

movies.title: Erupcja
movies.description: When Bethany (Charli xcx) and her soon-to-be fiancé (Will Madden) are unexpectedly stranded in Warsaw, Poland in the wake of a volcanic eruption, the former takes the explosive event as a sign to ditch her baggage, reunite with childhood friend Nel (Lena Góra), and traipse across lofts, clubs, and back alleys, all the while becoming entangled in an emotional web that challenges her sense of self. American maverick Pete Ohs ( Everything Beautiful Is Far Away ) directed, edited, photographed, and produced this dizzyingly charming European postcard, an anti-romantic comedy about the pains and pleasures of being in love. Join us for a Q&A following the May 6, 7:10pm screening with Pete Ohs and Jeremy O. Harris, moderated by Nia Dacosta

movies.title: Eve's Bayou
movies.description: One of the essential works of the 1990s and recently selected for the Library of Congress’ National Film Registry, Eve’s Bayou is a film of rich, steamy sexuality and an incredible sense of place, that follows the loss of innocence that occurs when…

movies.title: Everything Seemed Possible + Short Films Of The Puerto Rican Film Unit
movies.description: In the midst of the Cold War, Puerto Rico was rapidly industrializing and aligning itself with U.S. interests. Seeking to shape the narrative of a modernizing country, the government sent a group of artists into rural communities to make films about the country’s new direction. But what emerged was something far more unexpected. In close collaboration with residents, these artists created dozens of films that gained international recognition—works that powerfully questioned the official story of progress. In Everything Seemed Possible , filmmaker Ramón Rivera Moret weaves the stories of these remarkable films with the memories of his family, crafting an intimate portrait of the filmmakers, their collaborations, and a moment in Puerto Rico marked by profound political and social transformation and the desire to imagine the country anew. The feature will be accompanied by three original films from Puerto Rico’s Division of Community Education: La manos del hombre , Una voz en la montaña and Modesta .

movies.title: Eve’S Bayou
movies.description: Kasi Lemmons made a splash with one of the most distinctive directorial debuts of the 1990s, a richly atmospheric, Southern Gothic stew of sex, lies, and voodoo in which a young girl witnesses secrets and deceptions tearing her wealthy Louisiana family apart. A primordial American blend of Creole folklore, magic, and mysticism, Eve’s Bayou provides a scintillating showcase for a powerhouse ensemble of Black actresses.

movies.title: Exit 8
movies.description: A man trapped in an endless, sterile subway passageway sets out to find Exit 8. The rules of his quest are simple: do not overlook anything out of the ordinary. If you discover an anomaly, turn back immediately. If you don’t, carry on. Then leave from Exit 8. Even a single oversight will send him back to the beginning. A rare video game adaptation that faithfully captures the feel of its critically-acclaimed source material, Kawamura’s eerie psychological thriller thrusts its audience into the tension of its protagonist, posing questions about guilt and redemption along the way. Director Genki Kawamura will join us for a Q&A on Friday, 4/10 at 8pm

movies.title: F For Fake
movies.description: Forgery. Fraud. Magic. In F for Fake , a free-form sort-of documentary by Orson Welles, the legendary filmmaker and self-described charlatan gleefully reengages with the central preoccupation of his career: the tenuous lines between illusion and truth, art and lies. Beginning with portraits of the world-renowned art forger Elmyr de Hory and his equally devious biographer, Clifford Irving, Welles embarks on a dizzying journey that simultaneously exposes and revels in fakery and fakers of all stripes—not the least of whom is Welles himself. Charming and inventive, F for Fake is an inspired prank and a clever examination of the essential duplicity of cinema. An inventive practitioner of cinematic magic, Welles was also a lifelong devotee of magic’s more traditional form. F for Fake will be preceded by a half-hour program in which Welles takes the stage as a magician.

movies.title: F.T.A.
movies.description: “The Show the Pentagon Couldn’t Stop!” At the height of the Vietnam War, Jane Fonda and Donald Sutherland toured an anti-war comedy show across Southeast Asia, directly engaged with and inspired by veterans against the war. Naturally, the highly controversial tour upset U.S. military higher-ups despite its positive reception among stationed soldiers. Francine Parker’s film version was quickly taken out of circulation due to political pressures, and has been difficult to access for decades. New 4K restoration by IndieCollect, created in association with Academy Film Archive with funding from the Golden Globe Foundation.

movies.title: Fallen Angels
movies.description: Part hard-boiled crime thriller and part soft, featherweight giddiness, Fallen Angels was first conceived as a segment of Wong’s Chungking Express, then developed into a darker companion piece to his glistening pop-romantic masterpiece, the story of a…

movies.title: Falling Leaves
movies.description: Iosseliani’s debut feature—winner of the FIPRESCI Award at Cannes—follows newly minted oenologists Nico and Otar, just out of winemaking school, as they head to work at an agricultural cooperative in Tbilisi, there to have their first intimate…

movies.title: Favorites of the Moon
movies.description: Having relocated to France in 1982, Iosseliani wasted no time in showing the world he hadn’t left his singular gifts behind upon leaving Georgia, taking home the Special Jury Prize at the 41st Venice International Film Festival for this puckish…

movies.title: FILM CLUB
movies.description: Film Noir Cinema presents: “FILM CLUB” - an evening with moving image. The films are chosen each time by a different member of the club without anybody but the chooser knowing the title. Pure cinematheque fun.

movies.title: Film Comment Live: Play Me Something
movies.description: In 1989, John Berger collaborated with Scottish director Timothy Neat to make a film out of “Play Me Something,” his short story first published in The Three Penny Review in 1985, and later included as the final chapter of Berger’s short-story collection, Once in Europa (1987). Set in a small airport on the Scottish island of Barra, where planes land on a tidal beach, Play Me Something draws on Celtic oral tradition and European modernism to tell the beguiling story of a storyteller: a mysterious raconteur played by Berger in a bowler hat. He appears as a motley band of passengers waits for a delayed plane and begins to narrate his tale of an Italian farmer and an urbane young woman who meet at a Communist festival on the Venetian island of Giudecca. As Berger recounts the story, we see it unfold in bits of 16mm color and black-and-white footage, scenes on a television, and still photographs by Jean Mohr. The gaps are filled in by the audience of enraptured passengers—including a young Tilda Swinton and Scottish philosopher Hamish Henderson—so that the nonplace of the airport becomes a site of collective conjuring. Part of Hold Everything Dear—John Berger and Cinema , a multi-venue Film Comment series celebrating Berger’s centennial.

movies.title: FILM NOIR MONDAY
movies.description: Film Noir Mondays are dedicated to bring to light lesser known as well as very obscure films that fit Film Noir cinema, including international titles. In Noir fashion the movie titles are not revealed beforehand, keeping the audience in total darkness. . .

movies.title: Finding Emily
movies.cast: Angourie Rice, Spike Fearn, Minnie Driver
movies.description: When a lovesick musician is given the wrong number for his dream girl, he teams up with a driven psychology student to find her. Together, they spark a hilarious campus-wide frenzy that tests their own hearts and ambitions along the way.

movies.title: First Blood
movies.description: The movie whose runaway success singlehandedly landed Carolco in the ranks of legit Tinseltown players, Kotcheff’s taut adaptation of David Morrell’s 1972 novel of the same name introduces Sylvester Stallone as burnt-out Vietnam vet John Rambo, in the…

movies.title: For Sama
movies.description: Named for her daughter, For Sama depicts Waad al-Kateab’s life through five years in Aleppo. The journey takes her from economics student to her marriage to Hamza al-Kateab (later a doctor at one of Aleppo’s few remaining hospitals) and finally the birth of her daughter, all told against the backdrop of the Battle of Aleppo and succeeding conflict as it engulfs the city. She and her husband are ultimately faced with the decision to flee the city or selflessly stay in service of the war’s innocent victims.

movies.title: Four Adventures of Reinette and Mirabelle
movies.description: Shot quickly in and around Paris during a production break on Rohmer’s Le Rayon Vert, this breezy, witty film traces the exploits of two young women—one an ethnology student from the city, the other an unsophisticated aspiring artist from the country.…

movies.title: Freaks
movies.description: The cinematic equivalent of listening to one of the field recordings made by folk historians in the early 20th century, this profoundly troubling, mysterious, and uncanny film follows a devious trapeze artist intent on murdering a dwarf in a carnival troupe to gain his inheritance. She soon finds that these performers live a lifestyle characterized by their communal bonds, and sees the full limits of what they’re capable of when one of their own is threatened. Composed of a cast of the era’s stars alongside actual sideshow performers, Browning’s viscerally striking thriller was initially met with shock upon its release, but has been re-appraised in recent years as a force—equally haunting and serving as an early plea for a more nuanced understanding of an ostracized community.

movies.title: Freedom Way
movies.description: Freedom Way (2024) Dir. Afolabi Olalekan With Jesse Suntele, Ogranya Jable 83min; DCP Nigeria In English and Yoruba with English subtitles Software developers Themba (Jesse Suntele) and Tayo (Ogranya Jable) finally realize their long-awaited venture, Easy Go, a rideshare app connecting motorcyclists with customers across Lagos, Nigeria. The excitement of the launch quickly gives way to mounting pressure as they confront restrictive government laws, shifting regulations, and the threat of police brutality. On the periphery, the lives of nine individuals begin to collide in Afolabi Olalekan’s feature debut, a fast-paced, electric thriller shot on location in Lagos. Preceded by Ifeyinwa (2025) Dir. Jay Ikechukwu Okoroafo 13min; DCP US New York Premiere Ifeyinwa is a short film weaving director Jay Ikechukwu Okoroafo’s mother's life and migration from Enugu, Nigeria to Houston using personal family photographs, VHS footage, interviews, and sound, as told by her. The work explores the relationship between encounter, memory, and activation.

movies.title: Frontline Pbs Presents: 2000 Meters To Andriivka
movies.description: Created by FRONTLINE PBS in collaboration with the Associated Press, 2000 Meters to Andriivka offers a rare, unfiltered view of modern warfare through combat bodycam footage and intimate moments of reflection. Following a Ukrainian platoon on a high-stakes mission to liberate the village of Andriivka, the film documents not only the physical distance of 2,000 meters, but also the embedded emotional and human cost. At once visceral and deeply human, 2000 Meters to Andriivka is a stunning portrayal of war in the trenches from the Oscar-winning team behind 20 Days in Mariupol . The film is a winner of the Sundance Film Festival’s World Cinema Documentary Directing Award, the Directors Guild of America Award for Outstanding Directorial Achievement in Documentary, the Writers Guild of America Award for Best Documentary Screenplay, and the American Society of Cinematographers Award, and has been nominated for Emmy and Peabody Awards. Join us for a post-screening conversation with special guests connected to the film. Created by BAM and FRONTLINE PBS Impact teams, this program is rooted in a shared mission to spark dialogue, deepen cultural understanding, and engage audiences around meaningful social issues.

movies.title: Gabbeh
movies.description: Mohsen Makhmalbaf journeyed to Iran’s remote steppes to film a vanishing nomadic tribe, but, enchanted by the landscape and the stories woven into their gabbeh carpets, his documentary evolved into a lyrical folktale. On a riverbank, an elderly couple washes their gabbeh . From its woven threads emerges a beautiful young woman—Gabbeh herself—who tells her story: She loves a mysterious horseman who trails her nomadic clan across the mountains. Though her father has blessed their union, seasons pass and the rider only circles closer, never arriving. This tender romance is interlaced with the lives of the nomads, whose days are shaped by nature’s rhythms and the brilliantly-hued carpets that hold their histories.

movies.title: Gaza Fights For Freedom
movies.description: In this gut-wrenching depiction of Gaza’s protest movement, Abby Martin paints a portrait of a people determined to return to their historic homeland. This film features a plethora of interviews with Palestinians participating in the Great March of Return, a weekly series of protests that saw tens of thousands march up to the border fence between Gaza and Israel. While hundreds were killed and thousands were injured, these protests continued unabated for months. Amid tragedy, Martin encounters immense hope and steadfastness, proving that a people can only remain oppressed for so long.

movies.title: Germaine Acogny - The Essence Of Dance
movies.description: North American Premiere Germaine Acogny, the "mother of African contemporary dance," is one of Africa’s most influential artists. This documentary traces her journey as a pioneer in blending traditional West African dance with European influences, creating the Acogny Technique, which has shaped contemporary dance worldwide. With over 50 years of performing and teaching, the 80-year-old dance icon received the Golden Lion for Dance at the 2021 Venice Dance Festival for her lifetime achievements. Followed by a Q&A with Ghyslaine de Souza, Germaine Acogny’s daughter, moderated by Tracy Austin

movies.title: Ghost In The Machine
movies.description: Screening followed by a panel discussion with Angela Saini, Jessie Daniels and Mutale Nkonde, moderated by Annie Dorsen. A visceral investigative essay documentary from director Valerie Veatch ( The Zoo , Love Child ), Ghost in the Machine explores how emerging technologies reshape identity, culture, and global power. Based on conversations with 36 leading AI experts (and over 100 hours of conversation), Veatch unearths the buried history of artificial intelligence: one rooted not in neutral algorithms, but in racism, misogyny, eugenics, and entrenched systems of power that shaped the technology long before it entered our daily lives. By revealing the origins and ideologies embedded in AI’s foundations, the film confronts viewers with questions that feel not just timely, but essential.

movies.title: Girl 6
movies.cast: Theresa Randle, Isaiah Washington, Spike Lee, Jenifer Lewis, Debi Mazar, Peter Berg

movies.title: Golden Goal Presents: Offside
movies.description: In Tehran, a girl (Shima Mobarak-Shahi) disguises her gender to elude the regime’s stadium ban against women ahead of a men’s qualifying match for the 2006 World Cup. When she is detained and jailed, she joins a group of riotous women bent on watching their country play. Bored but dutiful soldiers look after the women, and occasionally provide game commentary. Bold Iranian cinema luminary Jafar Panahi ( It Was Just an Accident , No Bears ) was inspired by his own football-loving daughter’s exploits to make Offside , filming at the actual match with two improvised outcomes prepared to anticipate victory or defeat. Golden Goal , an independent literary magazine, explores the politics and allure of the World Cup. Celebrating this year’s series, BAM is thrilled to screen Offside , followed by a discussion with Iranian author Amir Ahmadi Arian and Solmaz Sharif, founder of Shirzanan , the first women’s sports magazine in Iran, moderated by Golden Goal co-editors Miguel Salazar and Alex Shephard.

movies.title: Gonza The Spearman
movies.description: New 4K Restoration “Gonza the Spearman is a tragic period drama based on a classic play by Chikamatsu Monzaemon. The story follows Gonza, a low-ranking samurai whose life unravels after he becomes caught in a forbidden relationship with his lord’s wife. Bound by rigid social codes and ideas of honor, the pair are pushed toward an inevitable tragedy. With elegant cinematography, restrained pacing, and strong influences from traditional bunraku puppet theater, the film creates a tense, emotionally rich atmosphere, anchored by a subtle performance from Ken Ogata.” - Shun Inoue

movies.title: Good Morning
movies.description: Two brothers in a modern Japanese suburb go on strike to bring their parents to their knees and achieve their cherished dream: owning a television set for watching sumo matches. While borrowing from his own classic I Was Born, But… (1932), Ozu turns in…

movies.title: Good Time
movies.description: A relentless, breakneck, candy-colored chase through the heart of Queens and Nassau County, the Safdies’ long, dark night of the soul thriller follows ne’er-do-well punk grifter “Connie” Nikas (Robert Pattinson) as he scrambles to spring brother…

movies.title: Good Time
movies.description: A precursor to Uncut Gems and Marty Supreme , the Safdie Brothers’ heart-pumping style of snowballing, stake-raising antics was solidified with Good Time . After a botched bank robbery lands his younger brother in prison, Constantine "Connie" Nikas (Robert Pattinson) embarks on a twisted odyssey through the city's underworld in an increasingly desperate—and dangerous—attempt to get his brother Nick (Benny Safdie) out of jail. Over the course of one adrenalized night, Connie finds himself on a mad descent into violence and mayhem as he races against the clock to save his brother and himself, knowing their lives hang in the balance.

movies.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
movies.description: The Fu-Ho Grand, a movie palace in Taipei, is closing its doors. Its valedictory screening: King…

movies.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
movies.description: Like the Royal Theater in The Last Picture Show and the movie house in Cinema Paradiso , the Fu-Ho, a run down Taipei movie palace, is shutting down for good, playing its final film to a motley smattering of spectators. Even as the theater's ill-mannered patrons snack noisily, remove their shoes, and generally treat this temple of cinema like their living room, the sense that moviegoing as a communal experience is slipping away takes on a powerful and painful resonance. Yet Tsai Ming-liang’s Goodbye, Dragon Inn is too multifaceted to collapse into a simple valentine to the age of pre-VOD cinephilia. Instead, Ming-liang rises to the narrative challenge, offering a series of sly and delicate character arcs via his signature long, static shots and sparse use of dialogue. Featuring a reading by James Malzone before the screening on February 19

movies.title: Greetings From Out Here
movies.description: Accompanied by her dog Sam and a video camera, filmmaker Ellen Spiro traveled from Virginia to Texas and back exploring openly gay culture in the Deep South. Highlighted by spontaneous encounters with local eccentrics and mechanics (her van breaks down frequently), Greetings from Out Here provides detailed portraits of small-town queer Southerners—from Rita, a retired military officer turned drag queen in New Orleans to Iris, a Black lesbian living in a bus in the Ozarks. Filmed on location at the Texas Gay Rodeo, Mardi Gras, Gay Pride in Atlanta, Dollywood, Miss Miller's Eternal Love and Care Pet Cemetery, and the Short Mountain Radical Faerie sanctuary, Spiro captures the richness, vitality and courage of "out" gay Southern life in the early 1990s.

movies.title: Güeros
movies.description: Ever since the National University strike broke out, Sombra (Huerta) and Santos (Ortizgris) have been living in angst-ridden limbo. Education-less, motionless, purposeless, and unsure of what the strike will bring, they begin to look for strange ways to kill time. But their idiosyncratic routine is interrupted by the unexpected arrival of Tomas (Aguirre), Sombra's kid brother. Unable to fit in amongst these older slackers, Tomas discovers that unsung Mexican folk-rock hero Epigmenio Cruz has been hospitalized somewhere in the city. Tomas convinces Sombra and Santos they must track him down in order to pay their final respects on his deathbed. But what they thought would be a simple trip to find their childhood idol soon becomes a voyage of self-discovery across Mexico City's invisible frontiers.

movies.title: Haifa
movies.description: Haifa, nicknamed after the city he longs for, comes and goes in a Palestinian refugee camp. Although he is seen as the town fool, there are many things that only he knows. He is closely related to the family of Abu Said, a former policeman who has high hopes for the political developments promised by the peace process. Oum Said, his wife, hangs her hope instead on the imminent release of their eldest son, Said, from jail. Their youngest son, Siad, is cynical and rebellious. Sabah, their 12-year-old daughter, sees the future through the eyes of a romantic, searching for what it might hold in store for her.

movies.title: Hamnet
movies.description: In 16th-century England, an impoverished Latin tutor named William Shakespeare (Mescal) meets free-spirited Agnes (Buckley), sparking an affair that leads to marriage and three children. As Will seeks his fortune in the London theater, Agnes anchors the domestic sphere alone. The couple’s bond is tested when tragedy strikes, but their shared experience sets the stage for the creation of Shakespeare’s timeless masterpiece, Hamlet . Academy Award-winning filmmaker Chloé Zhao ( Nomadland , The Rider ) illuminates the complexities of love and the healing power of art and creativity.

movies.title: Hannibal
movies.description: Hopkins reprises his role from 1991’s The Silence of the Lambs as psychiatrist-turned-cannibal serial killer Hannibal Lecter in Scott’s follow-up, a gristly fairy tale that finds FBI special agent Clarice Starling (Julianne Moore, ably taking on the…

movies.title: Happy Birthday
movies.description: Eight-year-old Toha works as a maid for a wealthy family in Cairo, and is set on hosting a successful birthday party for her best friend: her employer’s daughter. She soon discovers the social hierarchy that divides them in this poignant debut reflecting class schisms in contemporary Cairo. Happy Birthday made its world premiere at the 2025 Tribeca Film Festival, where it won Best International Narrative Feature, Best Screenplay in an International Narrative Feature, and the Nora Ephron Award.

movies.title: Happy Hour
movies.description: Four longtime friends in their late thirties living in Kobe, played by Sachie Tanaka, Hazuki Kikuchi, Maiko Mihara, and Rira Kawamura—together recipients of the Best Actress award at the Locarno Film Festival—are thrown into turmoil when one announces…

movies.title: Happy Together
movies.description: Hong Kong cinema superstars Tony Leung and Leslie Cheung play a pair of lovers living out the waning days of their relationship as expatriates in Buenos Aires. Lusty tango bars, the salsa music of the La Boca sidewalks, and a hypnotic visit to the nearby…

movies.title: High School II
movies.description: Frederick Wiseman's long anticipated follow-up to his sophomore feature, High School (1968), saw the bard of verité turn his attention from the Keystone State to New York City, where his subject, Central Park East Secondary School, had been founded just a few years prior to serve the youth of Spanish Harlem according to the principles of the nascent Small Schools Movement. A masterful examination of the clash between the folly of youth and the weight of institutions, High School II gives us a front row seat to hours of PTA meetings, student government assemblies, and messy experiments in multilateral conflict resolution, while also inviting us into the lives of a few dozen young people, who—despite centuries of systemic disadvantage and institutional inertia—manage to keep their dreams alive and their spirits uncrushed. This September, Low Cinema joins Union Docs, the Museum of the Moving Image, Spectacle Theater, and Anthology Film Archives in celebrating Wiseman's chronic obsession with New York City. All related programs can be found on Union Docs' series page . -CB Special thanks to Zipporah Films.

movies.title: Hijra
movies.description: A journey to Mecca for a grandmother and her two granddaughters is interrupted when the eldest sister disappears, sending the remaining duo on a search across the Kingdom in this intergenerational road-trip drama about family tensions, buried secrets, and unexpected bonds between Saudi women. Hijra premiered at the Venice International Film Festival, where it won the NETPAC Award for Best Asian Film.

movies.title: Himiko
movies.description: 35mm print imported from Japan (courtesy National Film Archive of Japan) Drawing again from the forms of Japanese theater and visual arts, this singular film retells the story of Himiko: a shaman queen in ancient Japan who is central to Shinto and national origin stories. Using the past to comment on the present, Shinoda presents Himiko navigating the patriarchal military powers of the surrounding kingdoms as well as her own physical desire for her recently returned half-brother. With a brilliant performance by Shima Iwashita—an actress in the work of Ozu, Kinoshita, and Kobayashi, as well as Shinoda’s wife and long time collaborator— Himiko was made in collaboration with the legendary avant garde Japanese film production company Art Theater Guild.

movies.title: Hot Spot
movies.cast: Andrzej Konopka, Noomi Rapace, Reika Kirishima
movies.description: Set in a near future society ruled by sentient A.I., a private eye investigates a murder case only to discover a rebel group capable of undermining the digital overlord. As the detective's identity slowly unravels, his world enters a state of hypnotic meltdown.

movies.title: House
movies.description: A demonic house cat is only one of the cast of outlandish characters in Ôbayashi’s psychedelic ghost story in which a schoolgirl and six of her teen classmates go on a trip to her ailing aunt’s mist-wreathed country house and find themselves caught…

movies.title: How To Build A Library
movies.description: In 2017, Kenyan writer Shiro Koinange and publisher Angela Wachuka set out to reclaim Nairobi’s McMillan Memorial Library, a colonial-era institution that had once barred Black patrons and remained frozen in the image of the British Empire. Determined to transform the decaying monument into a vibrant public space, they secure a tenuous management contract, inherit a skeptical staff, and begin reimagining its collections, programming, and purpose. As they digitize hundreds of thousands of texts and challenge colonial knowledge systems embedded in structures like the Dewey Decimal classification, tensions arise—both internally and externally with government officials whose shifting demands threaten the project’s future. Fundraising galas, satellite library launches, and even a visit from King Charles III bring visibility and prestige, yet underscore the enduring entanglements of colonial history and contemporary power. Despite political instability and bureaucratic uncertainty, Shiro and Wachuka’s efforts ultimately transform the once-exclusionary library into a dynamic cultural hub, embodying a broader struggle to redefine Kenya’s past and imagine its sovereign future. Followed by a Q&A with Damilola Lemomu (June Givanni Archives) and Angela Wachuka, moderated by Daniella Brito

movies.title: Hud
movies.description: In Martin Ritt’s baroque adaptation of Larry McMurtry’s debut novel Horseman, Pass By , Paul Newman plays Hud Bannon: a sneering, womanizing, beer-chugging cattleman who is utterly impossible to take your eyes off of. Hud makes a magnetic counterexample to his principled father Homer (Melvyn Douglas) as they disagree over how to handle an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease. This generational struggle is observed by Hud’s teen nephew Lonnie (Brandon De Wilde) and the family housekeeper Alma (Patricia Neal), whose lonesome backstories contribute to the dusty, melancholic atmosphere conjured by cameraman James Wong Howe and Ritt, still underrated among proto-New Hollywood auteurs.

movies.title: I Am Black, I Am Beautiful
movies.description: I Am Black, I Am Beautiful (2023) Dir. Sabrina Onana 83min; DCP France New York Premiere Twelve Afro-French women talk about their relationship with hair, beauty standards, men, and representation in the media. Their journey of doubts, growth, alienation, reconciliation, resilience, and self-acceptance raises awareness about social and cultural issues in both African and Western societies. By publicly sharing their experiences, the documentary creates space for these women to speak, be seen, and be heard, while fostering an honest dialogue both within and beyond the Black community. Followed by a Q&A with director Sabrina Onana, moderated by Felicia Appenteng Preceded by: Children of Diaspora (2024) Dir. Sabrina Onana With Edwina Adelard, Mansour Diop, Monika Néréa Mouanza 8min; DCP France In French with English subtitles Through the inner monologue of a child of African immigrants, the film brings us originally and poetically to the heart of the identity journey of diaspora children.

movies.title: I Love Boosters
movies.description: In another surreal, politically-charged, and straight-up weird outing from eccentric director Boots Riley ( Sorry to Bother You ), I Love Boosters follows a crew of professional shoplifters (Keke Palmer, Naomi Ackie) as they take aim at a cutthroat fashion maven (Demi Moore)—in an effort they deem a community service. Sneak preview screening on May 19 at 7:30pm followed by a Q&A with Boots Riley

movies.title: I Want Your Sex
movies.description: The latest from New Queer Cinema pioneer Gregg Araki ( Mysterious Skin , The Doom Generation , White Bird in a Blizzard ), I Want Your Sex follows Elliot, a kind-hearted if unmotivated twentysomething (Hoffman), whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes young Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries, and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli XCX) and repressed roommate (Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the lines between satire, romantic comedy, mystery, and murder blur through the colorful and edgy visual language for which Araki is best known.

movies.title: I Want Your Sex
movies.description: When fresh-faced Elliot (Cooper Hoffman) lands an exciting job for renowned artist, icon, and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde), his fantasies come true as Erika taps him to become her sexual muse. But Elliot soon finds himself out of his depth as Erika takes him on a journey more profound than he ever could have imagined, into a world of sex, obsession, power, betrayal, and murder.

movies.title: Igualada + Landslide (Avalancha)
movies.description: Landslide (Avalancha) (2023) Dir. Daniel Santiago Cortés Ramírez 25min; DCP In Spanish with English subtitles Composed entirely of archival footage, this experimental documentary opens with solely sound: scraping, rattling, and rumbling, like pebbles coming loose and starting to roll down a slope. The earth stirs before it starts to slide. What follows is a procession that runs through time and always takes a different form. A funeral procession, a protest march, a sea of fedoras, uniformed men on horses. And the sound continues to swell. The result is not just a depiction of Colombian history, but of resistance broadly, and the lives lost in its wake. Igualada (2024) Dir. Juan Mejia Botero 81min; DCP In Spanish with English subtitles Deemed “rousing and intimate” by Variety , Botero’s film follows the 2022 campaign of Francia Márquez, a Black woman from a rural background in her pursuit of Colombia’s presidency. The film’s title, defined by an opening caption as “a derogatory term (based on class, race and gender) used to designate someone who acts as if they deserve rights and privileges that supposedly don’t correspond to them,” is transformed through Márquez’s campaign, drawing the historically underrepresented into the nation’s political process. Filmed over the course of 15 years, Botero provides a portrait that is both personal and socially moving.

movies.title: In My Skin
movies.description: De Van writes, directs, and stars in this morbidly transfixing, at times suffocatingly intimate psychodrama from the high heady horrifying heyday of New French Extremity, playing Ester, a seemingly well adjusted Parisian career woman whose life changes…

movies.title: In the Mood for Love
movies.description: Wong’s arthouse smash is the very simple tale of two people in early ’60s Hong Kong, Mr. Chow (Tony Leung Chiu-wai) and Mrs. Chen (Maggie Cheung), drawn to one another by the discovery that their spouses are getting together on the side. A little…

movies.title: In Vanda’S Room
movies.description: Costa’s second film of three set in the Fontaínhas district on the outskirts of Lisbon, In Vanda’s Room employs the life of a self-destructive heroin addict as an entrypoint to explore a marginalized people and community living on the fringes of urban society. Shot in an unflinchingly realist style consisting of entirely fixed shots, Costa—himself a student of Reis—reveals a narrativized evolution of the immensely personal style developed by Reis and Cordeiro thirty years prior.

movies.title: Inherent Vice
movies.cast:
Joaquin Phoenix, 
Josh Brolin, 
Owen Wilson, 
Katherine Waterston, 
Reese Witherspoon, 
Benicio del Toro, 
Martin Short, 
Jena Malone, 
Joanna Newsom
movies.description: The second Paul Thomas Anderson adaptation of a Pynchon novel ( The Master was loosely inspired by V) follows Larry "Doc" Sportello (Phoenix), a bungling private investigator fumbling through the criminal underworld of 1970 Los Angeles. Arguably the most quintessential presentation of Pynchon put to film tonally, the narration—as read by the musician Joanna Newsom—pulls some of the novel’s text verbatim.

movies.title: Insidious: Out of the Further
movies.description: The next entry in the James Wan-produced horror series brings us back to the world of INSIDIOUS, but this time, the demons are getting out. A young mother discovers she can travel into The Further, the purgatorial realm of lost souls, and, more troublingly, bring its inhabitants back with her. Once the Lipstick-Faced Demon and his cronies figure out what she can do, the walls between their world and ours start coming down. In addition to the franchise’s trademark jump scares, this one might be the first one to make a couch cushion fort terrifying.

movies.title: Inventing Cinema: Moustapha Alassane + Georges Mélies
movies.description: The invention of cinema was not a singular moment, but a series of parallel discoveries across the globe. Honoring the national film cultures of Niger and France, Inventing Cinema reintroduces the medium through two of its pioneering magicians. During the moving image’s nascent period, Georges Méliès bridged the nineteenth and twentieth centuries with fantastical experiments of theatricality and spectacle. Drawing on his background as an actor and illusionist, the French filmmaker invented editing techniques that continue to inform modern movie creation. Decades later, the autodidact Alassane Moustapha’s precocious childhood puppet shows and shadow plays laid the foundation for an improvised reinvention of cinema. Moustapha made films before ever seeing a camera, but eventually received formal training that led to a wayward and whimsical filmography of trenchant political satires, animated fables, and imaginative transpositions of oral storytelling. Illusions fantasmagoriques (1898) Dir. Georges Mélies, 1min L'illusionniste fin de siècle, ou L’impressionniste fin de siècle (1899) Dir. Georges Mélies, 1 min La lanterne magique (1903) Dir. Georges Mélies, 5min Le dirigeable fantastique (1905) Dir. Georges Mélies, 3min Le magician (1889) Dir. Georges Mélies, 1min Le mélomane (1903) Dir. Georges Mélies, 3min Le voyage dans la lune (1902) Dir. Georges Mélies, 15min Les illusions fantaisistes (1909) Dir. Georges Mélies, 5min Sorcellerie culinaire (1904) Dir. Georges Mélies, 4min Un homme de têtes (1889) Dir. Georges Mélies, 1min Bon Voyage, Sim (1966) Dir. Moustapha Alassane, 5min Kokoa (2001) Dir. Moustapha Alassane, 14min La mort de Gandji (1965) Dir. Moustapha Alassane, 5min Samba le Grand (1977) Dir. Moustapha Alassane, 14min

movies.title: Irreversible
movies.description: Fourteen long sequence shots arranged in reverse chronology take us on a journey from hell to heaven, from nightmarish violence to connubial bliss. In a BDSM club evocatively called Club Rectum, Pierre (Albert Dupontel) dashes in the face of a man who’s…

movies.title: Is This Thing On?
movies.description: As their marriage quietly unravels, Alex (Arnett) faces middle age and an impending divorce, seeking new purpose in the New York comedy scene while Tess (Dern) confronts the sacrifices she made for their family—forcing them to navigate co-parenting, identity, and whether love can take a new form. Bradley Cooper writes, directs, and co-stars in this understated, affecting portrait of the challenges and opportunities of starting over in middle age.

movies.title: Jacob's Ladder
movies.description: Having proven himself a reliable hitmaker through the 1980s with Flashdance, 9½ Weeks, and Fatal Attraction, Lyne took an excursion into troubling new territory with this headlong plunge into the damaged psyche of Vietnam veteran Jacob Singer (Tim…

movies.title: Jeanne Dielman, 23 Quai Du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles
movies.description: A singular and uniquely influential moment in film history, Chantal Akerman’s Jeanne Dielman, 23, quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles meticulously details, with a sense of impending doom, the daily routine of a middle-aged widow. In its enormous spareness, Akerman’s film seems simple, but it encompasses an entire world. Both an exacting character study and one of cinema’s most hypnotic and complete depictions of space and time, the slice-of-life narrative, composed of long takes and lingering sequences, ranked first in 2022’s Sight and Sound critic’s poll of the greatest films of all time.

movies.title: Jennifer's Body
movies.description: High school besties Anita and Jennifer (Amanda Seyfried and Megan Fox) are all but inseparable—though “Needy” Anita is a mousy bookworm and Jennifer a lusted-after member of the color guard—but can their opposites-attract dynamic survive…

movies.title: JFK
movies.description: The alpha and omega of conspiracy films, Stone’s deliriously entertaining cinematic inquest stars Kevin Costner as Jim Garrison, the New Orleans district attorney who came to find the circumstances of the 35th US president’s assassination more than a…

movies.title: Julia
movies.description: Based on a chapter from Lillian Hellman's 1973 autobiographical work Pentimento , Zinnemann’s political drama traces the stories of two women and the intersections of their lives before and during the Nazi era. The film, a tribute to a memory of Hellman’s childhood friend Julia (Redgrave), recounts the occasion of Julia’s request that Hellmen herself (Fonda) undertake a dangerous mission in service of the fight against Naziism.

movies.title: Klute
movies.description: In the first installment of what would eventually come to be referred to as Pakula’s "paranoia trilogy" (followed by The Parallax View and All the President's Men ), Fonda hauntingly portrays Bree Daniels, a high-priced call girl stalked by a psychopath. When she crosses paths with private eye John Klute (Sutherland), a blossoming romance thrusts Klute into the position of protector as he unravels the extent of Daniels’ predicament. Fonda won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her tour-de-force performance, cementing the eerie tone of a film that investigates surveillance and the weight of being watched.

movies.title: L'Argent
movies.description: A film in which sound, often off-screen, enriches the image, and carries enormous, frequently tragic implications: the tinkling shatter of a glass of white wine seen precipitously perched on an upright piano, the sound of an open palm crossing a young…

movies.title: La Collectionneuse
movies.description: Introduction by filmmaker Annie Baker on Saturday, July 11th

movies.title: La Haine
movies.description: A cinematic Molotov cocktail that was the first onscreen description of life (and death) in Paris’s banlieue housing projects that many French filmgoers had ever seen, La Haine depicts three armed and angry slum kids—Vincent Cassel, Hubert Koundé,…

movies.title: La Notte
movies.description: Novelist Giovanni Pontano (Marcello Mastroianni) is the toast of the Italian literary scene, but smothered by the trappings of success. His misery weighs heavily on his wife, Lidia (Jeanne Moreau), already carrying her own cargo of existential anguish. In…

movies.title: Lady
movies.description: In the restless night of Lagos, one of the city’s few female cab drivers, Lady, survives by staying tough and focused. She dreams of escape, saving her earnings for a new life far from the chaos of this Nigerian metropolis. But when long-lost childhood friend, Pinky - now a sex worker - returns with a burst of colour and trouble, Lady is pulled reluctantly into her orbit. Soon she’s driving a crew of glamorous, reckless, fun-loving women through the underbelly of Lagos nightlife. What begins as judgement becomes unexpected sisterhood: wild, tender, and disarming. As Lady becomes entangled in their world the nights grow more dangerous, and the city presses harder against old wounds she’s never confronted. Forced to face the trauma she’s long outrun, she cracks open - learning to feel, to belong, to see herself through new eyes. When everything reaches breaking point, Lady must make a choice that will change her life’s direction forever. In that choice lies a new kind of freedom: one rooted not in escape, but in transformation. Followed by a Q&A with director Olive Nwosu, moderated by Karen McMullen

movies.title: Lady in the Water
movies.description: To its detractors, evidence of auteur egomania run amok, to its admirers, among the most personal and individualistic studio productions of the last 20 years, Lady in the Water is a daring admixture of the quotidian and the fantastic, in which the…

movies.title: Laila’S Birthday
movies.description: When government cuts force a judge (Mohammed Bakri) to make a career pivot, Abu Laila finds himself driving a taxi in the hectic streets of the West Bank. On the day of his daughter's birthday, his wife insists that he needs to be home early with a present and a cake. The proud ex-judge embarks on a sprawling urban odyssey plagued by gridlock, disorderly passengers, and the myriad plights affecting daily life under occupation.

movies.title: Last Year At Marienbad
movies.description: Not just a defining work of the French New Wave but one of the great, lasting mysteries of modern art, Alain Resnais’s epochal Last Year at Marienbad (L ’année dernière à Marienbad ) has puzzled appreciative viewers for decades. Written by Alain Robbe-Grillet, a radical master of the New Novel, this surreal fever dream gorgeously fuses timelines while telling the ambiguous tale of a man and a woman (Giorgio Albertazzi and Delphine Seyrig) who may or may not have met a year ago, perhaps at the very same cathedral-like, mirror-filled château they now find themselves wandering. Unforgettable in both its haunting scope and confounding details (gilded ceilings, diabolical parlor games, a loaded gun, sudden appearances and disappearances) Resnais’s investigation into the nature of memory is disturbing, romantic, and maybe even a ghost story.

movies.title: Late Fame
movies.director: Kent Jones Starring Willem Dafoe, Greta Lee, And Edmund Donovan
movies.description: Willem Dafoe is Ed Saxberger, a postal worker whose former life as a downtown poet in late-70s New York is rediscovered by a young admirer (Donovan) and his “Enthusiasm Society,” a group of 20-somethings with a comically romanticized sense of the past. In the company of his new friends, including the mysterious and mercurial Gloria (Lee of PAST LIVES), Ed has the uncanny feeling of merging with his younger self. Directed by Kent Jones (DIANE) from a witty, razor-sharp script by Samy Burch (MAY D

movies.title: Late Fame
movies.director: Kent Jones Starring Willem Dafoe, Greta Lee, And Edmund Donovan
movies.description: Willem Dafoe is Ed Saxberger, a postal worker whose former life as a downtown poet in late-70s New York is rediscovered by a young admirer (Donovan) and his “Enthusiasm Society,” a group of 20-somethings with a comically romanticized sense of the past. In the company of his new friends, including the mysterious and mercurial Gloria (Lee of PAST LIVES), Ed has the uncanny feeling of merging with his younger self. Directed by Kent Jones (DIANE) from a witty, razor-sharp script by Samy Burch (MAY D

movies.title: Le Pont Du Nord
movies.description: A bank robber (Bulle Ogier) recently released from prison and a young woman (portrayed by Bulle’s daughter, Pascale) roam the streets of Paris, cinematically reimagined as a sprawling board game, in a quest to understand the contents of a mysterious suitcase. A gorgeously rendered portrait of Paris imbued with an ever-present ominous rhythm, the playful middle period work from Rivette shares with Pynchon an interest in conspiracy and secret histories.

movies.title: Learning To Fly
movies.cast: Aisha McAdams, Eszter Csillag, Jim Walmsley
movies.description:
Under a full moon over the Alps, a headlamp bobs through the dark for the eighteenth hour. This is ultra running: 100 miles of mountain terrain, run through the night, chasing something just past the edge of what seems humanly possible.

LEARNING TO FLY follows Aisha McAdams - a photographer, and once a competitive runner herself - as she embeds with the sport's biggest names, including Jim Walmsley and Eszter Csillag, at the legendary Western States Endurance Run and the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc. Her lens captures the 2 a.m. camaraderie, heartbreaking losses, and euphoric finishes.

But the closer Aisha gets to these athletes, the closer she gets to the runner she left behind, and the reasons she walked away from a sport that once gave her everything. Watching this community chase the impossible, Aisha is forced to ask whether she still has it in her to fly.

movies.title: Les Bonnes Femmes
movies.description: An early and enormous artistic triumph of the French New Wave, Chabrol’s quietly class-conscious film records the dreams, dramas, and self-deceptions of a quartet of young Parisian girls working at an appliance shop, among them Bernadette Lafont and…

movies.title: Leviticus
movies.description: In a conservative Australian town, the most terrifying thing facing two queer teens isn’t just the ostracization of their community, but a more sinister entity that takes the form of the person they desire most: each other. With captivating performances from its breakout stars, this striking debut from director Adrian Chiarella deftly weaves a truly haunting premise and moments of sweet romance into a larger tapestry investigating the toll of contemporary bigotry.

movies.title: Linda Linda Linda
movies.description: With their last high school concert only days away, bandmates Kei, Kyoko, and Nozomi’s hopes of taking the stage appear to be dashed when their lead singer quits the group, leaving them to hastily recruit a Korean exchange student with a limited grasp…

movies.title: Lone Star
movies.description: In the sleepy hamlet of Frontera, two off-duty cops discover a buried skeleton at an old shooting range, prompting an investigation from straight-arrow Sheriff Sam Deeds (Chris Cooper). Soon it’s revealed the body belongs to Sam’s notoriously corrupt predecessor Charlie Wade (Kris Kristofferson) and a twisty, old-fashioned murder mystery ensues, aided immensely by a killer ensemble cast (Frances McDormand, Elizabeth Peña, Joe Morton and Matthew McConaughey) and music by Mason Daring. Maybe the most celebrated film of John Sayles’ career, Lone Star disentangles Texas mythology with shrewd attention to the shifting mores and demographics of the contemporary West.

movies.title: Los Angeles Plays Itself
movies.description: Los Angeles is more than where movies are made; it also provides the thematic undercurrent for a myriad of iconic moments in cinema history. Thom Andersen's documentary Los Angeles Plays Itself explores this complicated tapestry and the ways in which the town and the works created within it interact. An avowed fan of classic Hollywood, the west coast mecca has a major place in Pynchon’s personal lore as his primary residence in the 60s and early 70s. His examination of the city’s counter culture up close in Manhattan Beach informs a lot of his west coast novels, which are comfortably in conversation with Thom Anderson’s magnum opus on Hollywood and the history of power in California.

movies.title: Los Nadie (The Nobodies)
movies.description: In Medellín, five friends on the precipice of leaving adolescence are entrenched in the unrest, rage, and tenderness of youth. Living on the outskirts of a city that excludes them, they embrace music, street art, and friendship as weapons of resistance in this coming of age ensemble film.

movies.title: Los Punks + Beyond The Screams
movies.description: From Los Angeles to Chicago, New York, Santa Fe, and more, the Latino/Chicano punk movement developed within the U.S. as a means for young people to express themselves and resist growing societal oppression. Los Punks showcases the development of this movement specifically in LA, while Beyond the Screams explores the wider development of Latino punk throughout the U.S. from the ‘70s through the early ‘90s. Los Punks: We Are All We Have (2016) Dir. Angela Boatwright 79min; Digital This intimate documentary follows teens and young adults who find meaning in the thriving punk rock scene in the backyards of South Central and East Los Angeles. Beyond the Screams (Mas Alla de Los Gritos) (1999) Dir. Martin Sorondeguy 29min; Digital In English and Spanish with English subtitles From the late 1970s up until the early 1990s, young people looking for a way to empower themselves began to develop a Latino/Chicano punk movement across the U.S. Martin Sorrondeguy, singer of hardcore punk bands Los Crudos and Limp Wrist, and a prominent figure in both the straight edge scene and the queercore scene, follows the development of the scene through the decades in major Latino cities. Composed of interviews and live performances, this film focuses on the struggle of Latino/Chicano artists against globalization, poverty, and identity.

movies.title: Love in the Afternoon
movies.description: Introduction by Feed Me founder Emily Sundberg on Saturday, July 11th

movies.title: Maddie’S Secret
movies.description: Inspired by Douglas Sirk, Todd Haynes, Showgirls , and the nearly pornographic world of online food influencers, comedian, writer, and actor John Early makes his critically acclaimed directorial debut with the story of a breakout new-media star who’s hiding a secret. Early portrays Maddie, a dishwasher at L.A. food-content creation studio Gourmaybe, who makes her own vegetarian cooking videos at home with help from her adoring husband (Eric Rahill). When one of her videos goes viral, Maddie is thrust into the influencer sphere herself, straining her bond with her sassy queer BFF (Kate Berlant) and threatening to expose her struggle with an eating disorder. Blending satire and melodrama, the film announces a bold new voice in contemporary cinema.

movies.title: Malcolm X
movies.description: The culmination of a longtime dream, Malcolm X exemplifies director Spike Lee’s unique vision and style, moving elegantly between genres and time periods with a dazzling array of camera movements and meticulous editing as he tells the life story of the iconic leader. Denzel Washington embodies Malcolm with conviction, force, and dignity in one of his most indelible performances.

movies.title: Maluala
movies.description: Maluala takes us into a palenque —a fortified settlement of escaped slaves—hidden in Cuba’s eastern mountains, as the Spanish colonial forces attempt to sow discord among their leaders. The film marks Giral’s third entry into his trilogy of films about slavery in 19th-century Cuba and the Caribbean, combining a Marxist lens with the long arc of Black Liberation to trace the development from individual to collective struggle.

movies.title: Marty Supreme
movies.description: Timothée Chalamet “makes one of the most colossal movie performances of the 21st century seem as natural as a lay-up” ( IndieWire ) in the latest offering from director Josh Safdie (co-director, Good Time , Uncut Gems ). Performing with a distinguished cast that includes Gwyneth Paltrow, Odessa A'zion, and Tyler Okonma (a.k.a. Tyler, the Creator), Chalamet gives “the defining performance of his still-burgeoning career” ( Variety ) as would-be ping-pong champion Marty Mauser, a young man with a dream no one respects, who goes to hell and back in pursuit of greatness.

movies.title: Mary Jane'S Not A Virgin Anymore
movies.description: When a bright, self-possessed movie theater employee decides to lose her virginity, she discovers that sex is less a rite of passage than a series of awkward negotiations. Sasha Jacobson’s ( I Was a Teenage Serial Killer ) sharply observed indie coming-of-age story charts the debauched misadventures of a slacker squad of co-workers. Keep an eye out for cameos by iconic punk frontmen Jello Biafra and Davey Havok. Featuring a reading by Josh Bayer before the screening on February 14.

movies.title: María Antonia
