But when she visits the original movie's star, a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

movies.title: Teenage Sex And Death At Camp Miasma In 35Mm
movies.cast: Hannah Einbinder, Gillian Anderson, Amanda Fix, Arthur Conti, Patrick Fischler, Jack Haven
movies.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Hannah Einbinder, Hacks) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson, The X-Files, Sex Education), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

movies.title: Testament
movies.description: Sometimes released with the subtitle, “a warzone of memories,” Testament paints a portrait of the Kwame Nkrumah era in Ghanaian history. After two decades of exile following the 1966 coup d’état, government minister-turned-journalist Abena returns to her native country to interview director Werner Herzog, only to instead reckon with her political past through this fragmented, poetic film.

movies.title: The Adventures Of Buckaroo Banzai Across The 8Th Dimension
movies.description: Buckaroo Banzai (Weller), a cartoonishly over-qualified physicist, neurosurgeon, test pilot, and rock star, must stop alien invaders in this campy sci-fi cult film. Pynchonesque in its overly wacky plot, screenwriter Earl Mac Rauch's genre pastiche is also a reflection of the novelist’s taste for low-brow, pulp, and the sci-fi that colored his youthful media consumption.

movies.title: The Ballad Of Gregorio Cortez
movies.description: Adapted from Americo Paredes’ With His Pistol in His Hand , Robert M. Young’s The Ballad of Gregorio Cortez dramatizes the real-life case of Cortez (Edward James Olmos), a Mexican American farmer who became a folk hero after killing an abusive Texas Ranger in self-defense in 1901. With this lyrical yet unsentimental film, Young and his Chicano collaborators put a human face to a widely misunderstood chapter in Texas history. The Ballad of Gregorio Cortez is conversant with the corrido tradition that gives it structure, but also with the stale frontier tropes it challenges, resulting in a work of revisionism and reportage.

movies.title: The Bend In The River
movies.director: Robb Moss Executive Produced By Joel Coen And Frances Mcdormand
movies.description: Filming five friends intimately for nearly 50 years, director Robb Moss invites us to reflect on what it means to inhabit a life fully, in its contradictions and continuities. He began filming Barry, Danny, Cathy, Jeff, and Jim in 1978, when they worked as guides on the Colorado River and lived together in a nude commune—resulting in his short documentary, Riverdogs (1982). He resumed shooting as they came to terms with adulthood for his 2003 follow-up, THE SAME RIVER TWICE. The final installmen

movies.title: The Big Lebowski
movies.description: Jeff Lebowski, who actually only answers to “The Dude,” is mistaken for a millionaire of the same name and thrust into an intentionally over-complicated mystery in the Coen Brothers’ sprawling Raymond Chandler-inspired comedy. A predecessor to Pynchon’s Inherent Vice (and Paul Thomas Anderson’s later adaptation), this shaggy dog detective story similarly traces a derelict of the New Left navigating the power systems of Southern California.

movies.title: The Blair Witch Project
movies.description: The opening text of this era-defining indie horror reads: “In October of 1994 three student filmmakers disappeared in the woods near Burkittsville, Maryland, while shooting a documentary. A year later their footage was found.” In the diegetic filmmakers’ search for the truth of a local myth, the milestone late ‘90s horror calls back to colonial America’s obsession with the supernatural and the idea that something terrifying lingers in the woods at the frontier. Immensely terrifying, simple, and magnetic, the debut from Myrick and Sánchez launched a revival of found footage horror movies throughout the 2000s.

movies.title: The Blue Caftan
movies.description: Halim and Mina run a traditional caftan store in one of Morocco’s oldest medinas, and hire Youssef in order to keep up with customer demand. Mina gradually realizes how much her husband is moved by the young man’s presence. Morocco’s official entry for Best International Film at the 95th Academy Awards, The Blue Caftan tells a surprising, tender story of unconditional love and acceptance.

movies.title: The Burning Sunset (Aka Killers On Parade)
movies.description: 35mm print imported from Japan (courtesy of the Japan Foundation) A genre-hopping, candy colored comedy-noir-musical, Shinoda’s third feature captures the anarchic spirit of ‘60s filmmaking—recalling Jean-Luc Godard and Seijun Suzuki. When a muckraking journalist is targeted by a gang of youthful assassins (and their pet goat, The End), she must turn to another killer for help. Again working with poet/filmmaker Shuji Terayama as screenwriter, this jazzy satire of Japanese cinema is filled with comic book, pop art energy.

movies.title: The Chaser
movies.description: Drawing inspiration from the gristly exploits of South Korean serial killer Yoo Young-chul, Na’s astonishingly assured directorial debut stars Ha Jung-woo as a sadistic killer, Ji Yeong-min, and Kim Yoon-seok as Joong-ho, an ex-detective with a…

movies.title: The China Syndrome
movies.description: Named for the fictional result of a nuclear meltdown (where reactor fuel melts through the crust of the Earth all the way “to China”), Bridges’ biting thriller traces a reporter’s investigation of a cover-up of safety hazards at a Los Angeles nuclear plant. A gripping and timely depiction of the decade’s nuclear suspicion, the film’s coincidental (and perhaps prescient) release twelve days prior to the Three Mile Island nuclear accident spawned unanticipated conversation and acclaim. Both Fonda and Lemmon received Oscar nods for their portrayals of two strangers bound by a mutually terrifying discovery.

movies.title: The Christophers
movies.description: The estranged children (Corden, Gunning) of a beloved dormant artist (McKellen) hire Lori (Coel), an art restorer and former forger, to pose as a prospective assistant in an effort to access some unfinished canvases they believe to be instrumental to conjuring a worthwhile inheritance. As always, Steven Soderbergh is a master of embedding the formal and technical flourishes of the arthouse inside seemingly populist fare, as exemplified in his Ocean ’s trilogy and last year’s Black Bag (2025). In turns that Deadline deemed an "unusually emotional film for Soderbergh,” McKellen’s and Coel’s tête-à-tête makes for a quintessentially funny and engrossing addition to the director’s oeuvre.

movies.title: The Currents
movies.description: Lina (Isabel Aimé González Sola), an accomplished Argentine artist and designer, is in Switzerland to receive an award when she jumps from a bridge into the icy waters below. As she later confesses to a friend, she experienced a moment of deep peace until the thought of her young daughter drew her back to life. But the incident leaves her with a paralyzing fear of water and a growing sense of isolation that threatens both her career and her personal life. Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Milagros Mumenthaler ( Back to Stay ), The Currents is a quietly gripping portrait of a woman on the verge of unraveling.

movies.title: The Cycle Of Love
movies.cast: P.K. Mahanandia, Lotta Mahanandia, Mina Dale, Chirag Lobo
movies.description: In 1977, PK, a 23-year-old Delhi street artist from a poor, ‘untouchable’ family, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile cross-continent mission - to find Lotta, the woman who had captured his heart. A love story like no other, THE CYCLE OF LOVE is an inspiring, heart-warming, epic true-life adventure about the search for self-belief and risking everything for what your heart tells you.

movies.title: The Dark Knight
movies.description: The city of Chicago plays an oppressively glum Gotham in Nolan, Christian Bale, and Gary Oldman’s second Batman outing, a film of Langian architectural oppression that pits Bruce Wayne’s alter ego against Heath Ledger’s anarchic Clown Prince of…

movies.title: The Daytrippers
movies.description: Greg Mottola’s feature debut, teeming with deadpan humor and surprising emotional weight, established him as a voice of the ‘90s indie scene. After discovering a love letter written to her husband (Stanley Tucci), Eliza (Hope Davis) rallies her bombastic Long Island family to embark on a quest to uncover the truth. The group—sister (Posey) and pretentious boyfriend (Schriber), her headstrong mom (Anne Meara), and reserved father (McNamara)—traipses New York City in pursuit of answers throughout a detour-filled day that sends the family through the ringer as new revelations come to light and old familial schisms rear their heads.

movies.title: The Drama
movies.description: Days before they’re set to tie the knot, a happily engaged couple (Zendaya, Pattinson) is put to the test when one partner discovers some shocking truths about the other. In Kristoffer Borgli’s ( Dream Scenario ) highly-anticipated pairing of two of contemporary cinema’s brightest stars, Zendaya and Pattinson (set to appear onscreen together again this year in Dune: Part Three ) deliver a wedding movie for the ages.

movies.title: The Elephant Man
movies.description: New 4K Restoration Before Blue Velvet cemented Lynch as one of the century’s preeminent directors, he released The Elephant Man , an atmospheric historical drama and important moment in understanding the development of the auteur’s signature style. Set in Victorian England, the black-and-white film follows London surgeon Frederick Treves (Anthony Hopkins) and his developing friendship with freak-show performer John Merrick (John Hurt), challenging perceptions around disability and human dignity. With a stellar supporting cast that includes Anne Bancroft, John Gielgud, and Wendy Hiller, Lynch’s surreal take on a biopic was nominated for eight Academy Awards, cementing his reputation as one of American cinema’s most visionary talents.

movies.title: The End of Oak Street
movies.cast: Anne Hathaway, Ewan McGregor, Christian Convery, Maisy Stella
movies.description: A family must stick together to survive their unrecognizable surroundings

movies.title: The End of Oak Street
movies.cast: Anne Hathaway, Ewan McGregor, Christian Convery, Maisy Stella
movies.description: After a mysterious cosmic event rips Oak Street from suburbia and transports their neighborhood to someplace unknown, the Platt family soon discovers that their very survival depends on them sticking together as they navigate their now unrecognizable surroundings.

movies.title: The Fast and the Furious: 25th Anniversary
movies.description:
High stakes. Blazing speed. Heart-pounding action. A brotherhood fueled by adrenaline. Welcome to the world of underground street racing.
At the turn of the millennium, audiences across the world were introduced to a pulse-pounding, pedal-to-the-metal saga that would forever redefine the action genre... but it started on the streets.
Enter THE FAST AND THE FURIOUS, a high-octane thriller that follows undercover cop Brian O'Conner (Paul Walker) as he infiltrates the world of illegal street racing led by charismatic criminal Dominic Toretto (Vin Diesel). As loyalties are tested and relationships forged, an unforgettable partnership is born between the two rivals.
Combining the relentless speed of high-performance cars with jaw-dropping action sequences, THE FAST AND THE FURIOUS introduced a new breed of action heroes and sparked a legendary franchise. Witness the birth of a phenomenon that changed the way we experience action movies and ignited our desire for more.

movies.title: The Girl In The Yellow Jumper
movies.description: As fear spreads across Uganda about a serial killer haunting the highways, an off-duty police officer drives an elderly witness from a remote village back to town. Along the way, he picks up an injured stranger who begins recounting the violent events that led him to the roadside. As the journey unfolds, suspicion grows inside the car, and the officer realizes the truth may be far more dangerous than the story being told.

movies.title: The Good Fairy
movies.description: In 1935, the great German-born American director William Wyler made this film about Luisa Ginglebusher, a sweet-natured yet naive young woman recently released from an orphanage who becomes an usher at a local movie theater. In an attempt to do good, Luisa finds herself wrapped up in a series of hi-jinks and romantic entanglements. The Good Fairy is based on the Hungarian play of the same name by Ferenc Molnár.

movies.title: The Great Silence
movies.description: The traditional slow-speaking taciturnity of the Western hero is taken to the extreme in Django director Corbucci’s hard-nosed, politically-provocative snowbound Spaghetti Western, set in turn-of-the-last-century Utah but filmed in the Italian…

movies.title: The Green Room
movies.description: One of Truffaut’s most personal and beautiful films, photographed “in fecund greens and withering yellows” [Dave Kehr, Chicago Reader] by DP Néstor Almendros, and one of the least known of Truffaut’s major works—audiences, it seems, weren’t…

movies.title: The Harder They Come
movies.description: Perry Henzell’s The Harder They Come marked the epochal cultural moment that first brought reggae to the international stage and made the late Jimmy Cliff a star. Now, 50 years later, the film is as electric as ever. In a Scarface -y blend of crime drama and music, we follow a country boy in search of fame as he journeys through Jamaica as a laborer, recording artist, convict, ganja dealer, and outlaw folk hero.

movies.title: The Hunger
movies.description: A lush vampire romance with sex and style to spare, much of it provided by stars Catherine Deneuve and David Bowie as a couple of posh, centuries-old nightclubbing New York bloodsuckers who, when one begins to show the first signs of aging, recruit…

movies.title: The Invite
movies.cast: Seth Rogen, Olivia Wilde, Edward Norton, Penélope Cruz
movies.description: Have Joe and Angela reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down?

movies.title: The Invite
movies.cast: Seth Rogen, Olivia Wilde, Edward Norton, Penélope Cruz
movies.description: Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela’s (Olivia Wilde) marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors (Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton) for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down? A remake of the 2020 Spanish film The People Upstairs , Olivia Wilde’s star-studded take on a dinner party dramedy (written by Will McCormack and Rashida Jones) is a timely portrait of a modern marriage, teeming with wit, belly laughs, and a surprising poignancy.

movies.title: The Invite
movies.cast: Seth Rogen, Olivia Wilde, Edward Norton, Penélope Cruz
movies.description: Joe and Angela's marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down?

movies.title: The Island Of Saint Matthews
movies.description: When Kevin Jerome Everson’s inquiry about family photos reveals a lost history, he travels to meet the inhabitants of Westport—a small town just to the west of Columbus, Mississippi—to uncover how his familial record vanished. In this personal investigation of records lost to time and circumstance, Everson convenes with the Wesportians about the great flood of the Tombigbee River in 1973, when some people lost everything. An act of recovery and discovery, Emerson finds a piece of his own history in his pursuit of what was lost.

movies.title: The Jungle Book
movies.description: Inspired by the adventures of the foundling Mowgli in Rudyard Kipling’s 1894 collection of the same name, The Jungle Book—the final animated Disney feature to be overseen in its production by Uncle Walt—would become one of the studio’s biggest…

movies.title: The Last Supper
movies.description: In Tomás Gutiérrez Alea’s bold cinematic parable, the owner of a Havana sugar plantation attempts to teach Christianity to his enslaved workers by staging a recreation of the Biblical Last Supper. But when the enslaved refuse to be proselytized and learn that the Count has reneged on his compensatory promises, the film spirals into a darkly ironic critique of colonialism and religion, while showing the resistance of Black peoples.

movies.title: The Legend Of Suram Fortress
movies.description: Codirected by Dodo Abashidze and Sergei Paradjanov, this film is based on a legend from the Caucasus Mountains that tells of the Georgian people’s repeated efforts to construct a fortress amid threats of invasion. The structure continues to collapse until a fortune teller recalls a fateful prophecy. At once simple and marvelous, the story unfolds in a circular manner, while its mythic possibilities are realized in the film’s jewel-like colors and decor.

movies.title: The Magic Faraway Tree
movies.description: Some kids tumble down rabbit holes. Others step through wardrobes. In THE MAGIC FARAWAY TREE, adventure begins with a climb on a swing. After moving to the English countryside, three siblings discover an enchanted tree whose highest branches lead to magical new worlds filled with unusual characters and unexpected detours. Starring Claire Foy and Andrew Garfield, this fantasy spins Enid Blyton's classic children’s book into an adventure where every trip up the tree drops the kids somewhere completely different. See it on the big screen for a healthy dose of whimsy.

movies.title: The Magician
movies.description: Ingmar Bergman's 1958 feature is an engaging, brilliantly conceived tale of deceit from one of cinema’s premier illusionists. Max von Sydow stars as Dr. Vogler, a nineteenth-century traveling mesmerist and peddler of potions, whose magic is put to the test in Stockholm by the cruel, eminently rational royal medical adviser Dr. Vergérus. The result is a diabolically clever battle of wits that’s both frightening and funny, shot in rich, gorgeously gothic black-and-white.

movies.title: The Man Died
movies.description: During Nigeria’s civil war, writer and activist Wole Soyinka is imprisoned without trial by a military regime determined to silence his dissent. Enduring solitary confinement, torture, and deprivation, he refuses to surrender his commitment to justice, drawing strength from memories of his earlier life as a writer and public intellectual. In secret, he records his experiences on scraps of paper, which are smuggled out of his cell. His words become a beacon of hope and a call to action for others living under oppression, in this work based on the harrowing prison memoir by Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka. Followed by a Q&A with director Awam Ampka

movies.title: The Marching Band
movies.cast: Benjamin Lavernhe, Pierre Lottin, Sarah Suco
movies.description: A world-famous orchestra conductor discovers the brother he never knew he had — a school cafeteria worker who plays trombone in a local marching band. Detecting his brother's exceptional musical talent, he takes it upon himself to rectify the injustice of fate.

movies.title: The Milk of Sorrow
movies.description: Winner of the Golden Bear at the 59th Berlin International Film Festival, Llosa’s formidable sophomore feature focuses on Fausta (Magaly Solier, in a performance nearly free of dialogue), the only daughter of an aged Indigenous Peruvian woman who,…

movies.title: The Night is Short, Walk on Girl
movies.description: A surreal nocturnal animated odyssey from Yuasa, the mad genius behind Mind Game, rendered in a frenetic, galaxy-brained, endlessly morphing style. The Night is Short, Walk on Girl follows a mysterious high schooler known only as The Girl with Black Hair…

movies.title: The Night Of The Hunter
movies.description: With an illustrious acting career spanning decades and genres, it’s miraculous that Charles Laughton only stepped behind the camera for one film. Even more miraculous, perhaps, is how the towering English thespian managed to encapsulate so vividly the aesthetic and narrative thrust of the American Southern Gothic in The Night of the Hunter . This eerie story of a serial killer posing as a preacher weaves together elements of Expressionism and the style of silent films, imbuing a haunting tale with a truly singular visual identity. Featuring Robert Mitchum in his finest performance and silent film star Lillian Gish in a late career peak, the film is haunting, tense, and downright sinister. Laughton’s opus would go on to influence a generation of filmmakers including Robert Altman, Spike Lee, and Martin Scorsese.

movies.title: The Odyssey
movies.description: Shooting around the globe using 70mm IMAX film cameras, director Christopher Nolan ( Oppenheimer , Tenet , Inception ) transforms Homer’s ancient Greek epic into a luxuriously cast summer blockbuster inspired by Ray Harryhausen’s 1970s sword-and-sandal adventures and informed by Emily Wilson’s admirably savvy 2017 English translation of the original poem. The Odyssey recounts the tale of Ithacan king Odysseus (Matt Damon), confronted by literal monsters and menaces as he returns with his soldiers from the Trojan War, while at home his wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) and son Telemachus (Tom Holland) send off scheming suitors like Antinous (Robert Pattinson). This film contains sequences of flashing lights which might affect customers who are susceptible to photosensitive epilepsy.

movies.title: The Odyssey
movies.description:
How do you follow up a heavy-hitting, multiple Oscar-winning blockbuster like OPPENHEIMER? If you're Christopher Nolan, you tackle one of the most influential stories ever told.
THE ODYSSEY brings Homer's ancient Greek epic to the big screen with Matt Damon as Odysseus, a warrior king trying to get home after the Trojan War. What should be a straightforward trip turns into a decade-long odyssey filled with peril, adventure, and one setback after another. Basically, it's an epic story about an all-time terrible commute.
Make no doubt about it, this is a movie built for the big screen, and Alamo Drafthouse is the place to experience it.

movies.title: The Odyssey (35mm)
movies.cast: Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong’o, Zendaya, Charlize Theron, Jon Bernthal, Logan Marshall-Green, Benny Safdie, Mia Goth, John Leguizamo, Elliot Page
movies.description: Odysseus, king of Ithaca, embarks on a perilous journey to return home after the Trojan War

movies.title: The Odyssey (DCP)
movies.cast: Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong’o, Zendaya, Charlize Theron, Jon Bernthal, Logan Marshall-Green, Benny Safdie, Mia Goth, John Leguizamo, Elliot Page
movies.description: Odysseus, king of Ithaca, embarks on a perilous journey to return home after the Trojan War

movies.title: The Oldest Person In The World
movies.cast: Ann Blackwell, Violet Brown, Genia Carter
movies.description: A ten-year worldwide exploration tracks successive holders of the oldest living person title. A study of longevity transforms into reflection on time's flow, fate's unpredicability, and the joy of human existence.

movies.title: The Others
movies.description: Having enjoyed a palpable international hit with his Abre Los Ojos—picked up for an American remake, under the title Vanilla Sky, by Tom Cruise—Amenábar made his English-language debut with The Others, a dolorous, deftly directed Old Dark House…

movies.title: The Pawnbroker
movies.description: Lumet investigates the reverberations of the Holocaust two decades later in this haunting depiction of a life altered in its wake. Numb from his experience in a concentration camp, Sol Nazerman (Steiger) lives a life emotionally alienated from those around him in a heartbreaking portrayal of post-Holocaust life. Marking Morgan Freeman’s feature film debut, it’s also Lumet’s first film to shoot at Hoyt-Schermerhorn ahead of 1978’s The Wiz , and one of the major contributors to the deterioration of the Production Code throughout the ‘60s.

movies.title: The Piano
movies.description: One of the most critically acclaimed and highly awarded films of its year, THE PIANO arouses erotic passions and vengeful jealousies when Ada, a young mute woman (Holly Hunter), is desired by two men – her husband by an arranged marriage (Sam Neill), and the husband's darkly intense neighbor (Harvey Keitel). Violent emotions erupt, but only one man understands that Ada's heart can only be won through her beloved piano.

movies.title: The Piano
movies.description: One of the most critically acclaimed and highly awarded films of its year, THE PIANO arouses erotic passions and vengeful jealousies when Ada, a young mute woman (Holly Hunter), is desired by two men – her husband by an arranged marriage (Sam Neill), and the husband's darkly intense neighbor (Harvey Keitel). Violent emotions erupt, but only one man understands that Ada's heart can only be won through her beloved piano.

movies.title: The Place Without Limits
movies.description: Adapted from José Donoso’s iconic novel by the celebrated Mexican director Arturo Ripstein, The Place Without Limits centers its story on Manuela (Roberto Cobo) and her daughter, who run a fading brothel in the remote setting of El Olivo, Mexico. As the tumbleweed town withers, an unwelcome visitor—once treated as family by the town’s mayor—stirs long‑buried tensions that threaten its fragile peace. Rejected and mislabeled by those around her, Manuela navigates a world ruled by machismo and prejudice. Her resilience and luminous spirit make her the emotional core of a community pushed to the brink. Selected by Mexico as its entry for the Best Foreign Language Film at the 51st Academy Awards, The Place Without Limits is a gripping portrait of dignity and survival in a place determined to extinguish it.

movies.title: The President'S Cake
movies.description: While people across 1990s Iraq struggle to survive the war and food shortages, President Saddam Hussein requires each school in the country to prepare a cake to celebrate his birthday. Despite her efforts to avoid getting picked, 9-year-old Lamia is chosen among her classmates, and must use her wits and imagination to gather the scarcely-available ingredients in this directorial debut that earned the 2025 Caméra d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival

movies.title: The Projectionist + She Was An Acrobat'S Daughter
movies.description: The Projectionist (1970) dir. Harry Hurwitz. With Chuck McCann, Ina Balin, Rodney Dangerfield. 88min; 35mm An imaginative Midtown projectionist (Chuck McCann) whiles away the hours—interrupted by his jerk of a boss, Renaldi (Rodney Dangerfield, in his film debut), and kept company by the movie stars lining the walls of the booth. She Was An Acrobat's Daughter (1937) dir. Friz Freleng 8min; Digital Friz Freleng’s Golden Age animated short parodies the goings-on inside a local movie theater.

movies.title: The Razor's Edge + Lebanese, Hostage of Their City
movies.description: Saab’s fiction feature debut, here in a sterling new restoration, is not without its own documentary aspect—shot amidst the devastation of the Lebanese Civil War and set during the 70-day Siege of Beirut, which appears in archival footage, The…

movies.title: The Red Light Bandit
movies.description: Described by Sganzerla—21 years old when he directed his wild-eyed feature debut—as a “Western about the Third World,” The Red Light Bandit drew inspiration from the exploits of João Acácio Pereira da Costa, a recently arrested career criminal…

movies.title: The Rivals Of Amziah King
movies.cast: Matthew McConaughey, Angelina LookingGlass, Cole Sprouse, Scott Shepherd, Rob Morgan, Tony Revolori, and Kurt Russell
movies.description: Deep within the backwoods of rural Oklahoma, charismatic and musically gifted Amziah King herds a bluegrass-playing band of misfits while overseeing the premier honey-making operation in town. When Amziah’s estranged foster daughter unexpectedly returns, Amziah leaps at the possibility to renew connection and create a family business. But the honey game is ruthless, and Amziah’s rivals threaten to destroy everything he has built.

movies.title: The Rivals of Amziah King
movies.cast: Matthew McConaughey, Angelina LookingGlass, Cole Sprouse, Scott Shepherd, Rob Morgan, Tony Revolori, and Kurt Russell
movies.description: Some people steal cash. Some steal cars. In THE RIVALS OF AMZIAH KING, they're stealing bees. Matthew McConaughey stars as a charismatic Oklahoma beekeeper, bluegrass bandleader, and local legend whose thriving honey operation puts a target on his back. When his estranged foster daughter returns, he sees a chance to build something lasting together. But in the surprisingly cutthroat world of commercial honey, jealous rivals (including Kurt Russell) are ready to sting first.

movies.title: The Salt Path
movies.cast: Gillian Anderson, Jason Isaacs, Denis Lill
movies.description: The profound story of husband and wife Raynor and Moth Winn (Jason Isaacs & Gillan Anderson), who embark on a 630-mile trek after being forcibly removed from their home. Hoping that in nature they will find solace and a sense of acceptance, they walk through the beautiful but rugged coastlines of South West England - a journey that is exhilarating, challenging, and liberating in equal measure. THE SALT PATH is a powerful portrayal of home, and how it can be lost and rediscovered in the most unexpected ways.

movies.title: The Salt Path (Virtual Q&A)
movies.cast: Gillian Anderson, Jason Isaacs, Denis Lill
movies.description: The profound story of husband and wife Raynor and Moth Winn (Jason Isaacs & Gillan Anderson), who embark on a 630-mile trek after being forcibly removed from their home. Hoping that in nature they will find solace and a sense of acceptance, they walk through the beautiful but rugged coastlines of South West England - a journey that is exhilarating, challenging, and liberating in equal measure. THE SALT PATH is a powerful portrayal of home, and how it can be lost and rediscovered in the most unexpected ways.

movies.title: The Samurai and the Prisoner
movies.cast: Masahiro Motoki, Masaki Suda, Yuriko Yoshitaka, Munetaka Aoki
movies.description: Celebrated Japanese horror director Kiyoshi Kurosawa ( Cure , Serpent’s Path ) explores a new path in this lush treatment of Honobu Yonezawa's prizewinning historical novel, detailing palace intrigue in the court of a samurai nobleman during the Azuchi era at the end of the 16th century. Turning against Oda Nobunaga, the ruthless, power-hungry warlord he previously served, Araki Murashige (Masahiro Motoki, of Departures ) is besieged by Oda’s forces and bedevilled by a series of inexplicable crimes in his household. As tension rises and loyalties fray, Murashige is forced to strategize with Kuroda Kanbei (Masaki Suda, of Kurosawa’s 2024 thriller Cloud ), a samurai envoy sent by Oda and imprisoned by Murashige, while his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and loyalists fight to preserve order.

movies.title: The Secret Agent
movies.description: Set in Brazil in 1977, the most awarded film at Cannes this year stars Wagner Moura ( Narcos , Civil War ) as Marcelo, a former teacher and political dissident on the run during the waning years of Brazil’s military dictatorship. Hoping to reunite with his son, he travels to Recife during Carnival but quickly realizes that the city is not the safe haven he expected. Critics are calling Kleber Mendonça Filho’s vivid neo-noir thriller “a masterpiece” ( The Playlist ) and “superb in every way” ( The Guardian ).

movies.title: The Smallest Show On Earth + Box Office Bunny
movies.description: The Smallest Show on Earth (1957) dir. Basil Dearden 80min; DCP The Smallest Show on Earth follows a newly married couple who unexpectedly inherit a dilapidated British cinema and set out to save it from closure, aided—and often undermined—by its eccentric staff. The prolific Basil Dearden, who worked on over 45 films across his career, directs this warmhearted comedy about love, labor, and the quiet heroics of keeping the movies alive. Box Office Bunny (1990) dir. Darrell Van Critters 5min; Digital This delightful Looney Tunes short is set in a massive movie theater situated right above Bugs’ bunny hole and co-stars Elmer Fudd and Daffy Duck.

movies.title: The Square
movies.description: Nominated for Best Documentary Feature at the 86th Academy Awards, Jehane Moujaim’s film traces the ongoing Egyptian Revolution of 2011, immersing its viewer in the intense emotional drama of young people on the streets of Cairo. The work to claim their rights and create a society of conscience against the toppling of the government serves as an inspiring tribute to the power of citizenry. The May 7 screening will be followed by a Q&A with director Jehane Noujaim and cinematographer Ahmed Hassan, moderated by Alia ElKattan

movies.title: The Stories
movies.description: When aspiring Egyptian pianist Ahmed finds a pen pal in Austrian Liz, their blossoming relationship encourages the former to focus on his ambition of performing a concert during a tumultuous time for the nation. Based on the actual meeting of director Shawky’s parents, this combination of narrative vignettes interspersed with archival footage serves as a decade and nation-spanning time capsule of love in the seventies.

movies.title: The Taking Of Pelham 123
movies.cast: Walter Matthau, Robert Shaw, Martin Balsam, Héctor Elizondo, Jerry Stiller

movies.title: The Testament Of Ann Lee
movies.description: From award-winning writer-director Mona Fastvold ( The World to Come , The Brutalist ) comes the extraordinary true legend of Ann Lee, founder of the Shakers. Academy Award nominee Amanda Seyfried stars as the devotional sect’s irrepressible leader, who preached gender and social equality and was revered by her followers. The Testament of Ann Lee captures the ecstasy and agony of her quest to build a utopia, featuring more than a dozen traditional Shaker hymns reimagined as rapturous movements with choreography by Celia Rowlson-Hall ( Vox Lux ) and original songs and score by Academy Award winner Daniel Blumberg ( The Brutalist ). Join us for a Q&A with director Mona Fastvold, co-writer Brady Corbet, and actor Tim Blake Nelson following the 6:40pm screening on Friday, January 16.

movies.title: The Three Burials Of Melquiades Estrada
movies.description: After his eponymous best friend (Julio César Cedillo) is killed by a psychotic Border Patrol officer (Barry Pepper), rancher Pete Perkins (Tommy Lee Jones) kidnaps the murderer, forces him to exhume the body, and leads him south of the border so Estrada can receive a hometown burial. In crafting this existential neo-western, Jones and screenwriter Guillermo Arriaga (Amores Perros) were directly inspired by the shooting of Texan teenager Esequiel Hernandez by U.S. Marines in 1997. Jones’ directorial debut is both a taut cowboy thriller and pained, surreal reflection on the American death cult, leavened by startling moments of coal-black humor.

movies.title: The Time That Remains
movies.description: Subtitled “Chronicle of a Present Absentee,” this humorous, heartbreaking film—the final installment in a trilogy that includes Chronicle of a Disappearance and Divine Intervention —is set among the Arab community in Israel and shot largely in homes and places in which director Elia Suleiman’s family once lived. Inspired by his father’s diaries, letters his mother sent to family members who had fled the Israeli occupation, and the director’s own recollections, the film spans from 1948 until the present, recounting the saga of Suleiman’s family in elegantly stylized episodes. Inserting himself as a silent observer reminiscent of Buster Keaton, Suleiman trains a keen eye on the absurdities of life in Nazareth.

movies.title: The Travel Companion
movies.description: Simon is a struggling documentary filmmaker enjoying one perk making his practice a little easier: free flights courtesy of his best friend and roommate Bruce, who works for an airline. But when Bruce starts dating Beatrice, Simon starts to worry his infinite supply of pro bono travel may begin to dry up. To top it off, Beatrice is also a filmmaker, and a successful one. In their feature debut, the director duo serves up some delightfully deadpan humor as they unpack the woes of modern filmmaking, jealousy, and the highs and lows of friendship. Q&A with filmmakers on Friday, April 10 moderated by Jesse Trussell, Director, Film Programming at BAM, and on Saturday, April 11 moderated by Dara Messinger, Director of Programming at DCTV.

movies.title: The Traveler
movies.description: The all-consuming monomania of footy fandom is at the center of Kiarostami’s first full-length feature, in which Qassem, a 12-year-old from the provincial city of Malayer, is determined to see the Iranian national team play a match some 150 miles away…

movies.title: The Voice Of Hind Rajab
movies.description: Calling for help from inside a car under heavy Israeli military fire in Gaza, Hind Rajab, a 5-year-old Palestinian girl, reached countless listeners around the world after recordings of her desperate pleas were released online. This new film, made by Academy Award nominee Kaouther Ben Hania ( Four Daughters ) in collaboration with Hind’s family and the Palestine Red Crescent Society, combines archival audio with dramatic recreations of the emergency workers at the call center as they try to dispatch rescuers. Winner of the Grand Jury Prize at the 2025 Venice Film Festival, this powerful film compels us to face this tragedy with open eyes. Join us for a Q&A with lead actor Saja Kilani following the 7:30pm screening on Tuesday, January 13.

movies.title: The Warriors
movies.description: “Waaarriors! Come out and play-ay!” Falsely accused of responsibility for the assassination of New York’s most powerful ganglord during a citywide summit in the Bronx’s Van Cortlandt Park, Swan (Michael Beck) and his fellow Warriors now have to…

movies.title: The Warriors
movies.description: Accused of a murder they didn't commit, the members of The Warriors eponymous gang end up with targets on their back. In the Walter Hill-directed flick (with a screenplay by Hill and David Shaber), the Warriors traverse the city in a mission to evade death and prove their innocence. In a particularly memorable moment, the gang pulls into the alleged “96th Street Station” (really Hoyt-Schermerhorn) only to find the cops waiting, forcing them to bolt to the exit. Despite its lukewarm 1979 reception, The Warriors rightfully found its footing as a cult film, beloved for its campy approach to gangland.

movies.title: The Watermelon Woman
movies.description: Cheryl Dunye made cinematic history with The Watermelon Woman , the first American feature to be directed by a Black lesbian as well as an incisive, humorous critique of classic Hollywood's racist stereotypes. Dunye plays a video store employee and burgeoning filmmaker who sets out to make a documentary on the Watermelon Woman (Lisa Marie Bronson), an actress who specialized in "mammy" roles for Hollywood productions of the 30s and 40s. As Cheryl uncovers the Watermelon Woman's identity she not only learns about a secret behind-the-scenes interracial romance but also begins one of her own with Diana (Guinevere Turner), a white woman who arouses the ire of Cheryl's best friend Tamara (Valerie Walker).

movies.title: The Wiz
movies.description: Michael Jackson and Diana Ross star in The Wizard of Oz offshoot that modernized and added soul to a decades-old story. Reimagining Dorothy’s Technicolor adventure with an entirely Black cast, based on its preceding 1974 staged version, the Sidney Lumet-directed romp is a who’s who of the era’s soul music stars. Quincy Jones oversaw the adaptation of the 1974 musical’s songs by Charlie Smalls and Luther Vandross, and while it never quite reached the critical highs of the staged version, it shined an ever-spooky light on the Hoyt-Schermerhorn station—where MJ would go on to shoot his “Bad” music video almost a decade later.

movies.title: The Woman Who Poked The Leopard
movies.description: The Woman Who Poked The Leopard (2025) Dir. Patience Nitumwesiga With Stella Nyanzi, Baraka Bah, Kato Bah, Wasswa Bah 108min; DCP Uganda, South Africa, Germany, US US Premiere An outspoken poet, scholar, and activist, Dr. Stella Nyanzi has become one of the most uncompromising voices of resistance in Uganda. After publicly criticizing President Yoweri Museveni online, she was arrested in 2018 and imprisoned, where severe mistreatment led to the loss of her pregnancy. Undeterred, she returned to the public arena in 2020 to campaign for parliament, challenging Museveni’s continued rule. A radical feminist and advocate for queer rights in a country where homosexuality is criminalized, Nyanzi faces constant harassment from authorities determined to silence dissent. Interweaving footage from the campaign trail with archival scenes of protest and repression, alongside intimate moments with her three teenage children, the story reveals both Uganda’s fraught political landscape and the personal toll borne by those who dare to resist. Screening with a video introduction from director Patience Nitumwesiga Preceded by: A Kalabanda Ate My Homework (2017) Dir. Raymond Malinga 7min; DCP Uganda Tendo, a pupil, shows up to class one day without homework - claiming that a "Kalabanda" ate it. Who'd believe such a lame excuse? No-one. How will Tendo prove his story? Tendo's mischievous friend Kibe devises a method to protect him from Mr. Oketch's wrath. However, Mr. Oketch seeks out the perpetrator in a chilling yet comical outcome.

movies.title: There Once Was a Singing Blackbird
movies.description: Gia (Gela Kandelaki), a timpanist in the Tbilisi Philharmonic, has made a science of getting to work just on time to hit his lone cue and then dashing out the door, so as to leave the rest of his hours open for sweet-talking women and carousing with pals.…

movies.title: Three Crowns Of The Sailor
movies.description: Prolific Chilean director Raúl Ruiz’s 1982 magical realist film is a spellbinding labyrinth of stories within stories, a ghostly maritime fable that drifts between an ocean vessel and the far reaches of memory. When a desperate student encounters a mysterious sailor marked for death, he’s drawn into a nocturnal voyage of uncanny encounters, temporal slips, and philosophical riddles. Laced with Ruiz’s sly wit and oneiric logic, this cult classic is a hypnotic meditation on the porous border between life and afterlife.

movies.title: Ticks
movies.description: An assortment of unruly and misfit teens have all been forced to attend camp at a wildlife preserve, to commune with nature. What they don't realize is that nearby in the woods, an illicit marijuana growing operation is underway and the weed farmers have been using a pesticide which has had one very unintended side effect: turning ordinary ticks into giant, ravenous bloodsuckers...One of the quintessential creature features of the early 90s, Tony Randel's (HELLBOUND: HELLRAISER II, AMITYVILLE II: IT'S ABOUT TIME) TICKS pays loving tribute to 1950s giant monster movies, updating the formula by adding copious amounts of slime and heavily increased bloodshed. Starring Seth Green (AUSTIN POWERS), Alfonso Ribeiro (TV's FRESH PRINCE OF BEL AIR), Rosalind Allen (TV's SEINFELD) and a very memorable appearance from Clint Howard (ICE CREAM MAN), TICKS is newly remastered in 4K. (Vinegar Syndrome)

movies.title: To A Land Unknown
movies.description: Palestinian cousins Chatila and Reda are saving to pay for fake passports to get out of Athens. But when Reda loses their hard-earned cash to his dangerous drug addiction, Chatila hatches an extreme plan, which involves them posing as smugglers and taking hostages in an effort to get out of their hopeless environment before it is too late.

movies.title: To Sleep With Anger
movies.description: A slow-burning masterwork of the early 1990s, this third feature by L.A. Rebellion’s Charles Burnett is a singular piece of American mythmaking. In a towering performance, Danny Glover plays the enigmatic southern drifter Harry, a devilish charmer who turns up out of the blue on the doorstep of old friends in South Central Los Angeles. In short order, Harry’s presence seems to cast a chaotic spell on what appeared to be a peaceful household, exposing smoldering tensions between parents and children, tradition and change, virtue and temptation. Interweaving evocative strains of gospel and blues with rich, poetic-realist images, this modern tale of the Great Migration is a sublimely stirring film from an autonomous artistic sensibility, a portrait of family resilience steeped in the traditions of African American mysticism and folklore.

movies.title: Tokyo Godfathers
movies.description: In this animated feature from Satoshi Kon ( Perfect Blue , Paprika ), three homeless people’s lives are changed forever when they discover a baby girl at a garbage dump on Christmas Eve. As the New Year fast approaches, these three forgotten members of society band together to solve the mystery of the abandoned child and the fate of her parents. Along the way, encounters with seemingly unrelated events and people force them to confront their own haunted pasts, as they learn to face their future together.

movies.title: Tony
movies.cast: Dominic Sessa, Emilia Jones, Leo Woodall, Antonio Banderas, Stavros Halkias
movies.description: A young Anthony Bourdain stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen

movies.title: Tony
movies.cast: Dominic Sessa, Emilia Jones, Leo Woodall, Antonio Banderas, Stavros Halkias
movies.description: When 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain (Sessa) travels to Provincetown, happenstance propels him into a restaurant kitchen, kickstarting one of the most watched (and read about) careers in contemporary cooking. From Canadian indie darling Matt Johnson ( BlackBerry , Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie) comes a portrait of one of food media and literature’s most provocative minds. Pulled from excerpts of Kitchen Confidential , Tony eschews traditional sprawling biographical encomium, instead offering a candid glimpse into an especially formative season of Bourdain’s life.

movies.title: Tony
movies.cast: Dominic Sessa, Emilia Jones, Leo Woodall, Antonio Banderas, Stavros Halkias
movies.description: When a writing fellowship falls through, 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain (Dominic Sessa, THE HOLDOVERS) heads to Cape Cod to chase a college girl instead. What he finds is a dish pit, a hammock to sleep in, and the glorious madness of a Provincetown seafood kitchen. One of our favorite filmmakers, Matt Johnson (NIRVANNA THE BAND THE SHOW THE MOVIE, BLACKBERRY), captures the summer Bourdain accidentally discovered the calling that would change his life forever. Antonio Banderas gives one of the best performances of his career, trading swagger for warmth in a role that's funny, patient, and deeply felt.

movies.title: Toute une nuit
movies.description: Emotions boil over and thunder rolls during one oppressively humid summer night in Brussels in Akerman’s tender and melancholy film of brief encounters, furtive embraces, nocturnal despair, yearning vigils, and pregnant silences. A string of…

movies.title: Traces Of Home
movies.cast: Colette Ghunim, Hosni Ghunim, Iza Ghunim, Ramsey Ghunim
movies.description: In her (DOC NYC Grand Jury Prize) award-winning debut feature film Traces of Home, filmmaker Colette Ghunim embarks on journeys with her parents to find the ancestral houses they were forced to flee as children in Mexico and Palestine. Colette’s initial desire to heal her disconnect from her cultures and her parents reveals an internal quest to discover home within herself.

movies.title: Traces Of Home (Early Access Q&A)

movies.title: Tribute To Ken Jacobs
movies.director: Ken Jacobs Ken Jacobs was a master of recontextualization. The legendary experimental filmmaker, who passed away last year at the age of 92, was always on a quest to redefine existing images, from discarded newscast remnants to some of the very first scenes captured on film. Sometimes he aimed to exalt a sacred text (as in Gift of Fire ); other work revealed the ephemerality of the news and our consumption; in What Happened on 23rd Street in 1901 , he toyed with the audience, a metaphorical scolding of voyeuristic desire. Alongside his wife and artistic collaborator Flo, Jacobs produced work for over half a century, perhaps best-known for his 1969 experimental film Tom, Tom, the Piper's Son , an exploration of the techniques of early film that he would continue to work and rework for decades. . In this tribute, part of The Whole Shebang: Celebrating Ken & Flo Jacobs, a city-wide effort to honor his extraordinary career and legacy this month, BAM is honored to showcase some of the less-seen—but equally kinetic—work produced by Jacobs throughout the latter half of his career. WARNING: This screening contains throbbing light. Should not be viewed by individuals with epilepsy or seizure disorders. Perfect Film
movies.description: Ken Jacobs was a master of recontextualization. The legendary experimental filmmaker, who passed away last year at the age of 92, was always on a quest to redefine existing images, from discarded newscast remnants to some of the very first scenes captured on film. Sometimes he aimed to exalt a sacred text (as in Gift of Fire ); other work revealed the ephemerality of the news and our consumption; in What Happened on 23rd Street in 1901 , he toyed with the audience, a metaphorical scolding of voyeuristic desire. Alongside his wife and artistic collaborator Flo, Jacobs produced work for over half a century, perhaps best-known for his 1969 experimental film Tom, Tom, the Piper's Son , an exploration of the techniques of early film that he would continue to work and rework for decades. . In this tribute, part of The Whole Shebang: Celebrating Ken & Flo Jacobs, a city-wide effort to honor his extraordinary career and legacy this month, BAM is honored to showcase some of the less-seen—but equally kinetic—work produced by Jacobs throughout the latter half of his career. WARNING: This screening contains throbbing light. Should not be viewed by individuals with epilepsy or seizure disorders. Perfect Film (1986) Dir. Ken Jacobs 22min; Digital Serving as a meditation on what gets overlooked in the onslaught of news cycles, the cheekily named short presents a completely unedited discard from a newscast about Malcolm X’s assasination that Jacobs purchased for $5 on Canal Street. Capitalism: Slavery (2006) Dir. Ken Jacobs 3min; Digital WARNING: This work contains throbbing light. Should not be viewed by individuals with epilepsy or seizure disorders. A stunning example of Jacob’s practice of found image manipulation in service of narrative construction, Capitalism: Slavery depicts a Victorian stereograph (a double-photograph) of slaves picking cotton under an overseer, digitally altered to create a haunting illusion of depth and movement. Described by Jacobs as "silent, mournful, brief,” the work reactivates a moment trapped in the stasis of its era’s technology. What Happened on 23rd Street in 1901 (2009) Dir. Ken Jacobs 14min; Digital WARNING: This work contains throbbing light. Should not be viewed by individuals with epilepsy or seizure disorders. The century-old What Happened on Twenty-third Street, New York City was created by Edwin S. Porter, the director for Thomas Edison’s production company, advertised at the time as offering a glimpse of a "young lady's skirts suddenly raised to an almost unreasonable height, greatly to her horror and much to the amusement of the newsboys, bootblacks, and passersby." Subverting the audience’s desire built into the voyeuristic original, Jacobs’ riff on the 1901 movie instead stretches the film from its original 77 seconds to a drawn out 14 minutes, using a strobe effect (a Jacobs’ signature in his later work) to obscure the film’s most recognizable sequence. Gift of Fire: Nineteen (Obscure) Frames That Changed The World (2008) Dir. Ken Jacobs 28min; 3D Digital 3D Glasses will be provided Jacobs returns to what is likely the first recorded film in history, Louis-Aimé-Augustin Le Prince's 1888 footage of traffic crossing Leeds Bridge, for this iteration of recontextualizing existing footage. Despite the original film’s mere nineteen frame runtime and mundane subject matter, Jacobs’ experimentation exalts the work’s monumental position in cinematic history by intercutting contextual text and other watershed film moments, such as the Odessa Steps sequence in Sergei Eisenstein's Battleship Potemkin .

movies.title: Tricks, Spirits, And Flickering Lights
movies.description: This collection of short works, from the turn of the century to the contemporary, reveals how cinema creates deception through a play of light and attention. Is Spiritualism a Fraud? (AKA: The Medium Exposed) (1906) Dir. Walter R. Booth 7 min, digital In this British silent short, a medium is dramatically unmasked during a séance, and the mechanisms of his trick are revealed. The Magician’s Alms (La charité du prestidigitateur) (1905) Dir. Alice Guy-Blaché France 3 min, digital One of hundreds of shorts by cinematic pioneer Alice Guy-Blaché, the first woman to direct a film, this morality tale merges stop-motion and social commentary in an encounter between a magician and beggar. La Métamorphose du Roi de Pique (1903) Dir. Gaston Vell 1 min, digital A classic example of the trick film, a fixture of early cinema that used cinematic magic to enhance close-up magic, Vell pairs emerging technological innovations with traditions of illusory enchantment. 28.IV.81 (Bedouin Spark) (2009) Dir. Christopher Harris 3 min, digital Edited in-camera on a single reel of 16mm film, Christopher Harris’ mesmerizing close-up transforms a child’s night-light into swirling celestial vision through the use of a macro lens. Chronometer (Nervous Magic Lantern) (2006) Dir. Ken Jacobs 24 min, digital The experimental filmmaker Ken Jacobs and his partner and collaborator Flo Jacobs reimagined the origins of cinema with their Nervous Magic Lantern performances. Chronometer is a record of one such performance, during which Jacobs manipulates three-dimensional objects in front of a projected stream of light, producing, in his words, “voluptuous rounded forms in a delirious and drunken space.” Now I’m Turning to Face You (1982) Dir. Rea Tajiri 7 min, digital The filmmaker and visual artist Rea Tajiri combines classic cinematic moments with her own overlaid text, establishing a sly tension between the magicians of cinema, who craft powerful illusions, and the anonymous audience member, who imposes their own interpretations and machinations upon the work. Both are located out of sight, on either side of the screen, illustrating Tjiri’s assertion: “When I’m watching / you won’t see me.” Water to Wine to Water (1972–1973) Dir. John Baldessari 1 min, digital The conceptual artist John Baldessari performs an amateur magician’s rendition of the holy miracle. The Magician’s Cabinet (1974–1975) Dir. Cynthia Maughan 2 min, digital With her signature deadpan, Cynthia Maughan delivers a single-take performance directly to the camera, recounting the morbid history of a magician’s relic.

movies.title: Trouble In Mind
movies.description: Set in a realistic but outside of time environment, Alan Rudolph’s grimy ensemble movie follows ex-cop Hawk (Kristofferson) as he returns from prison to the fictional “Rain City,” inspired by Seattle. Partially responsible for the re-appraisal of Rudolph's work as an auteur in recent years, the neo-noir reflects a Pynchonesque undercurrent of existential romanticism in a time unplaceable as past or future.

movies.title: True Romance
movies.description: Comic shop clerk, Elvis aficionado, and repository of cult movie esoterica, Slater’s Clarence Worley goes from nerd to knight errant after his whirlwind romance with call girl Alabama (Patricia Arquette), taking her on the lam after he forcefully…

movies.title: Trás-Os-Montes
movies.description: A pioneering docudrama and the first feature in António Reis and Mararida Corederio’s trilogy, Trás-os-Montes paints a vivid portrait of the extraordinary titular region of north-east Portugal. Blurring the past, present, and future through a series of palpable vignettes, French filmmaker and anthropologist Jean Rouch said that the work “reveals a new cinematographic language.”

movies.title: Tuner
movies.description: A gifted piano tuner's meticulous skills for maintaining instruments lead him to discover an unexpected aptitude for cracking safes, turning his life upside down, in the debut feature by Canadian documentary filmmaker Daniel Roher ( Navalny ; Once Were Brothers: Robbie Robertson and the Band ). RogerEbert.com commends the “quiet yet compelling performance” by Leo Woodall as Niki White, the titular tuner, in a film that also provides a “lovely late-career showcase” for veteran actor Dustin Hoffman as Niki’s mentor, Harry Horowitz.

movies.title: Turk 182
movies.description: When firefighter Terry Lynch (Hutton) is denied benefits by the city in the wake of an off-duty rescue injury, his brother Jimmy (Urich) takes it upon himself to seek restitution. In an overstuffed 96 minutes, Jimmy’s quest takes him around the city—from the Queensboro Bridge to the Hoyt-Schermerhorn station. Fun fact: this was one of the first flicks to receive a PG-13 rating.

movies.title: Two by Robb Moss
movies.description: Q&A with filmmaker Robb Moss on Saturday, August 15th

movies.title: Two Pianos
movies.description: Once a rising star of the French musical scene and Eléna’s (Charlotte Rampling) prized pupil, pianist Mathias (François Civil) returns to France after many years spent teaching and performing in Japan. Soon after his arrival, a chance encounter with a child who looks just like him throws Mathias into turmoil, and leads him back to his first love, Claude (Nadia Tereszkiewicz). French master Arnaud Desplechin ( My Sex Life… , A Christmas Tale ) returns to some of his favorite themes—psychologically charged homecomings and unexpected reunions (romantic and otherwise)—in this sensual, Hitchcockian melodrama featuring one of Rampling’s most delicious roles in years.

movies.title: Under The Blossoming Cherry Trees
movies.description: 35mm print imported from Japan (courtesy National Film Archive of Japan) “Allured by a mysterious bewitching city woman (Shima Iwashita at the height of her powers), a secluded mountain thief (Tomisaburo Wakayama) starts beheading his seven wives. What follows is a descent into bloodshed, psychological affair, and madness—and more beheadings. Adapted from a short story by Ango Sakaguchi, this fantastical folktale uses the idea that one would go mad walking among cherry trees, and contrasts the relentless violence of the mountain man and the cold beauty of the woman. Shot by DP Tatsuo Suzuki, cherry blossom trees provide a beautiful, yet ominous backdrop heightened by the eerie score of Toru Takemitsu.” - Akinaru Rokkaku

movies.title: Under The Silver Lake
movies.description: A young man’s investigation into the disappearance of his neighbor unravels a sprawling and volatile conspiracy. Maligned on release but now reappraised as a cult classic, David Robert Mitchell’s ( It Follows ) feature is an almost explicit riff on Pynchon. In a modern twist, the naive detective is himself obsessed with conspiracy theories, revealing a character that seemed fringe a decade ago, but is all too common today.

movies.title: Union County
movies.description: This unflinching look at the opioid epidemic follows brothers Cody (Poulter) and Jack Parsons (Centineo) as they navigate a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program, and pursue the promise of a brighter, sober future together. Anchored by poignant, moving performances from its leading duo, Ohio-born filmmaker Adam Meeks’ creates a film imbued with realism for an honest, compassionate portrait of a battle being fought across America and the solidarity that flowers on its front lines.

movies.title: Variety + Life In The Cage
movies.description: Variety (1983) dir. Bette Gordon. With Sandy McLeod, Richard M. Davidson, Luis Guzmán 100min; DCP Both panned and praised by critics for its subject matter, Bette Gordon’s film follows an aspiring author who, desperate for cash, finds work as a ticket taker at a seedy Times Square porn theater. There, she becomes sexually awakened and finds herself irresistibly intrigued by the mysterious life of a wealthy patron. Literary iconoclast Kathy Acker wrote the screenplay for Variety , which LA Weekly likened to “a feminist Vertigo .” Life in the Cage (2025) Dir. David Cardoza 4min; Digital A box-office clerk is forced to deal with a hot-tempered patron in David Cardoza’s comedic short vignette.

movies.title: Vertigo
movies.cast: James Stewart, Kim Novak, Barbara Bel Geddes, Tom Helmore, Henry Jones
movies.description: Dress up becomes a matter of fevered fixation in Hitchcock’s utterly intoxicating thriller, in which ex-cop-cum-snoop-for-hire Scottie Ferguson (Jimmy Stewart) sets out on a routine job tailing the mysterious Madeline (Kim Novak), an old pal’s…

movies.title: Video 50 + Deafman Glance
movies.description: Video 50 (1978) Dir. Robert Wilson With Lucinda Childs, Philippe Chemin, Laura Condominas, Robert Wilson 52min; Digital An extraordinary video sketchbook, Video 50 is a composition of one hundred abbreviated “episodes” produced for television by Wilson, a perhaps prescient exploration of ultra-short form film. This series of 30-second vignettes unfolds in uninterrupted succession, snowballing into an enigmatic film essay that invokes a range of visual styles, from deadpan theatricality to tense surrealism. Rife with singular images—a man teetering above a waterfall, a floating chair, a winking eye, a parrot against the New York skyline—Wilson creates a work of startling wit and poetry. Deafman Glance (1981) Dir. Robert Wilson With Sheryl Sutton, Jerry Jackson. Rafael Carmona 27min; Digital This adaptation of Wilson's five-hour "silent opera" of the same title tells a vividly stylized story of murder, eschewing the spoken word in favor of light and movement as narrative tools. The ritualistic action, which moves from a spartan kitchen through the silent halls, stairways, and rooms of a lonely house, is both dreamlike and sinister. A somber, menacing woman washes white dishes and a gleaming carving knife, pours milk into a glass, and then slowly attacks first one young boy and then another. Not a word of dialogue is uttered. Suggesting the disparate worlds of both ancient Greek tragedy and contemporary tabloid headlines, Deafman Glance harbors paradox: the events are terrifying but not violent; characters are both real and symbols of reality; pacing reduces action to abstraction; and morality and mortality are ambiguous.

movies.title: Viva Viva
movies.description: Filmed between 2003 and 2005, Viva Viva captures São Paulo’s punk scene from favelas to the city center, across generations and social divides. From Toca, a young man building his home by hand, to Elisa, an innovator of the city’s queer punk scene, Carolina follows the daily lives of punks across the city, while tracing the history of a movement that emerged under the violent grip of Brazilian dictatorship. The June 12 screening will be followed by a Q&A with filmmaker Carolina Pfister.

movies.title: Waiting For Guffman
movies.description: 30th Anniversary screening When the town of Blaine, MO, approaches its sesquicentennial, there's only one way to celebrate: with a musical revue called Red, White and Blaine . Hoping the show will be his ticket back to Broadway, impresario Corky St. Clair (Christopher Guest) rounds up a cast of enthusiastic locals—portrayed by Eugene Levy, Parker Posey, Fred Willard, and the late, great Catherine O'Hara—to perform his ostensibly toe-tapping triumph. But when Corky reveals that theater agent Mort Guffman will attend the opening, things really kick into high gear. Screening to commemorate its 30th anniversary, this essential satire from director Guest ( Best in Show , A Mighty Wind ) blends comic absurdism, improvisation, and deadpan genius into a marvel of mockumentary. Screening on 35mm.

movies.title: Wajib
movies.description: Mohammed Bakri plays father to his real-life son Saleh Bakri in an intimate look at the lives of Palestinians living within Israel’s borders by director Annemarie Jacir—whose newest film, the historical drama Palestine 36 , opens at BAM Rose Cinemas on March 27. Abu Shadi, a divorced father in his mid-sixties and a school teacher in Nazareth, will be living alone after his daughter’s wedding in one month. Shadi, his architect son, arrives from Rome after years abroad to help his father in hand-delivering the wedding invitations to each guest, per local Palestinian custom. As the estranged pair spend the day together, the tense details of their relationship come to a head, challenging their fragile and very different lives.

movies.title: Walkabout
movies.description: Having fled into the Outback after their father has a psychotic episode that threatens their very lives, two Sydney-bred adolescent siblings (Jenny Agutter and Luc Roeg, the director’s son) meet an Aboriginal teenager (David Gulpilil, in his debut role)…

movies.title: WATCH ME
movies.description: Director:Ivan Malekin Runtime:94min Language:English Cast:Anastasia Kor, Nicolas Hackenberg, Andrea Véguez,  Antoine Topin, Ivona Tomiek Isla is an international student barely holding her life together. Overworked, directionless, and drowning financially, she reluctantly enters the world of webcam modelling after encouragement from her reckless, extroverted best friend Fay. What begins as survival soon becomes transformation. Trailer:https://youtu.be/Ih-G1XukOeE Tickets:https://www.eventbrite.de/e/watch-me-us-premiere-screening-filmmaker-qa-tickets-1989552119948

movies.title: Welcome Ii The Terrordome
movies.description: New restoration! Ngozi Onwurah’s radically ahead-of-its-time Afrofuturist vision Welcome II the Terrordome made history as the first theatrically distributed British feature directed by a Black woman. Nevertheless, it was largely dismissed upon its release by critics unable to see the urgency in its evocation of a gritty dystopia in which Black people have been relegated to a slum called the Terrordome, where simmering racial tension threatens to boil over in the wake of a young boy’s death. But over 30 years later, Onwurah’s fusion of political commentary and genre spectacle looks positively prescient, and her ability to build an entire cosmology that connects the history of slavery to present-day police brutality is nothing less than visionary. Q&As with Ngozi Onwurah following the 7pm screenings on Friday, July 31 and Saturday, August 1.

movies.title: Wet Hot American Summer: 25th Anniversary
movies.description:
Remember those kids who were too cool for school? Those kids are now your camp counselors.
David Wain and company (including members of MTV's The State, the Upright Citizens Brigade, SNL, and a pre-famed Bradley Cooper) make idiosyncratic, over-the-top. strangely touching comedy. These character creations are unlike anything you've ever seen AND people you can relate to. There's young love, steamy sessions in the shed, talking cans, and everybody's favorite activity...going to town!
So relive this unbelievably watchable, funny, original movie. It doesn't give one single f*ck...and that's the best part.

movies.title: What Lies Beneath
movies.description: Filmed during a lengthy production break on his Cast Away of the same year, Zemeckis’s What Lies Beneath is in many regards a fitting companion piece to the director’s better-known Hanks vehicle as a study in isolation—here, the gnawing loneliness…

movies.title: When Marnie Was There
movies.description: Yonebayashi’s Studio Ghibli–produced adaptation of British author Joan G. Robinson’s 1967 novel of the same name transplant the source’s action from the marshes of Norfolk to the Kushiro wetlands in Hokkaido, where young Anna, staying with…

movies.title: When The Levees Broke: A Requiem In Four Acts
movies.description: Released a year after Hurricane Katrina, When the Levees Broke comprises a series of interviews and news footage excerpts recounting the devastation of New Orleans and the critical mishandling of its aftermath. In his third documentary, Lee gives voice to survivors in a mournful and powerful work of meticulous documentation, redirecting the legendary director’s keen filmic eye towards a true modern tragedy, and the beacons of hope that lay in its wake.

movies.title: Where Is The Friend'S House?
movies.description: A schoolboy’s search for the home of his classmate evolves into a desperate adventure in this Kiarostami film inviting viewers to see the world through the wide eyes of a child. A quintessential film from the Iranian master, the inaugural edition of the Koker Trilogy finds beauty in the mundane as Ahmad’s quest takes him around multiple towns, encountering a myriad of people—both helpful and not. This invocation of the way children view the world serves as a portrait of rural Iranian society in the ‘80s, while celebrating the wonder imbued in every moment.

movies.title: Where is the Friend's House?
movies.description:
Presented in Persian with English subtitles
The first film in Abbas Kiarostami’s sublime, interlacing trilogy of films set in the northern Iranian village of Koker takes a premise of fable-like simplicity – a boy searches for the home of his classmate whose school notebook he has accidentally taken – and transforms it into a miraculous, child’s-eye adventure of the everyday. As our young hero zigzags determinedly across two towns, aided (and sometimes misdirected) by those he encounters, his quest becomes both a revealing portrait of Iranian society in all its richness and complexity and a touching parable about the meaning of personal responsibility. Shot through with all the wonder, beauty, tension, and mystery one day can contain, WHERE IS THE FRIEND'S HOUSE? established Kiarostami’s reputation as one of cinema’s most sensitive and profound humanists. (Janus)

movies.title: Whisper Of The Heart
movies.description: New 4K Restoration A chance encounter with a mysterious cat sends Shizuku, a girl with her head in the clouds, on a quest for her true talent. Together with a new friend Seij, and enchanted by The Baron, an antique cat figurine who guides her to listen to the whispers of her heart, Shizuku embarks on a life-changing adventure that takes her beyond the boundaries of her imagination. This precious gem from the Studio Ghibli catalog—based on a screenplay and storyboards from Hayao Miyazaki—was directed by veteran animator Yoshifumi Kondō, who the studio hoped would become Miyazaki’s successor before his untimely passing in 1998.

movies.title: White Material
movies.description: Raised in colonial French Africa until the age of 13, Denis would return to the continent in her cinema time and again, making it the scene of some of her richest and most redolent works. Here, Isabelle Huppert plays the manager of a coffee plantation in…

movies.title: Who Framed Roger Rabbit
movies.description: In one of the most critically-acclaimed comedies of all time, a grizzly private detective embarks on a mission to prove the innocence of a poorly-performing cartoon star. Pynchon—an avowed animation fan, making references to Looney Tunes , Popeye and more—surely must have loved Zemeckis’s masterpiece, which mashed up Chinatown , ‘40s noir, and Bugs into a singular classic.

movies.title: Wild Inside
movies.cast: Flaco the Owl
movies.description: A Eurasian Eagle-Owl named Flaco escapes from the Central Park Zoo and sets off on a magical odyssey through the island of Manhattan. Flaco overcomes his years of captivity and lack of survival skills to answer the call of the wild – and discovers he was wild inside all along. The 6:00PM screenings on August 18th and 19th will be followed by a Q&A with director Penny Lane , moderated by birder and filmmaker Harri Bailey . The Q&A on August 19th will also be joined by a wildlife photographer featured in the film. Courtesy of Sandbox Films and HBO.

movies.title: Wind Across The Everglades
movies.description: In the early 20th century, game warden and nature conservationist Walt Murdock (Christopher Plummer) is pitted against Cottonmouth (Burl Ives), the leader of a gang of flippant birdpoachers. With a prescient ecological message coursing through the film’s central narrative, this technicolor wonder displays the masterful use of color and nuanced approach to good versus evil paramount to so much of Ray’s ouvre—despite his untimely firing before the conclusion of production. In its rendering of a slow deterioration of traditional American ways of living, the film nods to the liberalizing forces of modernity and simultaneously attempts to scrub away the more sinister reminders of our shared history.

movies.title: Wiseman's NYC: Model
movies.description: Introduction by Genevieve Yue, film scholar, programmer, and lead facilitator of Wiseman's New York, on Saturday, September 5th

movies.title: Withnail and I
movies.description: Based loosely on writer/director Robinson’s memories of being a penniless actor in late ’60s London, Withnail and I stars Richard E. Grant and Paul McGann as two unemployed thesps and Camden Town flatmates—hard-drinking, dissolute Withnail and an…

movies.title: Woman In The Moon
movies.description: The successor to his revolutionary Metropolis , Fritz Lang’s next foray revisited science fiction with a spectacular portrayal of the first lunar expedition. Four decades before man actually walked on the moon, this meticulously-researched ode to space exploration was the first time a wide audience was introduced to the concept of interplanetary travel, and the first cinematic occurrence of a rocket countdown to zero. The masterpiece, written by Lang’s wife Thea von Harbou, plays in a Pynchonian milieu of interwar Europe and corporate spies. It was also banned by the Nazis for similarities to the in-development V2 rocket, also central to Gravity’s Rainbow .

movies.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
movies.description: Capping an incredible eight-year creative partnership with Almodóvar, repeat collaborator Carmen Maura here plays voice actress Pepa, who, abandoned by her lover, has resolved to kill herself by downing a batch of gazpacho laced with sleeping pills.…

movies.title: Women’S Stories, Family Memories
movies.description: Pairing documentaries by Afro-Cuban women filmmakers Sara Gómez and Gloria Rolando, this program looks at storytelling as a form of memory, history, and political analysis. Recording interviews and testimonials in the 60s, 70s and early 2000s, both filmmakers reflect on family, class struggle, and culture while centralizing the intergenerational stories and experiences of multidimensional Black girls and women. Followed by a conversation with series programmer Yasmina Price and curator, researcher, and activist Tarisse Iriarte Dialogo con mi abuela (Dialogue with My Grandmother) (2014) Dir. Gloria Rolando. 58 min, digital A beautifully constructed love letter transforming a 1993 interview conducted by the Cuban filmmaker with her grandmother into a celebration of not only her grandmother’s legacy but also a tribute to the larger history, struggle, and tenacity of Afro-Cubans and Afro-Cuban women in particular. Guanabacoa: Crónica de mi familia (1966) Dir. Sara Gómez. 15 min, DCP The prolific Cuban director Sara Gómez offers an honest portrait of her working class and middle class family in their hometown of Guanabacoa, weaving together the voices of her relatives, musical recordings, and photographs. Mi aporte (My Contribution) (1972) Dir. Sara Gómez 33 min, DCP Commissioned by the Federation of Cuban Women, Gómez examined women’s entry into the workforce in postrevolutionary Cuba. Through testimonials and portraits, she turns a self-reflexive, critical, and direct lens on the ongoing process of revolution, during which aspirational ideals met real limitations.

movies.title: Your Letter
movies.description:
Presented in Korean with English subtitles
Crunchyroll Anime Nights is proud to bring you a brand new animated film from South Korea. 
After summer vacation, So-ri transfers to a new school and finds an anonymous letter in her desk drawer with an introduction to the school and a clue to finding the next letter: “If you want to keep reading, find my second letter!”
While following the clues in the letters and searching all over the school like on a treasure hunt, So-ri keeps running into a same-aged student named Dong-soon. So-ri and Dong-soon quickly become friends as they search for the letters together. As she finds one letter after another, the special connection continues, and So-ri’s curiosity grows for the mysterious sender.
“I want to find the last letter and thank you in person.”

movies.title: “Wuthering Heights”
movies.description: Academy Award-winning writer and director Emerald Fennell ( Saltburn ) takes on Emily Brontë’s quintessential gothic novel. A ferocious love story set on the moors, “Wuthering Heights” follows Heathcliff (Elordi) and Catherine (Robbie) as desire gives way to obsession—and vengeance ripples across generations. After decades of adaptations by filmmakers from William Wyler to Luis Buñuel, Emerald Fennell’s glossy reimagining rejects strict fidelity in favor of an unconventional reinvention for a new generation.
